sanskrit_text: आस्यसुखस्वप्नसुखं दधि ग्राम्यौदकानूपान् । नवान्नपानं गुडविकृतिं च कफाभिवृद्धिकरं च सर्वम् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Āsyasukhasvapnasukhaṃ dadhi grāmyaudakānūpān | Navānnapānaṃ guḍavikṛtiṃ ca kaphābhivṛddhikaraṃ ca sarvam || 1 ||
commentary: The Guru Vijayarakṣita who has bright fame has built the honeycomb like commentary upto the disease Aśmarī. The disciple Śrīkaṇṭhadatta has taken up the task of completing the work from meha rogas, supported by reverence to his guru. After expounding on urinary calculus, the prameha, (turbid and excessive urination) is being detailed since there is similarity in terms of the locus standi of the diseases i.e the bladder. Pleasure derived out of doing nothing while sitting is Āsyasukham. Pleasure of sleep is also to be understood in the same manner. This means that sitting with difficulty or sleeping with difficulty are not considered as aetiological factors of prameha. Without specification, all that increases kapha has been given as common reason for this disease. The specific reason is given in Caraka nidāna - hayanaka, uddalaka etc. for kapha type of prameha; where sour and salty foods for pitta type and kaṭu, tikta and kaṣāya tasted foods for vātaja prameha. (Ca. Ni. 4). Thus it is implied that the common and specific aetiological factors cause prameha of kaphaja type etc., or else, it can be understood that the Āsya sukham etc. should be taken as factors causing kaphaja prameha.

sanskrit_text: मेदोमांसशरीरजक्लेदान् मूत्राशयस्थः कफः प्रदुष्टः । स्तनयेदति मेहान् कफजान् द्वयोस्तु पित्तेन ॥ २ ॥ क्षीणेषु दोषेषु पुनर्वातो नयति धातून् मूत्राशयम् । ते चापि मेहान् कुर्वन्ति वातिकान् चतुरः ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Medomāṃsaśarīrajakledān mūtrāśayasthaḥ kaphaḥ praduṣṭaḥ | Stanayedati mehān kaphajān dvayostu pittena || 2 || Kṣīṇeṣu doṣeṣu punarvāto nayati dhātūn mūtrāśayam | Te cāpi mehān kurvanti vātikān caturaḥ || 3 ||
commentary: Medas (fat), māṃsa (muscle tissue) and the wetness of the body are vitiated by the kapha situated in the urinary bladder and cause urinary flux. (This is in the case of kaphaja prameha). The same factors when vitiated by aggravated pitta due to foods and drugs of hot nature, pittaja prameha is resulted. In depleted state of doṣa and etc., vāta again brings down the tissues to the bladder and causes vātaja prameha. But of these, ten caused by kapha are curable due to sāmakriyatā (i.e the treatment to the aggravated kapha and vitiated factors is common) while the six caused by pitta are only manageable because of viṣamakriyatā (i.e the treatment of aggravated pitta further vitiates the vitiated factor and hence it is not congenial to body) and the four caused by vāta are incurable due to the acuteness in the manifestation.

sanskrit_text: कफः सपित्तः पवनश्च दोषाः, मेदोऽस्रशुक्राम्बुवसालसीकाः। मज्जारसौजः पिशितं च दूष्याः, प्रमेहिणां विशतिरेव मेहाः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Kaphaḥ sapittaḥ pavanaśca doṣāḥ, medo'sraśukrāmbuvasālasīkāḥ | Majjārasaujaḥ piśitaṃ ca dūṣyāḥ, pramehiṇāṃ viśatireva mehāḥ || 4 ||
commentary: The doṣas involved in this disease are kapha along with pitta and vāta and the dūṣyas- medas (fat), Asra (blood), Śukra (semen), ambu (watery part of the body), Vasā (oily content of the muscle tissue), Lasīkā (The liquid underneath the skin), majjā (bone-marrow), rasa (chyle), ojās (immunity factor) and piśita (muscle tissue). And the varieties of prameha are twenty.

sanskrit_text: दोषदूष्यविशेषात्तु भवन्ति बहवो मलाः । ते चोपजायन्ते मूत्रे तेषां भेदाद्विशेषतः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration: Doṣadūṣyaviśeṣāttu bhavanti bahavo malāḥ | Te copajāyante mūtre teṣāṃ bhedādviśeṣataḥ || 5 ||
commentary: The varieties of pramehas are numerous depending upon the different doṣas and dūṣyas involved. The cause of this innumerability is the combination and permutation of these factors leading to varied manifestations in the urine.

sanskrit_text: उदकमेही स्रुतं मूत्रं स्पष्टं बहु सितं शिशिरं गन्धवर्जितम् । ईषत्तु विमलं च पिच्छिलमिति लक्षणम् । इक्षुमेही मधुरमतिशयेन मेहति । सान्द्रमेही स्थिरीभवति स्थापितं रात्रौ । सुरामेही सुरासवसमं मूत्रं मुञ्चति । पिष्टमेही पिष्टोदकनिभं सितं रोमहर्षणम् । शुक्रमेही शुक्रनिभं शुक्रमिश्रं वा मेहति । सिकतामेही सिकतोपमैर्मलैर्मूत्रम् । शीतमेही मधुरं बहु शीतस्पर्शम् । सानैर्मेही मन्दं मन्दं मेहति । लालामेही पिच्छिलं लालातन्तुनिभम् ॥ ७-१२ ॥
transliteration: Udakamehī sṛtaṃ mūtraṃ spaṣṭaṃ bahu sitaṃ śiśiraṃ gandhavarjitam | Īṣattu vimalaṃ ca picchilamiti lakṣaṇam | Ikṣumehī madhuramatiśayena mehati | Sāndramehī sthirībhavati sthāpitaṃ rātrau | Surāmehī surāsavasamaṃ mūtraṃ muñcati | Piṣṭamehī piṣṭodakanibhaṃ sitaṃ romaharṣaṇam | Śukramehī śukranibhaṃ śukramiśraṃ vā mehati | Sikatāmehī sikatopamairmalairmūtram | Śītamehī madhuraṃ bahu śītasparśam | Sānairmehī mandaṃ mandaṃ mehati | Lālāmehī picchilaṃ lālātantunibham || 7-12 ||
commentary: The individual passes urine that is clear, excessive, whitish, cold, odourless, looks like water with slight turbidity and sticky when he is known to be suffering from udakameha. In ikṣumeha, the patient passes urine that is very sweet like the juice of sugarcane. The person is labelled as having sāndrameha if his urine gets solidified on keeping aside overnight. The urine has some solid precipitations at the bottom and the upper part is clear like alcohol on preserving which is seen in surāmeha. The piṣṭameha patient passes urine that looks like flour-washed water, white in colour and he has horripilation. The urine of the patient of śukrameha looks like semen or mixed with semen. There will be visible particles which are impurities that look like sand in the urine if one is suffering from Sikatāmeha. The individual suffering from Śītameha passes urine that is sweet in taste, excessive in quality and very cold in touch. In sānairmeha the individual passes urine very slowly. The urine in lālāmeha is sticky and hence thready in nature like saliva.

sanskrit_text: गन्धवर्णरसस्पर्शैः क्षारेण क्षारतोयवत् । नीलमेहेन नीलाभं कालमेही मसीनिभम् ॥ १३ ॥ हारिद्रमेही कटुकं हरिद्रासंनिभं दहेत् । विस्रं माञ्जिष्ठमेहेन मञ्जिष्ठासलिलोपमम् ॥ १४ ॥ विस्रमुष्णं सलवणं रक्ताभं रक्तमेहतः ॥
transliteration: Gandhavarṇarasasparśaiḥ kṣāreṇa kṣāratoyavat | Nīlamehena nīlābhaṃ kālamehī masīnibham || 13 || Hāridramehī kaṭukaṃ haridrāsaṃnibhaṃ dahet | Visraṃ māñjiṣṭhamehena mañjiṣṭhāsalilopamam || 14 || Visramuṣṇaṃ salavaṇaṃ raktābhaṃ raktamehataḥ ||
commentary: The urine in kṣārameha has the smell, colour, taste and touch of water mixed with Kṣāra (alkali). The urine will be bluish in colour in Nīlameha. In Kālameha, urine looks as if mixed with charcoal powder. The Hāridrameha patient passes urine with burning sensation in turmeric colour and it has pungent taste. In māñjīṣṭameha the individual has fast smell in the urine that looks like the mañjīṣṭā (Rubia majishta)- Soaked water. In the case of Raktameha the urine has salty taste and looks like blood.

sanskrit_text: वसामेही वसामिश्रं वसानिभं वा पुनः पुनः । मज्जामेही मज्जमिश्रं मज्जानिभमथापि वा ॥ १५ ॥ कषायमधुरं रूक्षं क्षौद्रमेही तु मेहति । हस्तिमेही तु मेहत्यनियतं लसीकया सह मूढवर्चाः ॥ १६-१७ ॥
transliteration: Vasāmehī vasāmiśraṃ vasānibhaṃ vā punaḥ punaḥ | Majjāmehī majjamiśraṃ majjānibhamathāpi vā || 15 || Kaṣāyamadhuraṃ rūkṣaṃ kṣaudramehī tu mehati | Hastimehī tu mehatyaniyataṃ lasīkayā saha mūḍhavarcāḥ || 16-17 ||
commentary: The individual afflicted by Vasāmeha repeatedly passes urine mixed with vasā that also looks like vasā. The majjāmehī (one suffering from majjāmeha) has micturition where urine is either mixed with majjā (bone-marrow) or that looks like majjā. If one passes urine which has kaṣāya (astringent) and madhura (sweet) tastes and dry in nature, he should be known to be suffering from kṣaudrameha. The suffering individual from hastimeha urinates like a rogue elephant repeatedly without any particular timing or bouts and along with lasīkā (the liquid that appears on peeling of skin) and is also constipated.

sanskrit_text: अविपाकोऽरुचिश्छर्दिर्निद्रातिस्यन्दकासिता । कफजेषु प्रमेहेषु ज्ञेयो वातकफो भवेत् ॥ १८ ॥ पित्तजेषु भवेत्तोदो मुष्कावदरणं ज्वरः । तृष्णाम्लिका मूर्च्छा चातीसारश्चोपद्रवाः ॥ १९ ॥ वातजेष्वानाहः कम्पो हृदयग्रहः । आहारलोलता शूलभ्रमक्लमकासश्वासाः ॥ २० ॥
transliteration: Avipāko'ruciśchardirnidrātisyandakāsitā | Kaphajeṣu prameheṣu jñeyo vātakapho bhavet || 18 || Pittajeṣu bhavettodo muṣkāvadaraṇaṃ jvaraḥ | Tṛṣṇāmlikā mūrcchā ca cātīsāraścopadravāḥ || 19 || Vātajeṣvānāhaḥ kampo hṛdayagrahaḥ | Āhāralolatā śūlabhramaklamakāsaśvāsāḥ || 20 ||
commentary: Indigestion, distaste, nausea and vomiting, excessive sleep, and cough with nasal congestion are complications that appear in Kaphaja prameha. Pinning sensation in the bladder and urethra, breaking of the skin of the testes, fever, thirst, sour belchings, syncope and diarrhoea are seen as complications in pittaja prameha. The complications in vātaja prameha are blocking of the abdomen, trembling, gripping in the heart, desire to eat more food, pain, dizziness, emaciation, cough and dyspnoea.

sanskrit_text: यथोक्तोपद्रवाविष्टमतिप्रस्तुतमेव च । पिडकापीडितं गाढं प्रमेहो हन्ति मानवम् ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration: Yathoktopadravāviṣṭamatiprastutameva ca | Piḍakāpīḍitaṃ gāḍhaṃ prameho hanti mānavam || 21 ||
commentary: The prameha that manifests along with all the complications, with excessive urination, having carbuncles and deep rooted, kills that individual.

sanskrit_text: जातः प्रमेही मधुमेहिनो वा न साध्य उक्तः स हि बीजदोषात् । ये चापि कुलजाः केचित् कुष्ठादयो विकाराः ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration: Jātaḥ pramehī madhumehino vā na sādhya uktaḥ sa hi bījadoṣāt | Ye cāpi kulajāḥ kecit kuṣṭhādayo vikārāḥ || 22 ||
commentary: Another stage of incurability in prameha is being explained here. Due to excessive vitiation of Śleṣma and Medas, there will be sweetening of urine, fat and Śleṣma in a madhumeha patient - such individuals also can not be cured. 'Bījadoṣāt' means the prameha caused by the defective gene that is set to cause prameha. Madhumeha, here refers to only meha. It is to be understood as madhumeha of vāta type or that caused by not treating the pramehas in time, then the congenital prameha patients must not have been categorised as incurable; whereas madhumeha caused by taking birth to a madhumeha individual with gene affliction, has got a similarity in cause and effect and therefore madhumeha patient or the madhumeha patient born to an individual suffering from madhumeha - is incurable such statement sounds apt. Infact this incurability need not also be told because madhumeha itself is incurable.

sanskrit_text: सर्व एव प्रमेहास्तु मधुमेहत्वमागताः । उपेक्षया विशेषेण मधुमेहः प्रजायते ॥ २३ ॥ यदा तु दोषो दुष्यं वा स मधुसमं मेहति । तं मधुमेहमित्याहुरसाध्यं च विशेषतः ॥ २४-२५ ॥
transliteration: Sarva eva pramehāstu madhumehatvamāgatāḥ | Upekṣayā viśeṣeṇa madhumehaḥ prajāyate || 23 || Yadā tu doṣo duṣyaṃ vā sa madhusamaṃ mehati | Taṃ madhumehamityāhurāsādhyaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ || 24-25 ||
commentary: To make it clear that leaving without treating the pitta and kapha prameha(s) make them also madhumeha - this stanza, 'sarva eva pramehastu....' is mentioned here. Madhumeha occurs due to aggravated vāta either by emaciation of tissues or by obstruction or covering caused by other doṣa or dhātus. The adjective madhu-sama (equal to or like honey) is applicable to the urine. It manifests the Vāta symptoms and also those of the covering doṣa - pitta or kapha; without any reason - means suddenly. At one moment the manifestation of vāta is weakness and at another moment is full which makes the situation incurable.

sanskrit_text: प्रायः सर्वेषु मेहेषु मधुरं मधुसन्निभम् । मेहति स्यान्मधुमेहस्तेन सर्वप्रमेहिणाम् ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration: Prāyaḥ sarveṣu meheṣu madhuraṃ madhusannibham | Mehati syānmadhumehastena sarvapramehiṇām || 26 ||
commentary: Generally in all pramehas the individual passes urine that is sweet in taste and looks like honey and his body also gets sweetened, hence the name madhumeha is given to all these pramehas.

sanskrit_text: शराविका कच्छपिका जालिनी विनताऽलजी । मसूरिका सर्षपिका पुत्रिणी सविदारिका ॥ २७ ॥ विद्रधिश्चेति पिडकाः प्रमेहोपेक्षया दश । सन्धिमर्मसु जायन्ते मांसलेषु च धामसु ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration: Śarāvikā kacchapikā jālinī vinatā'lajī | Masūrikā sarṣapikā putriṇī savidārikā || 27 || Vidradhiśceti piḍakāḥ pramehopekṣayā daśa | Sandhimarmasu jāyante māṃsaleṣu ca dhāmasu || 28 ||
commentary: The carbuncles (also referred to as diabetic carbuncles) are ten in number, viz., śarāvikā, kacchapikā, jālinī, vinatā, alajī, masūrikā, sarṣapikā, putriṇī, vidārikā and vidradhi. These occur due to neglecting the pramehas without treating. The carbuncles originate in the joints, vital parts and places where more musculature is there.

sanskrit_text: अन्तरुन्नता तु तद्रूपा निम्नमध्या शराविका । गौरसर्षपसंस्थाना तन्मात्रा च सर्षपी ॥ २९ ॥ सदाहा कूर्मसंस्थाना ज्ञेया कच्छपिका बुधैः । जालिनी तीव्रदाहा तु मांसजालसमावृता ॥ ३० ॥ अवगाढरुजाक्लेदा पृष्ठे वाऽप्युदरेऽपि वा । महती पिडका नीला विनतानाम सा स्मृता ॥ ३१ ॥ महत्यल्पपिडका च ज्ञेया पिडका च पुत्रिणी । मसूराकृतिसंस्थाना विज्ञेया तु मसूरिका ॥ ३२ ॥ रक्तासितस्फोटचिता दारुणा त्वलजी भवेत् । विदारीकन्दवद्वृत्ता कठिना च विदारिका ॥ ३३ ॥ विद्रधेर्लक्षणैर्युक्ता ज्ञेया विद्रधिका तु सा ॥
transliteration: Antarunnatā tu tadrūpā nimnamadhyā śarāvikā | Gaurasarṣapasaṃsthānā tanmātrā ca sarṣapī || 29 || Sadāhā kūrmasaṃsthānā jñeyā kacchapikā budhaiḥ | Jālinī tīvradāhā tu māṃsajālasamāvṛtā || 30 || Avagāḍharujākledā pṛṣṭhe vā'pyudare'pi vā | Mahatī piḍakā nīlā vinatānāma sā smṛtā || 31 || Mahatyalpapiḍakā ca jñeyā piḍakā ca putriṇī | Masūrākṛtisaṃsthānā vijñeyā tu masūrikā || 32 || Raktāsitasphoṭacitā dāruṇā tvalajī bhavet | Vidārīkandavadvṛttā kaṭhinā ca vidārikā || 33 || Vidradherlakṣaṇairyuktā jñeyā vidradhikā tu sā ||
commentary: The carbuncles in which the boundaries are risen, the centre is sunken and it looks like a Śarāva (cassarole), is called śarāvikā. Sarṣapi carbuncles look like white mustard seeds in shape and size. The kacchapī is associated with burning sensation and looks like the tortoise. Jālinī has muscular growth and associated with severe burning sensation. Vinatā is deep-rooted, painful and with some exudation. This is big in size, blue in colour and occurs on the pṛṣṭha (back) or on the udara (abdomen). The small one raising in the surroundings of bigger carbuncle is called putriṇī. The one which is in the shape and size of masūra (lentil) is called masūrikā. The one which is round like a vidārīkanda (puraria tuberosa) and hard to touch is Vidārīkā. The vidradhi type of carbuncles have the qualities like that of vidradhi (abcess).

sanskrit_text: ये यन्मयाः स्मृता मेहास्तेषामेतास्तु तन्मयाः ॥ ३४ ॥ विना प्रमेहमप्येता जायन्ते दुष्टमेदसः । तावच्चैता न लक्ष्यन्ते यावद्वास्तुपरिग्रहः ॥ ३५ ॥
transliteration: Ye yanmayāḥ smṛtā mehāsteṣāmetāstu tanmayāḥ || 34 || Vinā pramehamapyetā jāyante duṣṭamedasaḥ | Tāvaccaitā na lakṣyante yāvadvāstuparigrahaḥ || 35 ||
commentary: Whichever doṣa-dūṣya are involved in causing the prameha, the same factors are also involved in causing carbuncles in that prameha. These carbuncles can also occur even without prameha; that is due to vitiated medas. But they will not be clear till they are deep rooted.

sanskrit_text: स्वप्नशयनास्यसुखं मधुराम्लगुरु च ग्राम्यानूपौदकम् । स्निग्धान्नपानं नवमद्यमांसक्षीरविकृतिं च सेवमानः स्थूलो भवति ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Svapnaśayanāsyasukhaṃ madhurāmlaguru ca grāmyānūpaudakam | Snigdhānnapānaṃ navamadyamāṃsakṣīravikṛtiṃ ca sevamānaḥ sthūlo bhavati || 1 ||
commentary: The individual who sleeps a lot, enjoys sitting, consumes sweet, sour and heavy foods, eats meat of domestic, marshy and aquatic animals, takes unctuous foods and drinks, new grains, wine, meat and milk products, becomes obese.

sanskrit_text: मधुररसो रसो गुरुः स्निग्धः शीतश्च मेदो वर्धयति । तस्मादतिस्थूलस्य रसोऽतिमधुरो मन्दाग्निसम्भवः । स मेदो वर्धयति । तेनास्य मेदोदुष्ट्या स्थूलता भवति ॥ २-४ ॥
transliteration: Madhuraraso raso guruḥ snigdhaḥ śītaśca medo vardhayati | Tasmādatisthūlasya raso'timadhuro mandāgnisambhavaḥ | Sa medo vardhayati | Tenāsya medoduṣṭyā sthūlatā bhavati || 2-4 ||
commentary: The chyle that is sweet, heavy, unctuous and cold increases medas. In the excessively obese, the chyle becomes very sweet due to weak digestive fire. This further increases medas. Thus, due to vitiation of medas, obesity results.

sanskrit_text: स्थूलस्य लक्षणम् - स्थूलोदरः स्थूलपयोधरः स्थूलग्रीवः स्थूलस्कन्धः स्थूलमांसः । चलस्फिगुदरचलोरःस्थलः । अव्यायामार्हो भवति ॥ ५-९ ॥
transliteration: Sthūlasya lakṣaṇam - sthūlodaraḥ sthūlapayodharaḥ sthūlagrīvaḥ sthūlaskandhaḥ sthūlamāṃsaḥ | Calasphigudaracaloraḥsthalaḥ | Avyāyāmārho bhavati || 5-9 ||
commentary: The individual is called obese when his abdomen, chest, buttocks, neck, shoulders and muscles are large and bulky. His buttocks, abdomen and chest shake while walking. He is unable to perform physical exercise and has excessive sleep.

sanskrit_text: सर्व एव गदा मन्दाग्निकृताः, विशेषत उदराणि । अजीर्णदुष्टान्नसंग्रहमलप्रवृत्तिभ्यः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Sarva eva gadā mandāgnikṛtāḥ, viśeṣata udarāṇi | Ajīrṇaduṣṭānnasaṅgrahamalapravṛttibhyaḥ || 1 ||
commentary: All the diseases are caused by weak digestive fire and especially those of the abdominal origin have this (mandāgni- weak digestive fire) as chief pathogenic/ aetiological factor. They (the abdominal disorders) occur due to ajīrṇa (indigestion), ingestion of foods which are contaminated and also accumulation of impurities in the body.

sanskrit_text: दोषाः स्वेदाम्बुवहानि स्रोतांसि संरुध्य, प्राणाग्न्यपानान् प्रदूष्य, कुर्वन्त्युदराणि ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Doṣāḥ svedāmbuvahāni srotāṃsi saṃrudhya, prāṇāgnyapānān pradūṣya, kurvantyudarāṇi || 2 ||
commentary: The doṣas, having obstructed the channels that carry sweat and water, get accumulated and vitiate the prāṇavāyu, agni (the digestive fire) and apānavāyu and cause disorders of the abdomen.

sanskrit_text: आनाहोऽध्वगतिहानिर्दौर्बल्यं मन्दाग्निता च । शोफश्चाङ्गानां शिथिलीभावश्च । विण्मूत्रानिलसङ्गः सदाहश्च भ्रमश्च । सर्वेषूदरेषु भवन्ति ॥ ३ ॥ अष्टावेतानि वातपित्तकफसन्निपातप्लीहबद्धगुदक्षतोदकेषु । तेषां लक्षणं पृथक् वक्ष्यामः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Ānāho'dhvagatihānirdaurbalyaṃ mandāgnitā ca | Śophaścāṅgānāṃ śithilībhāvaśca | Viṇmūtrānilasaṅgaḥ sadāhaśca bhramaśca | Sarveṣūdareṣu bhavanti || 3 || Aṣṭāvetāni vātapittakaphasannipātaplīhabaddhagudakṣatodakeṣu | Teṣāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pṛthak vakṣyāmaḥ || 4 ||
commentary: Flatulance, inability in walking, weakness, weakness of the digestive fire, swelling and depression (looseness) in the limbs, constipation of faeces and fart, burning sensation and dizziness are seen in all the abdominal diseases. It is of eight types i.e. due to vāta, pitta, kapha, individually; all three of these doṣas, plīha (Spleen), baddha (obstruction) in the intestines, kṣata (injury) and also due to accumulation of water (ascitis). The symptomatology of these eight is being explained seperately.

sanskrit_text: वातोदरे - उदरं शूनं कठिनं रुग्णं सशब्दं स्निग्धं च भवति । उच्छ्वासनिश्वासौ रुध्नाति । मूत्रपुरीषवातसङ्गः ॥ ५-८ ॥
transliteration: Vātodore - udaraṃ śūnaṃ kaṭhinaṃ rugṇaṃ saśabdaṃ snigdhaṃ ca bhavati | Ucchvāsaniḥśvāsau rudhnāti | Mūtrapurīṣavātasaṅgaḥ || 5-8 ||
commentary: In vātaja udara, the abdomen is swollen, hard, painful, produces sound on percussion, and is unctuous. It obstructs inhalation and exhalation. There is constipation of urine, faeces and flatus.

sanskrit_text: पित्तोदरे - ज्वरो मूर्च्छा दाहस्तृष्णा कटुकास्यता भ्रमोऽतिसारः पीतत्वं त्वगादिषु । हरितपीतताम्रसिरानद्धमुदरम् ॥ ९-१० ॥
transliteration: Pittodore - jvaro mūrcchā dāhastṛṣṇā kaṭukāsyatā bhramo'tisāraḥ pītatvaṃ tvagādiṣu | Haritapītatāmrasirānaddhamudaram || 9-10 ||
commentary: In pittodara, there is fever, syncope, burning sensation, thirst, pungent taste in the mouth, giddiness, diarrhoea, yellowish discolouration of skin etc. The abdomen is covered with green, yellow and coppery veins.

sanskrit_text: श्लेष्मोदरे - अङ्गसदनं स्वापः श्वयथुगौरवम् । निद्रोत्क्लेशोऽरुचिः श्वासः कासः शुक्लत्वगादिता । उदरं स्तिमितं स्निग्धं शुक्लराजीतं महत् । चिराभिवृद्धं कठिनं शीतस्पर्शं गुरु स्थिरम् ॥ ११-१२ ॥
transliteration: Śleṣmodare - aṅgasadanaṃ svāpaḥ śvayathugauravam | Nidrotkleśo'ruciḥ śvāsaḥ kāsaḥ śuklatvagāditā | Udaraṃ stimitaṃ snigdhaṃ śuklarājītaṃ mahat | Cirābhivṛddhaṃ kaṭhinaṃ śītasparśaṃ guru sthiram || 11-12 ||
commentary: In śleṣmodara, there is exhaustion of limbs, swelling, heaviness, excessive sleep, nausea, distaste, dyspnoea, cough, whitish discolouration of skin. The abdomen is steady, smooth, with white lines, large, slowly developing, hard, cold to touch, heavy and stable.

sanskrit_text: स्त्रीभ्योऽत्रपानं नखलोममूत्रविड्वातं वैरिभिः प्रयुक्तं गरांश्च दुष्टाम्बुदूषीविषसेवनाद्वा । तेनाशु रक्तं कुपिताश्च दोषाः कुर्युः सुदारुणं जठरं त्रिलिङ्गम् ॥ १३-१४ ॥
transliteration: Strībhyo'trapānaṃ nakhalomamūtraviḍvātaṃ vairibhiḥ prayuktaṃ garāṃśca duṣṭāmbudūṣīviṣasevanādvā | Tenāśu raktaṃ kupitāśca doṣāḥ kuryuḥ sudāruṇaṃ jaṭharaṃ triliṅgam || 13-14 ||
commentary: When women with bad intentions give food and drinks added with nails, hairs, urine and faecal matter or when the enemies intentionally poison the food or when the individual consumes polluted water and foods that become poison by means of putrefaction, the blood and the doṣas get aggravated immediately and cause abdominal disorders with the symptomatology of all three doṣas.

sanskrit_text: प्लीहोदरे - विदाह्यन्नपानसेविनो रक्तं कफं च प्रदूष्य प्लीहा वर्धते । स वामपार्श्वे वृद्धिं गतः शून्यं कुरुते । तत्राल्पज्वरो मन्दाग्निः कफपित्तलिङ्गम् । दक्षिणपार्श्वे यकृद्वृद्धिर्यकृद्दाल्युदरम् ॥ १५-१७ ॥
transliteration: Plīhodare - vidāhyannapānasevino raktaṃ kaphaṃ ca pradūṣya plīhā vardhate | Sa vāmapārśve vṛddhiṃ gataḥ śūnyaṃ kurute | Tatrālpajvaro mandāgniḥ kaphapittaliṅgam | Dakṣiṇapārśve yakṛdvṛddhiryakṛddālyudaram || 15-17 ||
commentary: The individuals who regularly take over-burnt and very wet food stuffs get their blood and kapha vitiated which cause plīha vṛddhi (splenomegaly) - this condition is called plīhodara. Plīha (spleen) is situated in the left side of the abdomen which increases in size and there will be severe depression in the individual. He suffers from low fever, depleted digestive fire. He is troubled with the symptoms of imbalanced kapha and pitta. If the swelling is seen on the other side of the abdomen (right side), it is then to be considered that the yakṛt (Liver) is enlarged and such condition is called yakṛddālyudara.

sanskrit_text: उदावर्तरुगानाहैर्वातिकं विद्यात् । भ्रमतृष्णादाहज्वरैः पैत्तिकम् । गुर्वरुचिस्तैमित्यैः कफिकम् ॥ १८ ॥
transliteration: Udāvartarugānāhairvātikaṃ vidyāt | Bhramatṛṣṇādāhajvaraiḥ paittikam | Gurvarucistaimityaiḥ kaphikam || 18 ||
commentary: If the individual suffering from plīhodara or yakṛddālyudara is having udāvarta (bloating of the abdomen), ruja (pain) and ānāha (flatulance) - vāta predominance should be understood; if he has delusion, thirst, burning sensation and fever - pitta predominance and in case there is kapha predominance, the individual suffers from heaviness, distaste and rigidity in the abdomen.

sanskrit_text: बद्धगुदे - गुदमार्गे मलेनावृते वातो गुदं न गच्छति । तेनोदरमानह्यति । रुजाश्च भवन्ति हृदयनाभ्योः ॥ १९-२० ॥
transliteration: Baddhagude - gudamārge malenāvṛte vāto gudaṃ na gacchati | Tenodaramānahyati | Rujāśca bhavanti hṛdayanābhyoḥ || 19-20 ||
commentary: In baddhagudodara, when the anal passage is obstructed by faeces, vāta does not move through the anus. This leads to bloating of the abdomen and pain in the heart and navel.

sanskrit_text: शल्यं तथा ज्ञोपहितं यदन्नं भुक्तं भिनत्त्यागतमन्यथा वा । तस्मात्स्रुतोऽन्नात्सलिलप्रकाशः स्रावः स्वदेहै गुदतस्तु भूयः । नाभेरधश्चोदरमेति वृद्धिं निस्तुद्यते दाल्यते चातिमात्रम् ॥ २१ ॥
transliteration: Śalyaṃ tathā jñopahitaṃ yadannaṃ bhuktaṃ bhinattyāgatamanyathā vā | Tasmātsruto'nnātsalilaprakāśaḥ srāvaḥ svadehair gudatastu bhūyaḥ | Nābheradhaścodarameti vṛddhiṃ nistudyate dālyate cātimātram || 21 ||
commentary: When a foreign body enters into the abdomen along with food and pierces the intestines or by any other means, the intestines get perforated causing watery exudation which passes out from the anal canal repeatedly. There will be swelling in the abdomen in the region below the umbilicus. There will be pinning and tearing pain. This condition is also known as parisrāvyudara.

sanskrit_text: यः स्नेहपीतोऽप्यनुवासितो वा वान्तो विरिक्तोऽप्यथवा निरूढः । पिबेदजलं शीतलमाशु तस्य स्रोतांसि दुष्यन्ति हि तद्ग्रहाणि । स्नेहोपलिप्तेष्वथवाऽपि तेषु दकोदरं पूर्ववदुपैति ॥ २२-२४ ॥
transliteration: Yaḥ snehapīto'pyanuvāsito vā vānto virikto'pyathavā nirūḍhaḥ | Pibedajalaṃ śītalamāśu tasya srotāṃsi duṣyanti hi tadgrahāṇi | Snehopalipteṣvathavā'pi teṣu dakodaraṃ pūrvavadupaiti || 22-24 ||
commentary: If an individual, after snehapāna (Therapeutic consumption of unctuous substance), use of unctuous or decoction enema, therapeutic emesis and therapeutic purgation - immediately consumes cold water, the udakavāha (water-carrying) channels in the body which are drenched with substances or not - are vitiated and cause dakodara (Ascitis?). The skin of the abdomen becomes smooth, abdomen looks very big, the umbilicus loosens contact and looks as if the abdomen is filled with water.

sanskrit_text: जन्मनैवोदरं सर्वं प्रायः कृच्छ्रतमं मतम् । बलिनस्तदजाताम्बु यत्नसाध्यं नवोत्थितम् ॥ २५ ॥ पक्षाद् बद्धगुदं चैव सर्वं जातोदकं तथा । प्रायो भवत्यभावाय छिद्रान्नं चोदरं नृणाम् ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration: Janmanaivodaraṃ sarvaṃ prāyaḥ kṛcchratamaṃ matam | Balinastadajātāmbu yatnasādhyaṃ navotthitam || 25 || Pakṣād baddhagudaṃ caiva sarvaṃ jātodakaṃ tathā | Prāyo bhavatyabhāvāya chidrānnaṃ codaraṃ nṛṇām || 26 ||
commentary: In general, by nature, all udara rogas are considered very difficult for cure. The udara afflicting the strong individual and where water accumulation has not been taken place, such condition is curable with proper effort. Baddhagudodara, after fifteen days of onset, and all udaras where water accumulation is set in and chidrāntra (where intestines are pierced) - kill the individual.

sanskrit_text: शूनाक्षं कुटिलोपस्थमुपक्लिन्नतनुत्वचम् । अभिन्नपरिक्षीणमग्निं चोदरिणं त्यजेत् ॥ २७ ॥ भिन्नपार्श्वमरोचकशोफातीसारयुक्तम् । निरूढेऽपि च यस्योदरं पूर्यते त्याज्यम् ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration: Śūnākṣaṃ kuṭilopasthamupaklinna tanutvacam | Abhinnaparikṣīṇamagniṃ codariṇaṃ tyajet || 27 || Bhinnapārśvamarocakaśophātīsārayuktam | Nirūḍhe'pi ca yasyodaraṃ pūryate tyājyam || 28 ||
commentary: The individual suffering from udara, who has swollen eyes, deformed genitalia, thin and wet skin, depleted strength, blood, musculature and digestive fire - is not to be considered for treatment. The udara patient who has broken flanks (weak-chest), can not relish food, suffers from oedema, diarrhoea and whose abdomen fills even after purgation - is to be discarded from treating.

sanskrit_text: रक्तपित्तकफान् वायुः प्रदुष्टान् बहिःसिराः । नीत्वा रुद्धगतिस्तैः कुर्यादुत्सेधं त्वग्मांससंश्रयम् ॥ १ ॥ उत्सेधं संहतं शोथं तमाहुर्निचयादतः । सर्वं हेतुविशेषैस्तु रूपभेदात् नवात्मकम् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Raktapittakaphān vāyuḥ praduṣṭān bahiḥsirāḥ | Nītvā ruddhagatistaiḥ kuryādutsedhaṃ tvagmāṃsasaṃśrayam || 1 || Utsedhaṃ saṃhataṃ śothaṃ tamāhurnicayādataḥ | Sarvaṃ hetuviśeṣaistu rūpabhedāt navātmakam || 2 ||
commentary: The aggravated vāyu brings the vitiated rakta, pitta and kapha to the outer veins which block the former resulting in the swelling due to deposition of the above in the skin and muscle tissue. This disease is considered as having the involvement of all three of the doṣas. However basing on the difference of aetiology and symptomatology, Śotha is of nine types i.e. 3 due to three doṣas individually, 3 due to combination of each two of the three doṣas; 1 due to all three doṣas together, 1 due to trauma, and 1 due to contact with poison.

sanskrit_text: दाहः सिरायामः सदनं चाङ्गानां पूर्वरूपाणि ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Dāhaḥ sirāyāmaḥ sadanaṃ cāṅgānāṃ pūrvarūpāṇi || 3 ||
commentary: The premonitory symptoms of śotha are - burning sensation, stretching pain in the veins and heaviness in the limbs.

sanskrit_text: शुद्धानामामयाविनामभुक्तानां क्षाराम्लतीक्ष्णोष्णगुरूणाम् । उपवासविशुद्धिक्षामाणां दधि मृद्वामशाकविरुद्धदुष्टगरचेष्टापीनसव्यायाममर्मोपघातविषमप्रसूतिप्रतिकर्मापचारैः । प्राकृतशोथः ॥ ४-५ ॥
transliteration: Śuddhānāmāmayāvināmabhuktānāṃ kṣārāmlatīkṣṇoṣṇagurūṇām | Upavāsaviśuddhikṣāmāṇāṃ dadhi mṛdvāmaśākaviruddhaduṣṭagaraceṣṭāpīnasavyāyāmamarmopaghātaviṣamaprasūtipratikarmāpacāraiḥ | Prākṛtaśothaḥ || 4-5 ||
commentary: Consumption of little amount of incompatible food by the individuals who have under gone cleansing therapy or afflicted by diseases, consumption of alkali foods, sour, fast, warm and heavy food by those who observe fasting or weakened after cleansing therapy or due to affliction of diseases : consumption of curds, wet mud, uncooked vegetables, incompatible food combination, purified foods and foods that are afflicted by poisons that originate due to typical combinations : suffering from piles, not indulging in any activity, not following the body cleansing measures, trauma to the vital parts, irregular child delivery and improper regimen after cleansing therapies; are the aetiological factors for the natural type of śotha (oedema caused by intrinsic factors).

sanskrit_text: चलं गुरु सशोफं सोष्मं सिरातनुत्वं रोमहर्षश्च वैवर्ण्यम् । सामान्यं शोथलिङ्गम् ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Calaṃ guru saśophaṃ soṣmaṃ sirātanutvaṃ romaharṣaśca vaivarṇyam | Sāmānyaṃ śothaliṅgam || 6 ||
commentary: Unstableness, feeling of heaviness, swelling, warmth on the skin, thinning of the veins, horripilation, and discolouration of the skin are the common signs and symptoms of Śotha.

sanskrit_text: चलस्तनुत्वक् परुषोऽरुणोऽसितः सुषुप्तिहर्षतोदयुतेऽनिमित्ततः । प्रशाम्यति प्रोन्नमति प्रपीडितो दिवाबली च श्वयथुः समीरणात् ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Calastanutvak paruṣo'ruṇo'sitaḥ suṣuptiharṣatodayute'nimittataḥ | Praśāmyati pronnamati prapīḍito divābalī ca śvayathuḥ samīraṇāt || 7 ||
commentary: Śotha of vāta-predominance keeps moving, the skin will be thin, rough, red and /or black in colour. There will be numbness, scintillation and pain. It palliates without any cause, swells back on pressing. And it will be prominent during day time.

sanskrit_text: मृदुः समुत्सन्नोऽसितपीतरागवान् । भ्रमज्वरस्वेदतृषामदान्वितः । उष्यते स्पष्टरुगस्रावकृत् । स पित्तशोथो भृशदाहपाकवान् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration: Mṛduḥ samutsanno'sitapītarāgavān | Bhramajvarasvedatṛṣāmadānvitaḥ | Uṣyate spaṣṭarugasrāvakṛt | Sa pittaśotho bhṛśadāhapākavān || 8 ||
commentary: The place of swelling is soft, sticking, black and yellow in colour and heat and pain is felt by touching. The individual has giddiness, fever, sweating, thirst and feeling of intoxication and his eyes are red in colour. Such state is called as Pitta śotha and has severe burning sensation and it ripens fast.

sanskrit_text: गुरुः स्थिरः पाण्डुररोचकान्वितः । प्रसेकनिद्राछर्दिमन्दाग्नियुक्तः । कृच्छ्रजन्मप्रशमो नोन्नमति प्रपीडितः । रात्रिबली कफशोथः ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration: Guruḥ sthiraḥ pāṇḍurarocakānvitaḥ | Prasekanidrāchardimandāgniyuktaḥ | Kṛcchrajanmapraśamo nonnamati prapīḍitaḥ | Rātribalī kaphaśothaḥ || 9 ||
commentary: The swollen part is heavy and stable. The individual has anaemia and anorexia; he dribbles saliva, feels sleepy, suffers from vomiting and has weak digestive fire. The swelling arises after long time and also takes long time to pacify. It does not raise back immediately after pressing (pitting oedema) the symptoms are prevalent during night time, such condition is known as kaphaja śotha.

sanskrit_text: युगपद्धेतुलिङ्गैस्तु द्वन्द्वजः । सर्वलिङ्गः सन्निपातिकः ॥ १० ॥
transliteration: Yugapaddhetuliṅgaistu dvandvajaḥ | Sarvaliṅgaḥ sannipātikaḥ || 10 ||
commentary: Due to admixture of the aetiological factors and symptomatology of any two of the three doṣas, Dvidoṣaja śotha takes place and combination of the signs and symptoms of all three doṣaja śothas, are seen in Sannipāta śotha.

sanskrit_text: अभिघातजः - शस्त्रप्रहारच्छेदनभेदनादिभिः । शीतोदधिवातैः । भल्लातककपिकच्छूरससंस्पर्शात् । त्वचि चलः सदाहरागः पित्तशोथसदृशः ॥ ११-१२ ॥
transliteration: Abhighātajaḥ - śastraprahāracchedanabhedanādibhiḥ | Śītodadhivātaiḥ | Bhallātakakapikacchūrasasaṃsparśāt | Tvaci calaḥ sadāharāgaḥ pittasothasadṛśaḥ || 11-12 ||
commentary: Śotha caused by trauma due to blow of weapons - cutting, breaking injuries etc; cold winds and winds of the sea; contact of juices of Bhallāta (marking nut) and awns of Kapikacchū (Mucuna pruriens) to the skin - is mobile on the skin, it has burning sensation reddish in colour with almost similarity of symptomatology of pitta type of śotha.

sanskrit_text: विषजः - सविषप्राणिनां परिसर्पणमूत्रणदंष्ट्रादन्तनखादिसंस्पर्शात् । विषमूत्रशुक्रपुरीषोपहतवस्त्रसंस्पर्शात् । विषवृक्षसमीरसंस्पर्शात् । संयोगजविषसंस्पर्शात् । मृदुश्चलोऽवलम्बी शीघ्रो दाहरुक्संयुतः ॥ १३-१४ ॥
transliteration: Viṣajaḥ - saviṣaprāṇināṃ parisarpaṇamūtraṇadaṃṣṭrādantanakhādisaṃsparśāt | Viṣamūtraśukrapurīṣopahatavastrasaṃsparśāt | Viṣavṛkṣasamīrasaṃsparśāt | Saṃyogajaviṣasaṃsparśāt | Mṛduścalo'valambī śīghro dāharuksaṃyutaḥ || 13-14 ||
commentary: Śotha of poisonous origin is caused by the contact in the form of crawling, urination of poisonous animals, bite by fangs, teeth, nails etc., of the poisonous, and non-poisonous animals; By wearing the cloths contaminated by faeces, urine, semen etc., of the poisonous animals, contact of the winds coming from poisonous trees and contact of combinational poisonous substances. The swelling in such cases is soft, mobile, moving downward in the body, fast and characterised by burning sensation and pain.

sanskrit_text: दोषाः श्वयथुमूर्ध्वं हि कुर्वन्त्यामाशयस्थिताः ॥ १५ ॥ पक्वाशयस्था मध्ये तु वर्चःस्थानगतास्त्वधः । कृत्स्नदेहमनुप्राप्ताः कुर्युः सर्वशरीरजम् ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration: Doṣāḥ śvayathumūrdhvaṃ hi kurvantyāmāśayasthitāḥ || 15 || Pakvāśayasthā madhye tu varcaḥsthānagatāstadhaḥ | Kṛtsnadehamanuprāptāḥ kuryuḥ sarvaśarīrajam || 16 ||
commentary: The doṣas situated in āmāśaya (stomach) produce śotha in the upper part of the body; those situated in the pakvāśaya (duodenum) cause swelling in the middle part of the body; those seated in the varca sthāna cause swelling in the lower part of the body and those situated all over the body cause swelling that spreads all over the body.

sanskrit_text: यो मध्यदेशे श्वयथुः स कष्टः सर्वगश्च यः । अर्धाङ्गेऽरिष्टभूतः स्याद्यश्चोर्ध्वं परिसर्पति ॥ १७ ॥ श्वासः पिपासा छर्दिश्च दौर्बल्यं ज्वर एव च । यस्य चात्र रुचिनाशः श्वयथुं तं विवर्जयेत् ॥ १८ ॥ अनन्योपद्रवकृतः शोथः पादसमुत्थितः । पुरुषं हन्ति नारीं च मुखजो गुह्यजो द्वयम् । नवोऽनुपद्रवः शोथः साध्योऽसाध्यः पुरेरितः ॥ १९ ॥ विवर्जयेत्कुक्ष्युदराश्रितं च तथा गले मर्मणि संश्रितम् ॥ २० ॥
transliteration: Yo madhyadeśe śvayathuḥ sa kaṣṭaḥ sarvagaśca yaḥ | Ardhāṅge'riṣṭabhūtaḥ syādyāś cordhvaṃ parisarpati || 17 || Śvāsaḥ pipāsā chardiśca daurbalyaṃ jvara eva ca | Yasya cātra ruci nāśaḥ śvayathuṃ taṃ vivarjayet || 18 || Ananyopadravakṛtaḥ śothaḥ pādasamutthitaḥ | Puruṣaṃ hanti nārīṃ ca mukhajo guhyajo dvayam | Navo'nupadravaḥ śothaḥ sādhyo'sādhyaḥ pureritaḥ || 19 || Vivarjayetkukṣyudarāśritaṃ ca tathā gale marmaṇi saṃśritam || 20 ||
commentary: The swelling manifesting in the middle is difficult for cure as also the one which spreads all over the body. Swelling that is manifested in half of the body as a complication to some other disease or as a definitive bad prognosis and that which spreads upwards and such śotha which is associated with dyspnoea, thirst, vomiting, debility, fever and lack of interest in consuming food, should be discarded. Śotha associated with complications that manifest on the feet in the men, kills them and that originating on the face in the women kills them. The śotha occurring on the genitalia of men and women kill both of them. New and uncomplicated śotha is curable while the others mentioned above are incurable. Śotha, occurring on the stomach and belly, throat and vital parts, that which is big in size, hard and rough and occurring in children, old and weak individuals - all these should be avoided from treatment.

sanskrit_text: वृद्धोऽनुव्यङ्गितवायुः शोथशूलकरश्चरन् । वङ्क्षणतः प्राप्य फलकोषाभिवाहिनीः ॥ १ ॥ प्रपीड्य धमनीर्वृद्धिं करोति फलकोषयोः । दोषास्रमेदोमूत्रान्त्रैः स वृद्धिः सप्तधा गदः ॥ २ ॥ मूत्रान्त्रजाव्यनिलाद्धेतुभेदस्तु केवलम् ॥
transliteration: Vṛddho'nuvyaṅgitavāyuḥ śothaśūlakaraścaran | Vaṅkṣaṇataḥ prāpya phalakoṣābhivāhinīḥ || 1 || Prapīḍya dhamanīrvṛddhiṃ karoti phalakoṣayoḥ | Doṣāstramedomūtrāntraiḥ sa vṛddhiḥ saptadhā gadaḥ || 2 || Mūtrāntrajāvyānilāddhetubhedastu kevalam ||
commentary: Aggravated Vāta which has downward movement and has the nature of causing Śotha (swelling) and Śūla (pain), reaches the testes and sac through groins enters the arteries that go into the testes, irritates them and causes swelling in the testes and the sac. This vṛddhi is of 7 types, viz., 1.Vātaja, 2. Pittaja, 3. Kaphaja, 4. Raktaja, 5. Medaja (Elephantiasis scrotum), 6. Mūtraja (Hydrocele) and 7. Antraja (Hernia). Though, mūtraja and antraja are of vāta origin, due to difference in aetiology, they are enumerated seperately.

sanskrit_text: वातवृद्धौ फलकोषं वातपूर्णमिव चलं रूक्षं रुजं चाऽहेतुकीम् । पित्तवृद्धावौडुम्बरसवर्णं दाहोष्मपाककरम् । कफवृद्धौ शीतगुरुस्निग्धकण्डूस्थिराल्परुक् । रक्तवृद्धौ कृष्णस्रावमपि पित्तलिङ्गम् । मेदोवृद्धौ कफलिङ्गं मृदु तालफलोपमम् । मूत्रवृद्धौ मूत्रधारणात् फलकोषः सशोफो जलपूर्णकल्पः सरुक् मूत्रकृच्छ्रवत् चलच्च ॥ ३-६ ॥
transliteration: Vātavṛddhau phalakoṣaṃ vātapūrṇamiva calaṃ rūkṣaṃ rujaṃ cāhetukīm | Pittavṛddhāvaudumbarasarvarṇaṃ dāhoṣmapākakaram | Kaphavṛddhau śītagurusnigdha kaṇḍūsthirālparuk | Raktavṛddhau kṛṣṇasrāvamapi pittaliṅgam | Medovṛddhau kaphaliṅgaṃ mṛdu tālaph alopamam | Mūtravṛddhau mūtradhāraṇāt phalakoṣaḥ saśopho jalapūrṇakalpaḥ saruk mūtrakṛcchravat calacca || 3-6 ||
commentary: Feeling of the sac as filled with vāta, mobility, rough in touch and pain without any stimulation are the signs and symptoms of vṛddhi caused by vāta. Vṛddhi of pitta is characterised by the colour of a fig fruit (Ficus glomerata), burning sensation, hot touch and ripening of blisters (if any); and the kapha type of vṛddhi has the signs and symptoms of cold touch, heaviness, smoothness, itching sensation, hardness and slight pain. In the Raktajavṛddhi, there will be blackish erosion apart from the symptomatology of pittaja vṛddhi. In the Medaja vṛddhi, the signs and symptoms of kaphajavṛddhi are seen and the sac is soft and appears like a Tālaphala (palmyrah fruit). The scrotum in the Mūtraja vṛddhi which occurs to the individual retaining urine for long- gets swollen and gives the feeling as if filled with water with irritation, soft and painful sensation as in dysuria while the scrotal sac keeps hanging.

sanskrit_text: वातप्रकोपकरैराहारविहारैः । क्षुद्रान्त्रं वातेनापनीतं वङ्क्षणे ग्रन्थिमिव करोति । तदुपेक्षया वृषणकोशे पतितं वृषणशोथमानाहरुक्स्तम्भकरम् । प्रपीड्यमानं स्वस्थानमागच्छति । मुक्तं पुनरागच्छति । एतदन्त्रवृद्धिरिति ज्ञेयम् ॥ ७-१० ॥
transliteration: Vātaprakopakarai rāhāravihāraiḥ | Kṣudrāntraṃ vātenāpanītaṃ vaṅkṣaṇe granthimiva karoti | Tad upekṣayā vṛṣaṇakośe patitaṃ vṛṣaṇaśothamānāharukstambhakaram | Prapīḍyamānaṃ svasthānamāgacchati | Muktaṃ punarāgacchati | Etadantravṛddhir iti jñeyam || 7-10 ||
commentary: Due to intake of vāta-provoking diet, bathing or sitting in cold water, oppression of natural urges and trying to pass them out forcibly, lifting weights, walking heavily, moving the bodily limbs irregularly and other disturbing activities, a part of the small intestines are irritated by vāta and brought down from its place and makes a tumour like appearance in the groin with swelling. On neglecting, (the intestines enter the scrotal sac and) it causes swelling of the scrotum, with bloating, pain and rigidity. On pressing, the intestines go back with a typical sound into the abdomen and on leaving, it comes into the scrotal sac. This is called antravṛddhi (Hernia) which has features as in vāta vṛddhi and is incurable.

sanskrit_text: कफमेदोभ्यां गलमध्ये गण्डः श्लेष्ममेदसोः प्रकोपात् । स च त्रिविधो वातपित्तकफभेदात् । तत्र वातिकं पित्तिकं कफिकं मेदोजं च । एतानि क्रमेण वक्ष्यामः ॥ १-२ ॥
transliteration: Kaphamedobhyāṃ galamadhye gaṇḍaḥ śleṣmamedasoḥ prakōpāt | Sa ca trividho vātapittakaphabhedāt | Tatra vātikaṃ pittikaṃ kaphikaṃ medojaṃ ca | Etāni krameṇa vakṣyāmaḥ || 1-2 ||
commentary: Due to vitiation of kapha and medas, a swelling (gaṇḍa) occurs in the middle of the neck. This is of three types based on vāta, pitta and kapha predominance. It can also be of four types including medoja. These will be described in order.

sanskrit_text: तोदान्वितः कृष्णसिरावनद्धः श्यावोऽरुणो वा पवनात्मकस्तु । पारुष्ययुक्तश्चिरवृद्ध्यपाको यदृच्छया पाकमियात्कदाचित् ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Todānvitaḥ kṛṣṇasirāvanaddhaḥ śyāvo'ruṇo vā pavanātmakastu | Pāruṣyayuktaściravṛddhyapāko yadṛcchayā pākamiyātkadācit || 3 ||
commentary: The individual suffering from vātaja galaganda has distaste in his mouth and his palate and throat are dried. He has pinning sensation in the affected part which is seen covered with blackish arteries, the skin is blackish or red in colour, rough in touch, develops slowly and the swelling does not ripen. Accidentally or very rarely it is ripened.

sanskrit_text: स्थिरः सवर्णो गुरुः सकण्डूः शीतो महांश्चापि कफात्मकस्तु । चिराभिवृद्धिं भजते चिराद्वा प्रपच्यते मन्दरुजः कदाचित् ॥ ४-५ ॥
transliteration: Sthiraḥ savarṇo guruḥ sakaṇḍūḥ śīto mahāṃścāpi kaphātmakastu | Cirābhivṛddhiṃ bhajate cirādvā prapacyate mandarujaḥ kadācit || 4-5 ||
commentary: In kapha type of galaganda, the swollen part is stable, has the colour of the body, heavy, has severe itching sensation, cold in touch and big in size. It grows slowly and also ripens after long course of time. It has mild pain rarely. The individual suffering with this, perceives sweet taste in his mouth and he has sticky feeling in the palate and throat.

sanskrit_text: मेदोजं स्निग्धं महत् स्थिरं मन्दरुजम् । तृतीयप्रभृतिषु चिराकारि ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Medojaṃ snigdhaṃ mahat sthiram mandarujam | Tṛtīyaprabhṛtiṣu cirākāri || 6 ||
commentary: Medoja galaganda is unctuous, large, stable and mildly painful. From the third type onwards, it takes a long time to manifest.

sanskrit_text: गलगण्डो गण्डमालां करोति क्षपयति च । सा गण्डमाला कफमेदोभ्याम् । कर्कन्धुकोलामलकप्रमाणैः । चिरात् पाकं गच्छति ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Galagaṇḍo gaṇḍamālāṃ karoti kṣapayati ca | Sā gaṇḍamālā kaphamedobhyām | Karkandhukolāmalakapramāṇaiḥ | Cirāt pākaṃ gacchati || 7 ||
commentary: Due to vitiated meda and kapha a number of gaṇḍas (morbid growths) occur in the arm pit, on the scapular region, neck, throat and the groin region in the size of karkandhu (small ziziphus fruit), kola (ordinary ziziphus fruit) and āmalakī (goose-berry) which ripen slowly after long time of onset, are called gaṇḍamālā.

sanskrit_text: ते ग्रन्थयः केचिदवाप्तपाकाः स्रवन्ति नश्यन्ति भवन्ति चान्ये । कालानुबन्धं चिरमादधाति सैवापचीति प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration: Te granthayaḥ kecidavāptapākāḥ sravanti naśyanti bhavanti cānye | Kālānubandhaṃ ciramādadhāti saivāpacīti pravadanti tajjñāḥ || 8 ||
commentary: Those tumour like swellings get ripened, exudate the slough and get suppressed and some others originate in the near vicinity. In this way this disease continues to last long. This is called apacī according to the specialist physicians.

sanskrit_text: वातादयो मांसमसृक् प्रदुष्टाः संदूष्य मेदश्च तथा सिराश्च । वृत्तोन्नतं विग्रथितं च शोथं कुर्वन्त्यतो ग्रन्थिरिति प्रदिष्टः ॥ ९ ॥ स्थिरोन्नतो विग्रथितो वृत्तः खरः स्निग्धः कठिनो मृदुश्च ॥ १० ॥
transliteration: Vātādayo māṃsam asṛk praduṣṭāḥ saṃdūṣya medaśca tathā sirāśca | Vṛttonnataṃ vigrathitaṃ ca śothaṃ kurvantyato granthiriti pradiṣṭaḥ || 9 || Sthironnato vigrathito vṛttaḥ kharaḥ snigdhaḥ kaṭhino mṛduśca || 10 ||
commentary: The aggravated Tridoṣas vitiate māṃsa (muscle-tissue), Asṛk (blood), meda (fat) and sirā (blood vessels) and cause swelling which is round in shape, big in size and hard for touch that looks solidified which is why it is called granthi (tumour). It can be stable, elevated, round, rough, unctuous, hard or soft.

sanskrit_text: रूक्षः कृष्णारुणो विषमः स्तब्धः स्निग्धः स्पर्शासहः । आयम्यवृश्च्यमानमथ्यमानभिद्यमान इव मन्यते । अस्रावी च ॥ ११-१२ ॥
transliteration: Rūkṣaḥ kṛṣṇāruṇo viṣamaḥ stabdhaḥ snigdhaḥ sparśāsahaḥ | Āyamyavṛścyamānamathyamānabhidyamāna iva manyate | Asrāvī ca || 11-12 ||
commentary: Vātaja granthi is rough, blackish-red, irregular, rigid, unctuous and tender to touch. The patient feels as if he is thrown out, squeezed and broken. The tumour is black in colour, soft and blown like bladder and on opening, it exudes clear liquid.

sanskrit_text: दाहोष्मयुतः शीघ्रपाकः प्रज्वलन्निव । रक्तपीतहारिद्राभः सोष्मास्रावी च ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration: Dāhoṣmayutaḥ śīghrapākaḥ prajvalanniva | Raktapītahāridrābhaḥ soṣmāsrāvī ca || 13 ||
commentary: In pittaja granthi, there is severe burning sensation, warmth in the tumour; it ripens fast and the individual feels as if it is burning. The colour of the tumour is red or yellow or yellowish red and on opening there is warm exudation.

sanskrit_text: शीतः सवर्णोऽल्परुक् स्थिरः पाषाणवत् । चिरवृद्धिः पक्वे श्वेतं घनं पूयं स्रवति ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration: Śītaḥ savarṇo'lparuk sthiraḥ pāṣāṇavat | Ciravṛddhiḥ pakve śvetaṃ ghanaṃ pūyaṃ sravati || 14 ||
commentary: The kapha-type of tumour is cold in touch, has same colour as the skin, with slight sensation and little pain. It is solidified as a stone. The growth is very slow and on opening, there is white - thick pus as exudation.

sanskrit_text: शरीरवृद्धिक्षयानुवृद्धिक्षयः । स्निग्धदर्शनस्पर्शो महान् सकण्डूरल्परुक् । भिन्ने मधूच्छिष्टतिलपिण्याकनिभं मेदः स्रवति ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration: Śarīravṛddhikṣayānuvṛddhikṣayaḥ | Snigdh darśanasparśo mahān sakaṇḍūralparuk | Bhinne madhūcchiṣṭatilapiṇyākanibhaṃ medaḥ sravati || 15 ||
commentary: The medoja (fat-originated) tumour repletes and depletes as the body of the patient increases and decreases; it is oily in looks and touch, big in size with itching sensation and little pain and on getting opened, it exudes meda that looks like the mixture of ghee and sesame cake.

sanskrit_text: चलो रुग्वान् यः स कृच्छ्रसाध्यः । निश्चलो निरुजो महान् मर्मजश्च त्याज्यः ॥ १६-१७ ॥
transliteration: Calo rugvān yaḥ sa kṛcchrasādhyaḥ | Niścalo nirujo mahān marmajaśca tyājyaḥ || 16-17 ||
commentary: A granthi which is mobile and painful is difficult for cure. The same when becomes painless, immobile, big in size and also originated on one of the marmas (vital points), should be avoided from treating.

sanskrit_text: ग्रीवादिषु मांसमसृक् संमूर्च्छितं वृत्तमचलमल्परुजं महत् । स्थिरं चिरवृद्ध्यपाकमवगाढं चार्बुदम् ॥ १८-१९ ॥
transliteration: Grīvādiṣu māṃsamasṛk saṃmūrcchitaṃ vṛttam acalam alparujaṃ mahat | Sthiraṃ ciravṛddhyapākam avagāḍhaṃ cārbudam || 18-19 ||
commentary: In some part of the neck, the doṣas accumulate and vitiate māṃsa (muscle) and asṛk - blood and create muscular growth which is round in shape, immobile, having less pain, big in size, big based that grows slowly, does not get ripened and deep rooted. This is called arbuda (a kind of tumour).

sanskrit_text: दोषः प्रदुष्टो रक्तं सिराश्च संकुच्य सम्पीड्य । वृत्तमुत्सन्नमपाकं सास्रावं मांसपिण्डमाशुवृद्धं मांसाङ्कुरैराचितं करोति । अजस्रं रुधिरं स्रवति । एतद्रक्तार्बुदमसाध्यम् ॥ २०-२१ ॥
transliteration: Doṣaḥ praduṣṭo raktaṃ sirāśca saṃkucya sampīḍya | Vṛttamutsannamapākaṃ sāsrāvaṃ māṃsapiṇḍam āśuvṛddhaṃ māṃsāṅkurairācitaṃ karoti | Ajasraṃ rudhiraṃ sravati | Etad raktārbudam asādhyam || 20-21 ||
commentary: The aggravated doṣa, having occupied blood and veins, constricts, and squeezes them and causes a round morsel shaped muscle tissue which does not ripen, keeps exudating and filled with small muscular growth all around. There will be continuous oozing of blood from this growth. This variety of arbuda which is called raktārbuda is considered incurable.

sanskrit_text: मुष्टिप्रहारादिभिरभिहतेऽङ्गे मांसं प्रदुष्टं जनयेच्छोथम् । अवेदनं स्निग्धमनन्यवर्णमपाकमश्मोपममप्रचाल्यम् । प्रदुष्टमांसस्य नरस्य गदमेतद्भवेन्मांसपरायणस्य ॥ २२-२३ ॥
transliteration: Muṣṭiprahārādibhirabhihate'ṅge māṃsaṃ praduṣṭaṃ janayecchotham | Avedanaṃ snigdhamananyavarṇamapākamaśmopamamapracālyam | Praduṣṭamāṃsasya narasya gadametadbhavenmāṃsaparāyaṇasya || 22-23 ||
commentary: Due to blows of fist etc., the individual gets the muscle of that area vitiated and there arises growth (after some time) which has no pain, oily in touch, same colour as that of the skin, does not ripen, solid like a stone and which can not be moved. This generally occurs to those who have vitiated māṃsadhātu (muscle tissue) and those who consume more of meat in food. This is called māṃsārbuda and is said to be incurable.

sanskrit_text: स्राविणां मर्मजानामचलानां चार्बुदानां त्यागः ॥ २४ ॥
transliteration: Srāviṇāṃ marmajānāmacalānāṃ cārbudānāṃ tyāgaḥ || 24 ||
commentary: Among the curable ones also those which have exudation, originated on the vital point and are immobile - are to be avoided from treatment.

sanskrit_text: यद्यर्बुदादर्बुदमुत्पद्यते तदध्यर्बुदम् । युगपदेकतः पृथग्वा द्विरर्बुदम् ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration: Yadyarbudādarbudamutpadyate tadadhyarbudam | Yugapadekataḥ pṛthagvā dvirarbudam || 25 ||
commentary: If a new arbuda arises on the existing one, it is called adhyarbuda by the specialists. If two of them arise at one time or one after another, it is known as dvirarbuda and is incurable.

sanskrit_text: कफप्राधान्यान्मेदसो बाहुल्याद्दोषस्थिरत्वाद्ग्रन्थिनिबिडत्वाच्चार्बुदानामपाकः ॥ २६ ॥
transliteration: Kaphaprādhānyānmedaso bāhulyāddoṣasthiratvādgranthinibiḍatvāccārbudānāmapākaḥ || 26 ||
commentary: The arbudas do not get ripened because of predominance of kapha, excessive quantity of medas, stability of doṣas and closely woven nature of the doṣas in arbuda. This is the nature of all types of arbuda.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तकफैः क्षीणशोणितमांसानां श्लीपदं जायते । तद्वातिकं पैत्तिकं कफजं संनिपातिकं च । तत्र वातिके चलं सशूलं रूक्षं कृष्णारुणम् । पैत्तिके पीतं सदाहं सरुजम् । कफजे श्वेतं स्निग्धं स्थिरं गुरु सकण्डूम् । संनिपातिके सर्वलिङ्गम् ॥ १-३ ॥
transliteration: Vātapittakaphaiḥ kṣīṇaśoṇitamāṃsānāṃ ślīpadaṃ jāyate | Tadvātikaṃ paittikaṃ kaphajaṃ sannipātikaṃ ca | Tatra vātike calaṃ saśūlaṃ rūkṣaṃ kṛṣṇāruṇam | Paittike pītaṃ sadāhaṃ sarujam | Kaphaje śvetaṃ snigdhaṃ sthiraṃ guru sakaṇḍūm | Sannipātike sarvaliṅgam || 1-3 ||
commentary: Ślīpada (elephantiasis) is caused by vāta, pitta and kapha in individuals with depleted blood and muscle tissue. It is of four types: vātika, paittika, kaphaja and sannipātika. In vātika type, it is mobile, painful, rough and blackish-red. In paittika type, it is yellow, with burning sensation and pain. In kaphaja type, it is white, unctuous, stable, heavy and with itching. In sannipātika type, all symptoms are present.

sanskrit_text: वल्मीकमिव संजातं बहुशिखराकारं ग्रन्थिभिरुपचितम् । संवत्सरातीतमतिमहत् श्लीपदं वर्जयेत् ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Valmīkamiva sañjātaṃ bahuśikhākāraṃ granthibhirupacitam | Saṃvatsarātītamatimahat ślīpadaṃ varjayet || 4 ||
commentary: Ślīpada which looks like an ant-hill, filled with thorny growth all over, crossed one year of duration and very big in size - should not be considered for treatment.

sanskrit_text: श्लीपदानि कफोच्छ्रितानि । गुरुत्वं च महत्त्वं च यस्मान्नाति कफं विना ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration: Ślīpadāni kaphocchritāni | Gurutvaṃ ca mahattvaṃ ca yasmānnāti kaphaṃ vinā || 5 ||
commentary: Though these (Ślīpadas) are three in number kapha is the predominant doṣa because the heaviness and magnitude are not possible without kapha.

sanskrit_text: पुराणोदकभूविष्ठाः सर्वर्तुषु च शीतलाः । ये देशास्तेषु जायन्ते श्लीपदानि विशेषतः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Purāṇodakabhūviṣṭhāḥ sarvartuṣu ca śītalāḥ | Ye deśāsteṣu jāyante ślīpadāni viśeṣataḥ || 6 ||
commentary: In the places where stagnant water is abundant and temperature is low in all seasons, more incidence of Ślīpada, specially, is seen.

sanskrit_text: यः कफप्रकृतिः कफवृद्धिकरमाहारविहारं च सेवते । स श्लीपदी स्रावी संप्राप्तसमस्तलिङ्गः सकण्डूः श्लेष्मयुतः प्रत्याख्येयः ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Yaḥ kaphaprakṛtiḥ kaphavṛddhikaramāhāravihāraṃ ca sevate | Sa ślīpadī srāvī saṃprāptasamastaliṅgaḥ sakaṇḍūḥ śleṣmayutaḥ pratyākhyeyaḥ || 7 ||
commentary: If the individual, who has kapha temperament and consumes food and also follows the routine that increases kapha in the body and suffers from Ślīpada with exudation, associated with highly developed complete symptomatology, pruritus and oozing kapha (phlegm), he should not be considered for treatment.

sanskrit_text: पित्तरक्तमांसमेदोमज्जमूत्राणि दोषैः संमूर्च्छितानि विद्रधिं जनयन्ति । सा त्वन्तर्वा भवति बहिर्वा । बहिर्विद्रधिः षड्विधो वातपित्तकफसन्निपातरक्तागन्तुभेदात् ॥ १-३ ॥
transliteration: Pittaraktamāṃsamedomajjamūtrāṇi doṣaiḥ saṃmūrcchitāni vidradhiṃ janayanti | Sā tvantarvā bhavati bahirvā | Bahirvidradhiḥ ṣaḍvidho vātapittakaphasannipātaraktāgantubhedāt || 1-3 ||
commentary: Pitta, rakta, māṃsa, medas, majjā and mūtra when vitiated by doṣas cause vidradhi. It is either internal or external. External vidradhi is of six types based on vāta, pitta, kapha, sannipāta, rakta and āgantu.

sanskrit_text: कृष्णोऽरुणो वा विषमो भृशमत्यर्थवेदनः । चित्रोत्थानप्रपाकश्च विद्रधिर्वातसंभवः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Kṛṣṇo'ruṇo vā viṣamo bhṛśamatyarthavedanaḥ | Citrotthānaprapākaśca vidradhirvātasaṃbhavaḥ || 4 ||
commentary: The colour of the Vidradhi will be either black or red; irregular in size, has severe pain and has typical onset and ripening - in the case of Vāta predominance in Vidradhi.

sanskrit_text: पक्वौडुम्बरसंकाशः श्यावो वा ज्वरदाहवान् । क्षिप्रोत्थानप्रपाकश्च विद्रधिः पित्तसंभवः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration: Pakvauḍumbarasaṃkāśaḥ śyāvo vā jvaradāhavān | Kṣiprotthānaprapākaśca vidradhiḥ pittasaṃbhavaḥ || 5 ||
commentary: Vidradhi caused by the predominance of pitta looks in the colour of a ripened fig fruit or blackish. It is associated with fever and burning sensation and originates and ripens fast.

sanskrit_text: शरावसदृशः पाण्डुः शीतः स्निग्धोऽल्पवेदनः । चिरोत्थानप्रपाकश्च विद्रधिः कफसंभवः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Śarāvasadṛśaḥ pāṇḍuḥ śītaḥ snigdho'lpavedanaḥ | Cirotthānaprapākaśca vidradhiḥ kaphasaṃbhavaḥ || 6 ||
commentary: In kapha-type, the vidradhi looks like a śarāva (earthen cassarole) in shape, pale in colour, cold in touch, oily and associated with slight pain. The onset and ripening are delayed in this case.

sanskrit_text: नानावर्णरुजास्रावो घाटावद्विषमो महान् । विषमोत्थानपाकश्च विद्रधिः सन्निपातिकः ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Nānāvarṇarujāsrāvo ghāṭāvadviṣamo mahān | Viṣamotthānapākaśca vidradhiḥ sannipātikaḥ || 7 ||
commentary: The sannipāta type of vidradhi is associated with various colour, pain and exudation; looks like the ghāṭā (the high rising preceding part of the neck on the back of an ox); irregular in size and ripening style and very big in size.

sanskrit_text: तैस्तैराघातैरभिहते क्षते वाऽपथ्यकारिणः । क्षतोष्मा वायुविसृतः सरक्तं पित्तमीरयेत् । ज्वरतृष्णा च दाहश्च जायते तस्य देहिनः । आगन्तुर्विद्रधिर्ज्ञेयः पित्तविद्रधिलक्षणः ॥ ८-९ ॥
transliteration: Taistairāghātairabhihate kṣate vā'pathyakāriṇaḥ | Kṣatoṣmā vāyurvisṛtaḥ saraktaṃ pittamīrayet | Jvaratṛṣṇā ca dāhaśca jāyate tasya dehinaḥ | Āganturvidradhirjñeyaḥ pittavidradhilakṣaṇaḥ || 8-9 ||
commentary: Having hit by sticks and or stones, weapons etc., if the individual indulges in incompatible foods and behaviour aspects, the warmth of the injury gets provoked by vāta and disturbs pitta along with rakta, causing fever, thirst and burning sensation to him. This is called Āgantuja vidradhi. Its symptomatology is similar to that of pitta vidradhi.

sanskrit_text: रक्तजः कृष्णसिराजालचितः कृष्णरक्तः सदाहरुक् । पित्तविद्रधिलक्षणः ॥ १० ॥
transliteration: Raktajaḥ kṛṣṇasirājālacitaḥ kṛṣṇaraktaḥ sadāharuk | Pittavidradhilakṣaṇaḥ || 10 ||
commentary: The vidradhi caused by rakta has black, striated erosions on it, blackish in colour and associated with severe burning sensation and pain. The symptomatology is like that of pitta vidradhi.

sanskrit_text: गुल्मवल्मीकवदुन्नतं दोषाः कुर्वन्ति गुदबस्तिनाभ्युदरवङ्क्षणकटीकपालयकृद्प्लीहोरःक्लोमादिषु । तत्र गुदे वातमूत्रसङ्गः । बस्तौ मूत्रसङ्गः । नाभ्यां हिक्कानाहौ । उदरे वातकोपः । वङ्क्षणयोः कटीपृष्ठरुक् । पार्श्वसंकोचः प्लीह्नि । हृदि सर्वाङ्गग्रहः । कासश्वासहिक्काः यकृति । क्लोम्नि तृष्णा ॥ ११-१६ ॥
transliteration: Gulmavalmīkavadunnataṃ doṣāḥ kurvanti gudabastinābhyudaravaṅkṣaṇakaṭīkapālayakṛdplīhoraḥklomādiṣu | Tatra gude vātamūtrasaṅgaḥ | Bastau mūtrasaṅgaḥ | Nābhyāṃ hikkānāhau | Udare vātakopaḥ | Vaṅkṣaṇayoḥ kaṭīpṛṣṭharuk | Pārśvasaṃkocaḥ plīhni | Hṛdi sarvāṅgagrahaḥ | Kāsaśvāsahikkāḥ yakṛti | Klomni tṛṣṇā || 11-16 ||
commentary: The Doṣas having aggravated, either individually or unitedly, cause vidradhi which looks like gulma (a bush like formation) and valmīka (ant-hill) and high rising. This development takes place in the anus at the orifice of bladder, navel, abdomen, groins, kidneys, spleen, liver and/or pancreas. The symptomatology is to be understood as in the case of external vidradhi. As per the place of origin, there are specific features such as - when vidradhi arises in the anus, there is obstruction in vāta (fart), dysuria, in the case of vidradhi originating in the basti (bladder); hiccup and bloating when it is in the navel, aggravation of vāta when vidradhi takes root in the abdomen and when the vidradhi makes shelter in the groins, there will be severe gripping sensation in low-back and back; constriction in flanks is the sign of vidradhi that originates in kidneys; the intake of breath is obstructed when vidradhi occurs in the spleen; when it occurs in the heart, there is severe gripping sensation/rigidity in all over the body and cough; dyspnoea and hiccup are seen when it occurs in the liver and if it raises in the pancreas, severe thirst is present.

sanskrit_text: अधः पाको विद्रधेर्जीवति । ऊर्ध्वं पाके म्रियते । हृन्नाभिबस्तिषु भिन्नं म्रियते । अन्यत्र भिन्ने जीवति ॥ १७-१८ ॥
transliteration: Adhaḥ pāko vidradherjīvati | Ūrdhvaṃ pāke mriyate | Hṛnnābhibastiṣu bhinnaṃ mriyate | Anyatra bhinne jīvati || 17-18 ||
commentary: A patient of vidradhi having exudation from the lower end, usually lives (escape from the death). The disease kills him when the exudation comes from the upper end. When the exudation comes out through the skin from the vidradhi arisen in other than heart, navel and bladder, the individual may, by chance, escape the death but if it is from the above mentioned places, death is inevitable.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपातं वर्जयित्वा पञ्च विद्रधयः साध्याः । आमपक्वदग्धत्वं सोथवत् । यस्य च विद्रधौ वातमूत्रसङ्गश्छर्दिहिक्कातृष्णारुक्श्वासाः स म्रियते ॥ १९-२० ॥
transliteration: Sannipātaṃ varjayitvā pañca vidradhayaḥ sādhyāḥ | Āmapakvadagdhatvaṃ śothavat | Yasya ca vidradhau vātamūtrasaṅgaśchardihikkātṛṣṇārukśvāsāḥ sa mriyate || 19-20 ||
commentary: Leaving the Sannipāta variety, other five types of vidradhi are curable. The stages of unripe, ripened and burnt conditions of vidradhi are to be understood as in the case of Śotha. If an individual suffering from vidradhi develops flatulance, obstruction of urine, vomiting, hiccup, thirst, pain and dyspnoea, he will be destroyed.

sanskrit_text: पूर्वरूपं व्रणस्य शोथः । स षड्विधः - वातपित्तकफसन्निपातरक्तागन्तुभेदात् । तत्र वातादीनां लक्षणं पूर्वोक्तम् ॥ १-२ ॥
transliteration: Pūrvarūpaṃ vraṇasya śothaḥ | Sa ṣaḍvidhaḥ - vātapittakaphasannipātaraktāgantubhedāt | Tatra vātādīnāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ pūrvoktam || 1-2 ||
commentary: The inflammation that occurs in a particular area is considered as a premonitory symptom of an wound. This of six types viz., three due to each of the three doṣas individually, one due to all of them, one due to rakta and one due to sudden cause. They have the same type of symptomatology as that of Śotha which are envisaged earlier. The specific features to determine the ripening or unripe condition are being explained (in the following stanzas).

sanskrit_text: वातजे विषमपाकः । पित्तजे शीघ्रपाकः । कफजे चिरपाकः । रक्तागन्तुजयोः पित्तजवत् ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Vātaje viṣamapākaḥ | Pittaje śīghrapākaḥ | Kaphaje cirapākaḥ | Raktāgantujayoḥ pittajavat || 3 ||
commentary: The ripening takes place irregularly in vāta type of vraṇa śotha. It occurs fast in pitta type and it is delayed in kapha type of vraṇa śotha. In rakta (blood) and āgantu (sudden) originated types the ripening takes place (fast), as in the case of pittaja vraṇaśotha.

sanskrit_text: अल्पोष्माल्पशोफः सवर्णः स्थिरः स्पर्शासहो रुक्च आमलिङ्गम् । पच्यमाने दग्धविदग्धमथ्यमानच्छिद्यमानभिद्यमानविद्धप्रतिविद्धानामिव वेदनाः । दाहोष्मा रागः स्पन्दनं च । नास्ति सुखं स्थितस्य । मूत्रकोशवदुच्छूनं सज्वरतृष्णारोचकम् ॥ ४-८ ॥
transliteration: Alpoṣmālpaśophaḥ savarṇaḥ sthiraḥ sparśāsaho rukca āmaliṅgam | Pacyamāne dagdhavidagdhamathyamānacchidyamānabhidyamānaviddhapratividdhānāmiva vedanāḥ | Dāhoṣmā rāgaḥ spandanaṃ ca | Nāsti sukhaṃ sthit asya | Mūtrakośavaducchūnaṃ sajvaratṛṣṇārocakam || 4-8 ||
commentary: Mild heat and inflammation, hardness having same colour as that of the skin and mild pain are the features of āma (unripe) vraṇa śotha. During the pacyamāna (ripening) stage, it feels as if being burnt by fire, being ripened forcibly by applying alkalies, being bitten by many ants, being cut, being opened by weapons, being hit by stick, being squeezed with hands and being pierced with needles. There is burning and feeling of heat on the inflamed area, discolouration and also feeling of manipulation with fingers. There is no relief even on sitting, lying down or standing as in the case of scorpion-sting. The swelling looks like the bloated bladder and the individual has fever, thirst and distaste during this stage.

sanskrit_text: पक्वे भृशं पित्तलिङ्गम् । शोथाद्व्रणः पाकात् ॥ ९ ॥ व्रणशोथस्य पाको रक्तस्यैव । कफजे तु मन्दपाकः ॥ १०-११ ॥
transliteration: Pakve bhṛśaṃ pittaliṅgam | Śothādvraṇaḥ pākāt || 9 || Vraṇaśothasya pāko raktasyaiva | Kaphaje tu mandapākaḥ || 10-11 ||
commentary: When the inflammation ripens, pitta symptoms are seen predominantly during that ripening stage because the baking takes place due to aggravation of pitta. The baking or ripening occurs in the morbid factors only. Fever, thirst, distaste etc., are only the features of pitta. In the kapha śotha, the ripening is delayed.

sanskrit_text: गम्भीरपाके सर्वलिङ्गं दृश्यते । कफाभिघातजयोः पाकसंशयः । स्वर्णलाभे पाको विशेषः ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration: Gambhīrapāke sarvaliṅgaṃ dṛśyate | Kaphābhighātajayoḥ pākasaṃśayaḥ | Svarṇalābhe pāko viśeṣaḥ || 12 ||
commentary: In deep ripening of vraṇa śotha, features of all three doṣas are seen. In kapha and abhighāta (traumatic) types, there is confusion regarding the ripening. When the swelling attains skin colour, there is no doubt about ripening.

sanskrit_text: यथा वायुना क्षिप्तोऽग्निः सर्वं तृणराशिं दहति । एवमपक्वमपनष्टं पूयं मांससिरास्नायूनि दहति ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration: Yathā vāyunā kṣipto'gniḥ sarvaṃ tṛṇarāśiṃ dahati | Evamapakvamapanaṣṭaṃ pūyaṃ māṃsasirāsnāyūni dahati || 13 ||
commentary: As the fire burns the whole heap of grass with the help of vāyu (wind), in the same way the pus which is not drained out, eats away the muscle, veins and the ligaments.

sanskrit_text: आमपक्वपच्यमानज्ञः स वैद्यः शेषाश्चौराः । आमं छिन्दन् पक्वमच्छिन्दन् श्वपचौ स्याताम् ॥ १४-१५ ॥
transliteration: Āmapakvapacyamānajñaḥ sa vaidyaḥ śeṣāścaurāḥ | Āmaṃ chindan pakvamacchindan śvapacau syātām || 14-15 ||
commentary: He is the real physician who knows the state of unripe, ripening and ripened conditions (of vraṇa śotha) properly and the others (who do not possess this knowledge) are only thieves. The one who cuts open the unripe vraṇa śotha and the one who does not intervene after the vraṇa śotha gets ripened, are considered out-caste since they act without proper discrimination.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तकफसन्निपातरक्तागन्तुभेदात् षड्विधो व्रणः । वातिके रूक्षः कृष्णारुणः स्तब्धोऽल्पस्रावः । पैत्तिके पीतरक्तः स्रावी दाहज्वरकृत् । कफजे श्वेतः स्निग्धः स्थिरः सकण्डूः । सन्निपातिके सर्वलिङ्गम् । रक्तजे पित्तलिङ्गं कृष्णस्रावम् । आगन्तौ यथाघातम् ॥ १-४ ॥
transliteration: Vātapittakaphasannipātaraktāgantubhedāt ṣaḍvidho vraṇaḥ | Vātike rūkṣaḥ kṛṣṇāruṇaḥ stabdho'lpasrāvaḥ | Paittike pītaraktaḥ srāvī dāhajvarakṛt | Kaphaje śvetaḥ snigdhaḥ sthiraḥ sakaṇḍūḥ | Sannipātike sarvaliṅgam | Raktaje pittaliṅgaṃ kṛṣṇasrāvam | Āgantau yathāghātam || 1-4 ||
commentary: The wounds (vraṇa) are of six types based on vāta, pitta, kapha, sannipāta, rakta and āgantu. In vātika type, the wound is rough, blackish-red, rigid and with scanty discharge. In paittika type, it is yellow-red, with discharge and causes burning sensation and fever. In kaphaja type, it is white, unctuous, stable and with itching. In sannipātika type, all symptoms are present. In raktaja type, it has pitta-like symptoms with black discharge. In āgantu type, symptoms are as per the injury.

sanskrit_text: सुस्थाने तरुणे धीमति निरुपद्रवे नवे काले सुखसाध्यः । तद्विपरीते कृच्छ्रसाध्यः । सर्वविपरीते सोपद्रवे चासाध्यः ॥ ५-६ ॥
transliteration: Susthāne taruṇe dhīmati nirupadrave nave kāle sukhasādhyaḥ | Tadviparīte kṛcchrasādhyaḥ | Sarvaviparīte sopadrave cāsādhyaḥ || 5-6 ||
commentary: The wound occurring on a good place to a young and sensible individual without any complication, a fresh one and during congenial season is easily curable. Absence of any of the above criteria makes it difficult for cure. And the wound devoid of all the above qualities and associated with complication is just incurable.

sanskrit_text: पूतिः पूयातिदुष्टास्रस्राव्युत्सङ्गी चिरस्थितिः । दुष्टो व्रणोऽतिगन्धादिः शुद्धलिङ्गविपर्ययः ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Pūtiḥ pūyātiduṣṭāsrasrāvyutsaṅgī cirasthitiḥ | Duṣṭo vraṇo'tigandhādiḥ śuddhaliṅgaviparyayaḥ || 7 ||
commentary: Putrified, having abundant exudation of pus and vitiated blood, having sinuses, long standing, stinking etc., and having opposite qualities of healthy wound is called Duṣṭa vraṇa (putrified wound).

sanskrit_text: जिह्वतलाभोऽतिमृदुः श्लक्ष्णः स्निग्धोऽल्पवेदनः । सुव्यवस्थो निरास्रावः शुद्धो व्रण इति स्मृतः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration: Jihvatalābho'timṛduḥ ślakṣṇaḥ snigdho'lpavedanaḥ | Suvyavastho nirāsrāvaḥ śuddho vraṇa iti smṛtaḥ || 8 ||
commentary: Having the colour and lustre like those of the root of the tongue, very soft, fine, oily, less painful, well settled and no exudation are the features of Śuddha vraṇa (healthy wound).

sanskrit_text: अव्याधिरुह्यमाणे तु स्वभावाद्व्रणरोहणम् । पिच्छिलं बहलं नातिविवृतं कुरुते ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration: Avyādhiruhyamāṇe tu svabhāvādvraṇarohaṇam | Picchilaṃ bahalaṃ nātivivṛtaṃ kurute || 9 ||
commentary: In a healthy individual, the wound heals naturally. The healing wound becomes sticky, thick, and not too open.

sanskrit_text: कण्डूर्गुरुत्वं व्रणमार्गशोथः । पूयास्रस्रावो वेदना च । रूढवर्त्म सवर्णं समतलमग्रन्थि रूढं विद्यात् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration: Kaṇḍūrgurutvaṃ vraṇamārgaśothaḥ | Pūyāsrasrāvo vedanā ca | Rūḍhavartma savarṇaṃ samatalamagranthi rūḍhaṃ vidyāt || 10 ||
commentary: Itching, heaviness, swelling of the wound tract, discharge of pus and blood, and pain are the features during healing. The wound is considered properly healed when the scar is complete, equal in colour to the surrounding skin, level and without knots.

sanskrit_text: कुष्ठविषव्याधिप्रमेहिणां व्रणो याप्यः । व्रणान्तराणां दुःसाध्यः । वसामज्जमस्तिष्कस्रावी आगन्तुर्व्रणः साध्यः । प्राकृतश्चासाध्यः ॥ ११-१२ ॥
transliteration: Kuṣṭhaviṣavyādhipramehiṇāṃ vraṇo yāpyaḥ | Vraṇāntarāṇāṃ duḥsādhyaḥ | Vasāmajjamastiṣkasrāvī āganturvraṇaḥ sādhyaḥ | Prākṛtaścāsādhyaḥ || 11-12 ||
commentary: Vrana (wound) occurring to lepers, poison-stricken, emaciated and diabetics, and also as secondary to the patients already afflicted with Vrana can be managed with difficulty. When there is exudation of oily part, fat and also the brain-matter in wounds caused suddenly due to external stimuli, they are curable but if the same exudation exists in natural wounds caused by vitiated doṣas, they are incurable.

sanskrit_text: सुरागुरुघृतमालतीपद्मचन्दनचम्पकगन्धा दिव्यगन्धाश्च । मरणाय ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration: Surāgurughṛtamālatīpadmacandanacampakagandhā divyagandhāśca | Maraṇāya || 13 ||
commentary: There will be fragrance in the wounds like those of alcohol, aguru (Aquillaria agallocha), ghee, jasmine flowers, lotus, sandalwood and campaka (Fragrant yellow flowers) and divine fragrances which indicate nearing of the death of that particular individual.

sanskrit_text: शस्त्रप्रहारैर्नानाप्रकारैः शरीरावयवेषु नानाविधा व्रणा जायन्ते । ते च षड्विधाः - छिन्नो भिन्नो विद्धः क्षतः पिच्छितो घृष्टश्च ॥ १-२ ॥
transliteration: Śastraprahārairnānāprakāraiḥ śarīrāvayaveṣu nānāvidhā vraṇā jāyante | Te ca ṣaḍvidhāḥ - chhinnō bhinnō viddhaḥ kṣataḥ picchitō ghṛṣṭaśca || 1-2 ||
commentary: Due to blow of weapons of various edges and ends, wounds of various shape occur on various parts of the body. They are named as Chinna (cut), Bhinna (broken), Viddha (pierced), Kṣata (excised), Piccita (crushed) and Ghrṣṭa (bruised). Thus they are six in number.

sanskrit_text: तिर्यग्र्जु वा प्रहारात् छिन्नं पतति वा लम्बते वा । छिन्नव्रणः ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Tiryagrju vā prahārāt chhinnaṃ patati vā lambate vā | Chinnavraṇaḥ || 3 ||
commentary: The wound which is formed horizontally or vertically and wide in shape by which the particular limb is cut off completely or hangs after it is cut partially is called Chinna Vrana (cut wound).

sanskrit_text: तोमरदन्तशरासिफलाङ्कुशविषाणाभिघातात् स्रावी भिन्नव्रणः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Tomaradantaśarāsiphalāṅkuśaviṣāṇābhighātāt srāvī bhinnavraṇaḥ || 4 ||
commentary: On having been hit with a pointed weapon, tooth, arrow, end part of a sword or a horn, the wound which is formed, cuts open the particular viscera and is called Bhinna vrana (cut-open wound/punctured wound according to some) which will have some exudation.

sanskrit_text: आमाशयः पक्वाशयः क्षुद्रान्त्रं स्थूलान्त्रं मूत्राशयो रुधिराशयो हृदयमुण्डूकः फुफ्फुसश्चेति कोष्ठः । तत्र भिन्ने रक्ताकुलत्वं ज्वरदाहौ च । मूत्रपुरीषमुखनासिकाभ्यः रक्तं स्रवेत् । मूर्च्छाश्वासतृष्णानाहारोचकविण्मूत्रानिलसङ्गस्वेदाक्षिरागमुखलोहगन्धदेहदुर्गन्धहृन्नेत्रपार्श्वरुजाः । आमाशयगते रक्ते छर्दिरानाहो गुरुता च । अन्त्रगते तु रुक्गुरुत्वमधोभागशीतता च ॥ ५-१० ॥
transliteration: Āmāśayaḥ pakvāśayaḥ kṣudrāntraṃ sthūlāntraṃ mūtrāśayo rudhirāśayo hṛdayamuṇḍūkaḥ phuphphusaśceti koṣṭhaḥ | Tatra bhinne raktākulatvaṃ jvaradāhau ca | Mūtrapurīṣamukhanāsikābhyaḥ raktaṃ sravet | Mūrcchāśvāsatṛṣṇānāhārocakaviṇmūtrānilasaṅgasvedākṣirāgamukhalohagandhadehadurgandhahṛnnetrapārśvarujāḥ | Āmāśayagate rakte chardirānāho gurutā ca | Antragate tu rukgurutvamadhobhāgaśītatā ca || 5-10 ||
commentary: Āmāśaya (stomach), Agnyāśaya (duodenum), Pakvāśaya (intestines), Mūtrāśaya (urinary bladder), Rudhirāśaya (liver and spleen), Hṛt (heart), Uṇḍuka (caecum) and Phupphusa (lungs) - all these put together, are called koṣṭha. When there is a cut in the koṣṭha, it will be filled with blood. The individual suffers from fever and burning sensation. There will be bleeding through urethra, anus, mouth and nostrils. He also has syncope, dyspnoea, thirst, bloating of the abdomen, hatred towards food, blockage to stool, urine and fart, perspiration, redness of the eyes, iron-smell in the mouth, stinking of the body and pain in the heart and flanks. When the blood accumulates in the stomach there will be vomiting of blood accumulated in the stomach, heavy bloating and severe colic. When it is accumulated in the intestines, there will be pain, heaviness and especially the lower part of the body will become cold in touch.

sanskrit_text: शल्येन विद्धमुत्तुण्डितमनुत्तुण्डितं वा विद्धव्रणः ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration: Śalyena viddhamuttuṇḍitamanuttuṇḍitaṃ vā viddhavraṇaḥ || 11 ||
commentary: The wound which is pierced by a foreign body, whether the foreign body remains in the wound or comes out, is called Viddha vraṇa (pierced wound).

sanskrit_text: नातिच्छिन्नं नातिभिन्नं उभयलिङ्गं विषमं क्षतम् ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration: Nāticchinnaṃ nātibhinnaṃ ubhayaliṅgaṃ viṣamaṃ kṣatam || 12 ||
commentary: The wound that has neither too deeply nor too widely cut, but has the features of the both types and that causes irregularity to that particular limb is called 'kṣata vraṇa' (excised wound).

sanskrit_text: प्रहारपीडनाभ्यां पृथुतामुपगते मज्जरक्तस्रावी पिच्छितः ॥ १३ ॥
transliteration: Prahārapīḍanābhyāṃ pṛthutāmupagate majjaraktasrāvī picchitaḥ || 13 ||
commentary: When a limb becomes flattened due to blows or squeezing/pressing including bone (of that limb) and there is profuse oozing of majjā (bone-marrow) and raktā (blood), such an injury is called piccita vraṇa.

sanskrit_text: घर्षणप्रहाराभ्यां विकृतत्वचा सदाहस्रावा घृष्टः ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration: Gharṣaṇaprahārābhyāṃ vikṛtatvaca sadāhasrāvā ghṛṣṭaḥ || 14 ||
commentary: Due to friction or blow, when the injured part of the body is devoid of the skin and associated with burning sensation and oozing, such an wound is called ghrṣṭa vraṇa (bruised wound).

sanskrit_text: कृष्णः श्यावः सशोफः सर्षपिकाभिराचितः स्रावी मृदुर्मांसपिण्डैराचितः सशल्यव्रणः । शल्यं तु त्वचं भित्त्वा सिरादीन् परिहृत्य वा कोष्ठं गच्छति ॥ १५-१६ ॥
transliteration: Kṛṣṇaḥ śyāvaḥ saśophaḥ sarṣapikābhirācitaḥ srāvī mṛdurmāṃsapiṇḍairācitaḥ saśalyavraṇaḥ | Śalyaṃ tu tvacaṃ bhittvā sirādīn parihṛtya vā koṣṭhaṃ gacchati || 15-16 ||
commentary: When a wound is blackish in colour, associated with inflammation surrounded by small papules that ooze out blood repeatedly, soft in touch with high rising muscle tissue that looks like bubbles and is painful, is called Saśalya vraṇa, wound that is concealing the foreign body (which caused the wound). The foreign body that crosses the skin, either pierces through the veins etc., or tears them off and enters the alimentary canal, causes certain complications.

sanskrit_text: आन्तररुधिरे पाण्डौ शीताङ्गपादकरानने शीतनिश्वासे रक्ताक्षे सानाहे कोष्ठभेदं त्यजेत् ॥ १७ ॥
transliteration: Āntararudhire pāṇḍau śītāṅgapādakarānane śītaniḥśvāse raktākṣe sānāhe koṣṭhabhedaṃ tyajet || 17 ||
commentary: If the patient of Koṣṭhabheda is suffering from internal bleeding, pallor and cold touch in the legs, hands and face, cold breath, redness in the eyes and bloating of the abdomen, he should not be taken for treatment.

sanskrit_text: भ्रमः प्रलापः पतनं मोहश्चेष्टाविघातश्च । ग्लानिः स्रस्ताङ्गता मूर्च्छा चोर्ध्वगतिर्वायोः । तीव्रा च रुक् । मांससिरास्नाय्वस्थिसन्धिषु मर्मसु विकृतेषु मांसोदकप्रतीकाशः स्रावः सर्वेन्द्रियार्थोपरमश्च ॥ १८-१९ ॥
transliteration: Bhramaḥ pralāpaḥ patanaṃ mohaśceṣṭāvighātaśca | Glāniḥ srastāṅgatā mūrcchā cordhvagatirvāyoḥ | Tīvrā ca ruk | Māṃsasirāsnāyvasthisandhiṣu marmaṣu vikṛteṣu māṃsodakapratīkāśaḥ srāvaḥ sarvendriyārthoparamaśca || 18-19 ||
commentary: Giddiness, delirium, falling down, delusion, inaction or irregular action, fatigue, warmth, looseness of the body limbs, swooning, upward motion of Vāta, severe pain, other symptoms caused by vāta, exudation that looks like meat-washed water and all the senses stop working when there is injury in the five types of vital points.

sanskrit_text: सिराणां मर्मगतानामन्यत्र वा विद्धानां लिङ्गम् - यथा स्थानं रक्तस्रावः । मांसगते - पाण्डुता विवर्णता स्पर्शाज्ञता च ॥ २०-२४ ॥
transliteration: Sirāṇāṃ marmagatānāmanyatra vā viddhānāṃ liṅgam - yathā sthānaṃ raktasrāvaḥ | Māṃsagate - pāṇḍutā vivarṇatā sparśājñatā ca || 20-24 ||
commentary: The symptoms of injury to veins, whether on vital points or elsewhere, include bleeding according to the site. Injury to muscle tissue causes pallor, discolouration and loss of tactile perception.

sanskrit_text: सर्वेषां व्रणानां शोफरागदाहज्वरशूलतृष्णामोहाश्चोपद्रवाः ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration: Sarveṣāṃ vraṇānāṃ śopharāgadāhajvaraśūlatṛṣṇāmohāścopadravāḥ || 25 ||
commentary: Swelling, redness, burning sensation, fever, pain, thirst and delusion are the complications of all types of wounds.

sanskrit_text: भग्नं समासाद् द्विविधं हुताश! काण्डे च सन्धौ च हि तत्र सन्धौ । उत्पिष्टविश्लिष्टविवर्तितं च तिर्यग्गतं क्षिप्तमधश्च षट् च ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Bhagnaṃ samāsād dvividhaṃ hutāśa! kāṇḍe ca sandhau ca hi tatra sandhau | Utpiṣṭaviśliṣṭavivartitaṃ ca tiryaggataṃ kṣiptamadhaśca ṣaṭ ca || 1 ||
commentary: Hutāśa (Agniveśa)! fracture is of two types. The one that takes place in the shaft of the bone and the other in the joint. The fracture that takes place in the joint is of six types, viz, Utpiṣṭa (Fracture dislocation), Viślīṣṭa (Subluxation or incomplete dislocation), Vivartita (Lateral displacement), Tiryaggata (Complete dislocation), Kṣipta (Complicated dislocation) and Adhaḥkṣipta (Downward displacement).

sanskrit_text: प्रसारणाकुञ्चनवर्तनोग्रा रुक् स्पर्शासहत्वं विश्लेषणमेतदुक्तम् । सामान्यतः सन्धिगतस्य लिङ्गम् ॥ २ ॥ विशेषतो रात्रिभवा रुजा च विश्लिष्टजे तौ च रुजा च नित्यम् । विवर्तिते पार्श्वरुजश्च तीव्रास्तिर्यग्गते तीव्ररुजो भवन्ति ॥ ३ ॥ क्षिप्तेऽति शूलं विषमत्वमस्थ्नोः क्षिप्ते त्वधो रुग्विघटश्च सन्धेः ॥
transliteration: Prasāraṇākuñcanavartanogrā ruk sparśāsahatvaṃ viśleṣaṇametaduktam | Sāmānyataḥ sandhigatasya liṅgam || 2 || Viśeṣato rātribhavā rujā ca viśliṣṭaje tau ca rujā ca nityam | Vivartite pārśvarujaśca tīvrāstiryaggate tīvrarujo bhavanti || 3 || Kṣipte'ti śūlaṃ viṣamatvamasthnoḥ kṣipte tvadho rugvighaṭaśca sandheḥ ||
commentary: Severe pain on extension, flexion and rotation of the affected limb and not being able to bear the touch on that part are general symptoms of fracture of dislocation. In utpiṣṭā (fracture-dislocation) of the joint, there will be inflammation all over and pain during nights. In the case of viśliṣṭā (subluxation or incomplete dislocation) there will be continuous pain apart from above two symptoms. Vivartita (Lateral displacement) type of sandhibhagna is characterised by severe pain on sides of that particular joint. In Tiryaggata (complicated dislocation), there will be severe pain while in Adhaḥ kṣipta (downward displacement) there will be pain and the bone-ends are quite displaced.

sanskrit_text: कर्कटकाश्वकर्णविचूर्णितपिच्चितास्थिचल्लिकाकाण्डभग्नातिपातितमज्जगतस्फुटितवक्रच्छिन्नम् । द्विधा च्छिन्नं द्वादशधा प्रोक्तं काण्डे स्तब्धाङ्गता शोथरुगतिवृद्धिः ॥ ४-६ ॥
transliteration: Karkaṭakāśvakarṇavicūrṇitapiccitāsthicallikākāṇḍabhagnātipātitamajjagatasphuṭitavakracchinnam | Dvidhā cchinnaṃ dvādaśadhā proktaṃ kāṇḍe stabdhāṅgatā śotharugativṛddhiḥ || 4-6 ||
commentary: Karkaṭaka (sub-periosteal fracture), Aśvakarṇa (oblique fracture), Vicūrṇita (comminuted fracture), Piccita (complicated fracture), Asthicallika (Longitudinal fracture), Kāṇḍa bhagna (Transverse fracture), Atipātita (Multiple fracture), Majjagata (Impacted fracture), Sphuṭita (Fissured fracture), Vakra (Green-stick fracture) and Chinna (a type of fissured fracture) which is of two types; these twelve are the varieties of Kāṇḍa bhagna (breakage in the bone-shaft). Rigidity of the limbs, swelling, increased pain, crepitations at the broken point, not being able to bear the touch, pulsation, pinning sensation and not finding relief in any posture are the general symptomatology of Kāṇḍa bhagna.

sanskrit_text: भग्नान्यपि सन्ति बहूनि नामभिरेव तानि ज्ञेयानि ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Bhagnānyapi santi bahūni nāmabhireva tāni jñeyāni || 7 ||
commentary: There are many more varieties of fractures but all of them can be understood by the names given to those particular fractures.

sanskrit_text: वातात्मके जरसि बाले कृशे सोपद्रवे च भग्नं कृच्छ्रसाध्यम् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration: Vātātmake jarasi bāle kṛśe sopadrave ca bhagnaṃ kṛcchrasādhyam || 8 ||
commentary: Fractures in individuals with vāta temperament, in old age, children, emaciated persons and those with complications are difficult to cure.

sanskrit_text: भिन्नं कपालं कट्यां तु सन्धिमुक्तं तथा च्युतम् । जघनं प्रतिपिष्टं च वर्जयेद्धि विचक्षणः ॥ ९ ॥ असंश्लिष्टकपालं च ललाटे चूर्णितं च यत् । भग्नं स्तनान्तरे पृष्ठे शङ्खे मूर्ध्नि च वर्जयेत् ॥ १० ॥
transliteration: Bhinnaṃ kapālaṃ kaṭyāṃ tu sandhimuktaṃ tathā cyutam | Jaghanaṃ pratipiṣṭaṃ ca varjayeddhi vicakṣaṇaḥ || 9 || Asaṃśliṣṭakapālaṃ ca lalāṭe cūrṇitaṃ ca yat | Bhagnaṃ stanāntare pṛṣṭhe śaṅkhe mūrdhni ca varjayet || 10 ||
