commentary: When the fractures occur in the flat bone (of the skull), pelvic bone in the form of dislocation of the joint or downward displacement and dislocation of the joint are not to be treated. Dislocated fracture in the skull and multiple fracture on the fore-head and also fracture at the mediastinum, vertebra, temple bone and on the top of the fore-head are also to be discarded from treating.

sanskrit_text: संहितमपि दुर्निक्षेपनिबन्धनात् संक्षोभाद्वा विषमं भवति तदपि त्याज्यम् ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration: Saṃhitamapi durnikṣepanibandhanāt saṃkṣobhādvā viṣamaṃ bhavati tadapi tyājyam || 11 ||
commentary: Inspite of proper placing of the bone, if it is bandaged displacing it or by shaking or disturbing, that goes irregular. Such condition is also to be left without treating (since such condition is incurable).

sanskrit_text: तरुणानि नमन्ति, नलकानि भिद्यन्ते, कपालानि विभज्यन्ते, रुचकानि चूर्णयन्ति ॥ १२ ॥
transliteration: Taruṇāni namanti, nalakāni bhidyante, kapālāni vibhajyante, rucakāni cūrṇayanti || 12 ||
commentary: The cartilages bend, the long bones break, the flat bones separate or show cracks and the teeth break up into pieces on getting injured.

sanskrit_text: अज्ञो वैद्यः पक्वमपि पूयं सम्यगपनयेत् । तत् पूयं कोष्ठे प्रविश्य नाडीव्रणं करोति ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Ajño vaidyaḥ pakvamapi pūyaṃ samyagapanayet | Tat pūyaṃ koṣṭhe praviśya nāḍīvraṇaṃ karoti || 1 ||
commentary: If an ignorant physician neglects without treating, with a misunderstanding that it is still unripe or if he does not take up proper steps to completely drain the excessive pus from a ripened wound, then the pus enters forcibly inside the body, infecting the parts mentioned previously, leading to a sinus wound.

sanskrit_text: नाडीव्रणं नाम दीर्घमार्गं सुषिरमिव । तत् पञ्चविधं वातपित्तकफसन्निपातशल्यनिमित्तैः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Nāḍīvraṇaṃ nāma dīrghamārgaṃ suṣiramiva | Tat pañcavidhaṃ vātapittakaphasannipātaśalyanimittaiḥ || 2 ||
commentary: Nāḍī vraṇa (like a tubular path-way) means like a longitudinal hollow tube. The sinus wound is of five types by origination i.e., 3 due to one each of three doṣas, one due to all three of them together and other one due to foreign-body.

sanskrit_text: वातिके रूक्षे विवृते च स्तोकस्रावः फेनिलो रात्रौ । पैत्तिके पीतः सोष्मा दिवा च । कफजे श्वेतो घनः पिच्छिलः ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Vātike rūkṣe vivṛte ca stokasrāvaḥ phenilo rātrau | Paittike pītaḥ soṣmā divā ca | Kaphaje śveto ghanaḥ picchilaḥ || 3 ||
commentary: Vāta type of Nāḍīvraṇa is rough in touch, has narrow opening, painful and exudates froathy secretion more during nights. Pittaja type is associated with thirst, fever and burning sensation; the exudation is very warm and yellow in colour and also more during day time. Kaphaja type has exudation which is excessive, thick white in colour and sticky in nature.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपातिके सर्वलिङ्गं दाहज्वरश्वासमूर्च्छामुखशोषैर्युक्तं कालरात्रिसमम् ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Sannipātike sarvaliṅgaṃ dāhajvaraśvāsamūrcchāmukhaśoṣairyuktaṃ kālarātrisamam || 4 ||
commentary: Apart from the individual symptoms of all the three doṣas, there will be more burning sensation, fever, dyspnoea, swooning and dryness of the mouth in the Tridoṣaja type of Nāḍī vraṇa which is serious and causes death like a Kālarātri (the sister of death-god).

sanskrit_text: शल्यनिमित्ते सद्यः स्रावो रक्तमिश्र उष्णः फेनिलो मथितनिभः सरुक् च ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration: Śalyanimitte sadyaḥ srāvo raktamiśra uṣṇaḥ phenilo mathitanibhaḥ saruk ca || 5 ||
commentary: The foreign body that enters by any means into one of the eight locations of vraṇa and gets concealed in the place, makes way causing sinus wound in a short period. There is sudden exudation from such wound mixed with blood, warm and which is like churned curds in consistency and that wound is always associated with pain.

sanskrit_text: त्रिदोषजमसाध्यं शेषाश्चतस्रः साध्याः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Tridoṣajamasādhyaṃ śeṣāścatasraḥ sādhyāḥ || 6 ||
commentary: The tridoṣa type of sinus wound is incurable while the remaining four are curable when proper steps are taken.

sanskrit_text: गुदस्य द्व्यङ्गुले क्षेत्रे पार्श्वतः पिडका कृतकृत् । भिन्ना भगन्दरो ज्ञेयः स च पञ्चविधो मतः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Gudasya dvyaṅgule kṣetre pārśvataḥ piḍakā kṛtakṛt | Bhinnā bhagandaro jñeyaḥ sa ca pañcavidho mataḥ || 1 ||
commentary: When the painful blister that occurs within a distance of two inches surrounding the anus gets burst, it is to be known as Bhagandara. This is of five types.

sanskrit_text: कषायरूक्षैर्विकोपितोऽनिलस्त्वपानदेशे पिडकां करोति याम् । उपेक्षणात् पाकमुपैति दारुणं रुजा च भिन्नाऽरुणफेनवाहिनी ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Kaṣāyarūkṣairvikopito'nilastvapānadeśe piḍakāṃ karoti yām | Upekṣaṇāt pākamupaiti dāruṇaṃ rujā ca bhinnā'ruṇaphenavāhinī || 2 ||
commentary: By indulging in the use of Kaṣāya (astringent), Rūkṣa (rough) foods, the highly aggravated vāta causes blisters in the anus region which by neglecting, get ripened with severe pain and when they break-open, there is reddish froathy exudation. From those many wounds, urine, faeces and semen ooze out. This disease condition is called Shataponaka (the sieve).

sanskrit_text: पित्तेन रक्तमिश्रेण पिडका शीघ्रपाकिनी । कृच्छ्रभेदा सरक्तस्रावा कषाया च । उष्ट्रग्रीवा सा भगन्दरः ॥ ३-४ ॥
transliteration: Pittena raktamiśreṇa piḍakā śīghrapākinī | Kṛcchrabhedā saraktasrāvā kaṣāyā ca | Uṣṭragrīvā sā bhagandaraḥ || 3-4 ||
commentary: The blister caused by pitta mixed with rakta ripens quickly, has difficulty in opening, discharges blood and is astringent. This type of fistula is called Uṣṭragrīva (camel's neck).

sanskrit_text: श्लेष्मणा पिडका कण्डूमती घनस्रावा कठिना मन्दरुक् श्वेता च । परिस्रावी सा भगन्दरः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration: Śleṣmaṇā piḍakā kaṇḍūmatī ghanasrāvā kaṭhinā mandaruk śvetā ca | Parisrāvī sā bhagandaraḥ || 5 ||
commentary: The blister of kaphaja type of Bhagandara is associated with pruritus, thick exudation, hardness in touch, mild pain and whitish in colour. This is called Parisrāvī (the ever oozing).

sanskrit_text: सन्निपातेन पिडका नानावर्णरुजास्रावा । शम्बूकावर्तनिभा सा भगन्दरः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Sannipātena piḍakā nānāvarṇarujāsrāvā | Śambūkāvartanibhā sā bhagandaraḥ || 6 ||
commentary: The blister with exudation of multicolours and pain, looks like an udder of a cow and has the sinus that is formed in the shape of the inner structure of a snail-shell or a whirl-pool, is called Śambūkāvarta.

sanskrit_text: शल्येन गुदे नाडी कृमिभिरुपेक्षया वर्धिता नानामार्गान् गच्छति । सोन्मार्गी भगन्दरः ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Śalyena gude nāḍī kṛmibhirupekṣayā vardhitā nānāmārgān gacchati | Sonmārgī bhagandaraḥ || 7 ||
commentary: When a sinus is formed in the anus due to injury caused by a foreign-body and grows due to infection caused by worms (bacteria) because of negligence, it takes various passages causing a number of wound/openings which is called Unmārgi bhagandara.

sanskrit_text: शेषाश्चत्वारः साध्याः सन्निपातजश्चासाध्यः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration: Śeṣāścatvāraḥ sādhyāḥ sannipātajaścāsādhyaḥ || 8 ||
commentary: The remaining four types are curable, while the sannipātaja type is incurable.

sanskrit_text: अन्नमूत्रपुरीषकृमिशुक्राणि यस्य स्रवन्ति स म्रियते ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration: Annamūtrapurīṣakṛmiśukrāṇi yasya sravanti sa mriyate || 9 ||
commentary: If the fart, urine, faeces, worms and semen exude out from the fistula, such condition will kill that particular individual.

sanskrit_text: हस्तनखदन्ताघातादशौचात् रतिसेवनात् योनिरोगाच्चोपदंसः पञ्चविधः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Hastanakhadantāghātādaśaucāt ratisevanāt yonirogāccopadaṃsaḥ pañcavidhaḥ || 1 ||
commentary: There arise five types of syphilitic ulcers on the penis due to injury with hands, piercing with nails, biting with teeth, not cleaning it or over indulgence in sexual intercourse and also due to the vitiation/disease of the vagina where the sexual act is performed and many other bad deeds.

sanskrit_text: वातिके रूक्षः कृष्णः स्तब्धः सरुक् । पैत्तिके पीतः स्रावी दाहज्वरयुतः । कफजे श्वेतः स्निग्धः स्थिरः सकण्डूः । सन्निपातिके सर्वलिङ्गम् । रक्तजे पित्तलिङ्गं कृष्णस्रावम् ॥ २-४ ॥
transliteration: Vātike rūkṣaḥ kṛṣṇaḥ stabdhaḥ saruk | Paittike pītaḥ srāvī dāhajvarayutaḥ | Kaphaje śvetaḥ snigdhaḥ sthiraḥ sakaṇḍūḥ | Sannipātike sarvaliṅgam | Raktaje pittaliṅgaṃ kṛṣṇasrāvam || 2-4 ||
commentary: In vātika type, the ulcer is rough, black, rigid and painful. In paittika type, it is yellow, with discharge, burning sensation and fever. In kaphaja type, it is white, unctuous, stable and with itching. In sannipātika type, all symptoms are present. In raktaja type, it has pitta-like symptoms with black discharge.

sanskrit_text: अज्ञो य उपदंसमुपेक्षते रतिप्रसक्तः । शोफकृमिदाहपाकैः शिश्नमांसक्षयेण म्रियते ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration: Ajño ya upadaṃsamupekṣate ratiprasaktaḥ | Śophakṛmidāhapākaiḥ śiśnamāṃsakṣayeṇa mriyate || 5 ||
commentary: If an unwise individual does not take immediate treatment on the onset of upadamsa and continues to indulge in sexual activity, he will be affected by inflammation, worm-infestation, burning sensation and ripening and his penile musculature gets withered due to which he meets his end.

sanskrit_text: अक्रमेण शिश्नवृद्धिकामस्य शुकदोषा अष्टादश भवन्ति ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Akrameṇa śiśnavṛddhikāmasya śukadoṣā aṣṭādaśa bhavanti || 1 ||
commentary: When an unwise individual wishes to have his male organ to be grown unnaturally (and adopts application/unguentums to improve its size), he is afflicted by eighteen types of disease caused by such applications.

sanskrit_text: सर्षपिका अश्विलिका अलजी पुष्करिका स्पर्शहानिरुत्तमा शतपोणकाऽर्बुदं मांसार्बुदं मांसपाको विद्रधिः । तिलकालकश्च ॥ २-११ ॥
transliteration: Sarṣapikā aśvilikā alajī puṣkarikā sparśahāniruttamā śatapoṇakā'rbudaṃ māṃsārbudaṃ māṃsapāko vidradhiḥ | Tilakālakaśca || 2-11 ||
commentary: The eighteen types of Śūkadoṣa are: Sarṣapikā, Aśvilikā, Alajī, Puṣkarikā, Sparśahāni, Uttamā, Śatapoṇakā, Arbuda, Māṃsārbuda, Māṃsapāka, Vidradhi, and Tilakālaka.

sanskrit_text: कट्वम्ललवणक्षारविरुद्धाध्यशनाशनैः । दुष्टनिष्पावशाकाद्यैः प्रदुष्टपवनोदकैः ॥ १ ॥ क्रूरग्रहेक्षणाच्चापदेशे दोषाः समुद्धताः । जनयन्ति शरीरेऽस्मिन्दुष्टरक्तेन सङ्गताः ॥ २ ॥ मसूराकृतिसंस्थानाः पिडकाः स्युर्मसूरिकाः ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Kaṭvamlalavaṇakṣāraviruddhādhy aśanāśanaiḥ | Duṣṭaniṣpāvaśākādyaiḥ praduṣṭapavanodakaiḥ || 1 || Krūragrahekṣaṇāccāpadeśe doṣāḥ samuddhatāḥ | Janayanti śarīre'sminduṣṭaraktena saṅgatāḥ || 2 || Masūrākṛtisaṃsthānāḥ piḍakāḥ syurmasūrikāḥ || 3 ||
commentary: Due to consumption of foods that are pungent, sour, salty, alkali in nature, incompatible combinations, eating prior to digestion of previous food, putrified food, lentils, green leaves; drinking of contaminated water; exposure to contaminated air and also due to incompatible zodiac constellation, the doṣas aggravate, get into contact with blood which is already vitiated and cause vesicles of masūra (lathyrus sativa) size and shape which are called masūrikā.

sanskrit_text: सप्त महाकुष्ठानि - वातपित्तकफसन्निपातद्वन्द्वजानि । कपालमौदुम्बरमण्डलरूक्षजिह्वपुण्डरीकसिध्मकाकणन्तिकानि ॥ ४-७ ॥
transliteration: Sapta mahākuṣṭhāni - vātapittakaphasannipātadvandvajāni | Kapāla maudumbaramaṇḍalarūkṣajihvapuṇḍarīkasidhmakākaṇantikāni || 4-7 ||
commentary: The seven Mahākuṣṭhas are: Kapāla, Audumbara, Maṇḍala, Rūkṣajihva, Puṇḍarīka, Sidhma, and Kākaṇantikā. These are caused by vāta, pitta, kapha, sannipāta and their combinations.

sanskrit_text: अतिश्लक्ष्णत्वं खरत्वमतिस्वेदोऽस्वेदो वैवर्ण्यं दाहः कण्डूः सुप्तिस्तोदः कोठोन्नतिश्च कुष्ठपूर्वरूपाणि । भ्रमोऽरतिः सदनं च त्वग्दोषाः ॥ ८-९ ॥
transliteration: Atiślakṣṇatvaṃ kharatvamatisvedo'svedo vaivarṇyaṃ dāhaḥ kaṇḍūḥ suptistodaḥ koṭhonnatiśca kuṣṭhapūrvarūpāṇi | Bhramo'ratiḥ sadanaṃ ca tvagdoṣāḥ || 8-9 ||
commentary: Skin becoming very smooth or rough, over sweating or no sweat at all, discolouration, burning sensation and itching, loss of sensation, pinning sensation, occurrence of many patches on the skin, giddiness, painful and sudden ulceration on the skin that don't heal quickly, roughness even after healing, aggravation of the same even due to simple aetiology, horripilation and blackening of the blood are the premonitory symptoms of kuṣṭha.

sanskrit_text: कपाले कृष्णारुणं कपालसदृशं रूक्षं स्तब्धं तनु विषमम् । औदुम्बरे सदाहरागं रोमाञ्चितमौदुम्बरसदृशम् । मण्डले श्वेतं स्थिरं महत् स्निग्धं उत्सन्नमण्डलम् । रूक्षजिह्वे कठिनं नीलमध्यं रक्तान्तं मृगजिह्वासदृशम् । पुण्डरीके श्वेतं रक्तान्तं पद्मपत्रसदृशम् । सिध्मे श्वेतं ताम्रं तनुं चूर्णोत्सर्गि । काकणन्तिके काकणन्तिकासदृशं त्रिदोषलिङ्गम् ॥ १०-१६ ॥
transliteration: Kapāle kṛṣṇāruṇaṃ kapālasadṛśaṃ rūkṣaṃ stabdhaṃ tanu viṣamam | Audumbare sadāharāgaṃ romāñcitamaudumbarasadṛśam | Maṇḍale śvetaṃ sthiraṃ mahat snigdhaṃ utsannamaṇḍalam | Rūkṣajihve kaṭhinaṃ nīlamadhyaṃ raktāntaṃ mṛgajihvāsadṛśam | Puṇḍarīke śvetaṃ raktāntaṃ padmapatrasadṛśam | Sidhme śvetaṃ tāmraṃ tanuṃ cūrṇotsargi | Kākaṇantike kākaṇantikāsadṛśaṃ tridoṣaliṅgam || 10-16 ||
commentary: Kapāla - blackish-red, dry, rough, thin and irregular. Audumbara - with burning sensation, redness, hairy, like a fig fruit. Maṇḍala - white, stable, large, unctuous and elevated patches. Rūkṣajihva - hard, blue in centre, red at edges, like a deer's tongue. Puṇḍarīka - white centre with red edges, like a lotus petal. Sidhma - white, coppery, thin and scaly. Kākaṇantikā - like the seed of Abrus precatorius, with features of all three doṣas.

sanskrit_text: एककुष्ठं चर्मकुष्ठं किटिभं विपादिका अलसकं दद्रुमण्डलं चर्मदलं पामा कच्छू विस्फोटः शतारु विचर्चिका च ॥ १७-२२ ॥
transliteration: Ekakuṣṭhaṃ carmakuṣṭhaṃ kiṭibhaṃ vipādikā alasakaṃ dadrumaṇḍalaṃ carmadalaṃ pāmā kacchū visphoṭaḥ śatāru vicarcikā ca || 17-22 ||
commentary: The eleven Kṣudra Kuṣṭhas are: Ekakuṣṭha, Carmakuṣṭha, Kiṭibha, Vipādikā, Alasaka, Dadrumaṇḍala, Carmadala, Pāmā, Kacchū, Visphoṭa, Śatāru, and Vicarcikā.

sanskrit_text: खरं श्यावारुणं रूक्षं वातात्कुष्ठं सवेदनम् । पित्तात्प्रकथितं दाहरागस्रावान्वितम् । कफात्क्लेदि घनं स्निग्धं सकण्डूति गौरवम् ॥ २३-२४ ॥
transliteration: Kharaṃ śyāvāruṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ vātātkuṣṭhaṃ savedanam | Pittātprakathitaṃ dāharāgasrāvānvitam | Kaphātkledi ghanaṃ snigdhaṃ sakaṇḍūti gauravam || 23-24 ||
commentary: In vāta predominant kuṣṭha - hard, blackish-red, dry and painful. In pitta predominant - inflamed, with burning sensation, redness and discharge. In kapha predominant - moist, solid, unctuous, with itching and heaviness.

sanskrit_text: त्वक्स्थे वैवर्ण्यमङ्गेषु कुष्ठे रौक्ष्यं च जायते । त्वक्स्वापो रोमहर्षश्च स्वेदस्यातिप्रवर्तनम् । कण्डूर्विपूयकश्चैव कुष्ठे शोणितसंश्रिते ॥ २५-२६ ॥ बाहुल्यं वक्त्रशोषश्च कार्केश्यं पिडकोद्गमः । तोदः स्फोटः स्थिरत्वं च कुष्ठे मांसमाश्रिते ॥ २७ ॥ कौण्यं गतिक्षयोऽङ्गानां संभेदः क्षतसर्पणम् । मेदःस्थानगते लिङ्गं प्रागुक्तानि तथैव च ॥ २८ ॥ नासाभङ्गोऽक्षिगाश्च क्षतेषु क्रिमिसंभवः । स्वरोपघातश्च भवेदस्थिमज्जसमाश्रिते ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration: Tvaksthe vaivarṇyamaṅgeṣu kuṣṭhe raukṣyaṃ ca jāyate | Tvaksvāpo romaharṣaśca svedasyātipravartanam | Kaṇḍūrvipūyakaścaiva kuṣṭhe śoṇitasaṃśrite || 25-26 || Bāhulyaṃ vaktraśoṣaśca kārkeśyaṃ piḍakodgamaḥ | Todaḥ sphoṭaḥ sthiratvaṃ ca kuṣṭhe māṃsamāśrite || 27 || Kauṇyaṃ gatikṣayo'ṅgānāṃ saṃbhedaḥ kṣatasarpaṇam | Medaḥsthānagate liṅgaṃ prāguktāni tathaiva ca || 28 || Nāsābhaṅgo'kṣigāśca kṣateṣu krimisambhavaḥ | Svaropaghātaśca bhavedasthimajjasamāśrite || 29 ||
commentary: When kuṣṭha is in skin - discolouration and dryness. In blood - itching and pus formation. In muscle - multiple lesions, dryness of mouth, roughness, papules, pain, fissures and stability. In fat - deformity, loss of movement, breaking pain and spreading of wounds. In bone and marrow - nasal deformity, eye discharge, worm infestation and voice disturbance.

sanskrit_text: दम्पत्योः कुष्ठबाहुल्याद् दुष्टशोणितशुक्रयोः । यदपत्यं तयोर्जातं ज्ञेयं तदपि कुष्ठितम् ॥ ३० ॥
transliteration: Dampatyoḥ kuṣṭhabāhulyād duṣṭaśoṇitaśukrayoḥ | Yadapatyaṃ tayorjātaṃ jñeyaṃ tadapi kuṣṭhitam || 30 ||
commentary: When the Śukra and Śoṇita of kuṣṭha afflicted woman and man are vitiated by the disease, the off-spring, resulted by the conjugation of these two will also be affected by this disease and it is called 'kuṣṭhitam'.

sanskrit_text: कृच्छ्रसाध्यानि सर्वाणि कुष्ठानि । नवानि बलिनामनुपद्रवाणि सुखसाध्यानि । कालातीतानि विरुद्धाहारिणां व्याधितानां चासाध्यानि ॥ ३१-३२ ॥
transliteration: Kṛcchrasādhyāni sarvāṇi kuṣṭhāni | Navāni balināmanupadravāṇi sukhasādhyāni | Kālātītāni viruddhāhāriṇāṃ vyādhitānāṃ cāsādhyāni || 31-32 ||
commentary: All kuṣṭhas are difficult to cure. New ones in strong individuals without complications are easily curable. Chronic ones, in those who consume incompatible foods and are afflicted with other diseases, are incurable.

sanskrit_text: कपालौदुम्बरमण्डलानि वातकफजानि । सिध्मरूक्षजिह्वे वातपित्तजे । दद्रुशतारुविस्फोटपामाचर्मदलानि कफपित्तजानि । काकणन्तिका त्रिदोषजा ॥ ३३-३६ ॥
transliteration: Kapālaudumbaramaṇḍalāni vātakaphajāni | Sidhmarūkṣajihve vātapittaje | Dadruśatāruvisphoṭapāmācarmadalāni kaphapittajāni | Kākaṇantikā tridoṣajā || 33-36 ||
commentary: Kapāla, Audumbara and Maṇḍala are caused by vāta-kapha. Sidhma and Rūkṣajihva are caused by vāta-pitta. Dadru, Śatāru, Visphoṭa, Pāmā and Carmadala are caused by kapha-pitta. Kākaṇantikā is caused by all three doṣas.

sanskrit_text: कुष्ठैकसम्भवं श्वित्रं किलासं वारुणं भवेत् । निर्दिष्टमपिस्रावि त्रिधातूद्भवसंश्रयम् ॥ ३७ ॥ वाताद्रूक्षारुणं पित्तात्ताम्रं कमलपत्रवत् । सदाहं रोमहीनं च कफाच्छ्वेतं घनं गुरु ॥ ३८ ॥ सकण्डुरं क्रमाद्रक्तमांसमेदःसु चादिशेत् । वर्णेनैवद्रुणोभयं कृच्छ्रं तच्चोत्तरोत्तरम् ॥ ३९ ॥
transliteration: Kuṣṭhaikasambhavaṃ śvitraṃ kilāsaṃ vāruṇaṃ bhavet | Nirdiṣṭamapisrāvi tridhātodbhavasaṃśrayam || 37 || Vātādrūkṣāruṇaṃ pittāttāmraṃ kamalapatravat | Sadāhaṃ romahīnaṃ ca kaphācchetaṃ ghanaṃ guru || 38 || Sakaṇḍuraṃ kramādraktamāṃsamedaḥsu cādiśet | Varṇenaivadruṇobhayaṃ kṛcchraṃ taccottarottaram || 39 ||
commentary: Śvitra (Leucoderma) has similar aetiology to kuṣṭha. It is of three types based on doṣa and dhātu. Vāta type - dry and red. Pitta type - coppery like lotus leaf, with burning sensation and hair loss. Kapha type - white, solid, heavy and with itching. Seated in rakta, māmsa and medas respectively, it becomes progressively difficult to cure.

sanskrit_text: अशुक्लरोमाबहुलमसंश्लिष्टमनग्निदग्धं नवं श्वित्रं साध्यम् । अतोऽन्यत् त्याज्यम् । गुह्यतलकरपादौष्ठेषु नवमपि वर्जयेत् ॥ ४०-४१ ॥
transliteration: Aśuklaromābahulama saṃśliṣṭamanagnidagdhaṃ navaṃ śvitraṃ sādhyam | Ato'nyat tyājyam | Guhyatalakarapādauṣṭheṣu navamapi varjayet || 40-41 ||
commentary: Śvitra (Leucoderma) is curable when the hair on the affected area does not turn white, when the patches are not thick (big), not connected to each other, newly originated and not caused by burning due to contact with fire. Otherwise it is to be discarded from treating. It should not also be taken for treatment when it affects genitals, palms, soles and lips even on recent manifestation, if one wants success.

sanskrit_text: संस्पर्शनिश्वाससहभोजनशय्यासनवस्त्रभूषणात् कुष्ठज्वरशोषनेत्रामयाः सङ्क्रामन्ति ॥ ४२-४३ ॥
transliteration: Saṃsparśaniḥśvāsasahabhojanaśayyāsanavastrabhūṣaṇāt kuṣṭhajvaraśoṣanetrāmayāḥ saṅkrāmanti || 42-43 ||
commentary: Due to specific contact (coitus), bodily touch, respiration, sharing food, sharing bed and sharing the used garments and ornaments - kuṣṭha (skin-disease), jvara (fever), śoṣa (emaciation), netrābhisyanda (conjunctivitis) and other contagious diseases spread from one individual to another individual.

sanskrit_text: शीतवातातिसंस्पर्शात् कफवातौ प्रकुपितौ पित्तेन सह बहिरन्तर्विसर्पतः । सीतपित्तमुदर्दं च जनयतः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Śītavātātisaṃsparśāt kaphavātau prakupitau pittena saha bahirantarvisar pataḥ | Sītapittamudardaṃ ca janayataḥ || 1 ||
commentary: Due to continuous contact of cold winds, the kapha and vāyu get vitiated in the body and in association with pitta, spread inside and outside the body, causing Sītapitta and Udarda.

sanskrit_text: तृष्णारुचिछर्दिगात्रसदनगुरुत्वाक्षिरागाः पूर्वरूपाणि ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Tṛṣṇārucichardigātrasadanagurutvākṣirāgāḥ pūrvarūpāṇi || 2 ||
commentary: Thirst, distaste, nausea, tiredness of the body, heaviness in the limbs and redness in the eyes are the premonitory symptoms of the above diseases.

sanskrit_text: वराटककीटदष्टवदुत्सेधः कण्डूतोदच्छर्दिज्वरदाहयुतः । उदर्दः । स एव सीतपित्तम् ॥ ३-४ ॥
transliteration: Varāṭakakīṭadaṣṭavadutsedhaḥ kaṇḍūtodacchardijvaradāhayutaḥ | Udardaḥ | Sa eva sītapittam || 3-4 ||
commentary: The patches look like those caused by sting of the wasp; there will be upward inflammation associated with itching, pinning sensation, vomiting, fever and burning sensation in udarda. The other one (with same features) is called Sītapitta. Sītapitta is vāta dominated while udarda is of kapha predominance.

sanskrit_text: शैशिर उत्सन्नरागः कण्डूमानुदर्दः ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration: Śaiśira utsannarāgaḥ kaṇḍūmānudardaḥ || 5 ||
commentary: The kapha dominant disease occurring in śiśira ṛtu (winter), characterised by urticarial patches that are elevated, reddish in colour and associated with itching sensation is called udarda.

sanskrit_text: असंयग्वमनात् पित्तश्लेष्मान्नवेगावरोधाच्च कण्डूरागयुक्ताः पिडका बहुलाः कोठः । स एव पुनः पुनरुत्कोठः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Asaṃyagvamanāt pittaśleṣmānnavegāvarodhācca kaṇḍūrāgayuktāḥ piḍakā bahulāḥ koṭhaḥ | Sa eva punaḥ punarutkoṭhaḥ || 6 ||
commentary: Due to incomplete or improper emesis and also by suppressing the vomiting of pitta, śleṣma and food stuff, there arise plenty of patches with itching and redness in colour which is called koṭha. The same, if occurs repeatedly, is called utkoṭha.

sanskrit_text: विरुद्धदुष्टविदाह्यम्लपित्तप्रकोपणैश्च भोजनपानैः । संचितं पित्तमम्लपित्तमिति ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Viruddhaduṣṭavidāhyamlapittaprakopaṇaiśca bhojanapānaiḥ | Saṃcitaṃ pittamamlapittamiti || 1 ||
commentary: The pitta which has already accumulated in the body gets further aggravated by consuming incompatible food-combinations, putrified foods, sour foods, over burnt (that cause over burning sensation) foods and pitta-aggravating foods and drinks and is called amlapitta.

sanskrit_text: अविपाकः क्लमश्छर्दिरम्लकटुकोद्गारौ गुरुता च । हृदयकण्ठदाहोऽरुचिरिति लक्षणम् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Avipākaḥ klamaśchardiramlakaṭukodgārau gurutā ca | Hṛdayakaṇṭhadāho'ruciriti lakṣaṇam || 2 ||
commentary: Indigestion, fatigue, nausea, bitter and sour belching, heaviness of the body, burning sensation in the heart and throat and anorexia/distaste are to be pronounced by the physician as the feature of Amlapitta.

sanskrit_text: तृष्णादाहमूर्च्छाभ्रममोहयुक्तमधो वा प्रयाति । कदाचिद्विविधप्रकारं त्वग्दोषजाड्यमल्पाग्नित्वं रोमहर्षस्वेदपीतत्वानि च ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Tṛṣṇādāhamūrcchābhramamohayuktamadho vā prayāti | Kadācidvividhaprakāraṃ tvagdoṣajāḍyamalpāgnitvaṃ romaharṣasvedapītatvāni ca || 3 ||
commentary: Associated with thirst, burning sensation, syncope, giddiness and delusion, it (Amlapitta) comes downwardly or otherwise with various types (colours and odours). There will be occasional manifestation of allergic patches on the skin, dullness of the digestive fire, horripilation, over sweating of the body and yellowish colour of the skin.

sanskrit_text: हरितपीतनीलकृष्णरक्ताभं छर्दयति । मांसधोवननिभमतिपिच्छिलं कफमिश्रम् । कट्वम्ललवणं कदाचित् । अन्नस्यापाके शून्ये वा छर्दयति । अम्लकटूद्गारान् मुञ्चति । शिरोरुक्करम् । करपाददाहं कायोष्मारुचिज्वरान् करोति । कण्डूकोठबहुपिडकाजाड्यान्यरुचिच्छर्द्यादींश्च रोगान् जनयति ॥ ४-६ ॥
transliteration: Haritapītanīlakṛṣṇaraktābhaṃ chardayati | Māṃsadhovananibhamatipicchilaṃ kaphamiśram | Kaṭvamlalavaṇaṃ kadācit | Annasyāpāke śūnye vā chardayati | Amlakaṭūdgārān muñcati | Śirorukkaram | Karapādadāhaṃ kāyoṣmārucijvarān karoti | Kaṇḍūkoṭabahupiḍakājāḍyānyarucichardyādīṃśca rogān janayati || 4-6 ||
commentary: In the kapha associated amlapitta the vomitus is green, yellow, blue, black, light or dark red in colour, very sour in taste, the stuff looks like meat-washed water, very sticky, mixed with phlegm, some times salty, pungent and bitter in taste. On irregular digestion of food or even on empty stomach also, the patient vomits bitter and sour stuff; he belches with these tastes. He has associated symptoms like head ache. This kapha-associated amlapitta causes burning sensation in hands and feet, warmth in the body, distaste and fever. The body of the patient has itching, patches, innumerable vesicles and also indigestion, nausea etc., many other diseases.

sanskrit_text: रोगोऽयमम्लपित्ताख्यो यत्नात् संसाध्यते नवः । चिरोत्थितो भवेद्याप्यः कृच्छ्रसाध्यः स कस्यचित् ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Rogo'yamamlapittākhyo yatnāt saṃsādhyate navaḥ | Cirotthito bhavedyāpyaḥ kṛcchrasādhyaḥ sa kasyacit || 7 ||
commentary: This disease, called as Amlapitta is curable when it is of recent onset. The chronic one is prolongable and some times curable with difficulty.

sanskrit_text: लवणाम्लकटूष्णानां नित्यं सेवनात् । दोषाः कुपिता विसर्पं कुर्वन्ति । स च सप्तविधः । पृथग्वातपित्तकफैः सर्वैश्च द्वन्द्वैश्च ॥ १-३ ॥
transliteration: Lavaṇāmlakaṭūṣṇānāṃ nityaṃ sevanāt | Doṣāḥ kupitā visarpaṃ kurvanti | Sa ca saptavidhaḥ | Pṛthagvātapittakaphaiḥ sarvaiśca dvandvaiśca || 1-3 ||
commentary: Due to continuous consumption of foods of salty, sour and pungent tastes, and foods that are hot (in quality and potency), the doṣas aggravate and cause visarpa which is of seven types. 3 due to each of three doṣas, 1 due to the combination of all three doṣas and 3 due to dual combination of three doṣas.

sanskrit_text: वातिके चलं रूक्षं कृष्णारुणं सरुजम् । पैत्तिके पीतं सदाहं सरुजम् । कफजे श्वेतं स्निग्धं स्थिरं सकण्डूम् । सन्निपातिके सर्वलिङ्गम् ॥ ४-७ ॥
transliteration: Vātike calaṃ rūkṣaṃ kṛṣṇāruṇaṃ sarujam | Paittike pītaṃ sadāhaṃ sarujam | Kaphaje śvetaṃ snigdhaṃ sthiraṃ sakaṇḍūm | Sannipātike sarvaliṅgam || 4-7 ||
commentary: In vātika visarpa, it is mobile, rough, blackish-red and painful. In paittika, it is yellow, with burning sensation and pain. In kaphaja, it is white, unctuous, stable and with itching. In sannipātika, all symptoms are present.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तोद्भवे ज्वरच्छर्दिमूर्च्छातिसारतृष्णाभ्रमशूलारोचकतमकदाहाः । दीप्ताङ्गारावकीर्णवत् संज्ञां करोति । शान्ताङ्गारासितं नीलं रक्तं वा भवति । अग्निदग्धवत् स्फोटाः शीघ्रगतित्वान्मर्मानुसारिणः । न शर्म लभते । दुष्प्रबोधो निद्रामस्नुते । अयमग्निविसर्पः ॥ ८-१३ ॥
transliteration: Vātapittodbhave jvaracchardimūrcchātisāratṛṣṇābhr amaśūlārocakatamakadāhāḥ | Dīptāṅgārāvakīrṇavat saṃjñāṃ karoti | Śāntāṅgārāsitaṃ nīlaṃ raktaṃ vā bhavati | Agnidagdhavat sphoṭāḥ śīghragatitvānmarmānusāriṇaḥ | Na śarma labhate | Duṣprabodho nidrāmasnute | Ayamagnivisarpaḥ || 8-13 ||
commentary: Due to predominance of Vāta and Pitta in visarpa, there are fever, vomiting, syncope, diarrhoea, thirst, giddiness, tumours, breaking pain in the joints, loss of appetite, darkening before the eyes or severe dyspnoea (Tamaka), anorexia, feeling as if covered by burning coal; wherever this types of visarpa manifests in the body, that place becomes black like extinguished coal or blue or red, there will be blisters resembling those caused by burning that spread fast. It affects mostly the vital parts. Due to the influence of Vāta there will be severe pain, loss of consciousness, sleeplessness, severe dyspnoea and hiccup. Such patient will never get relief in any posture. He keeps sitting, lying down again and again to find relief; He goes into difficult position mentally and physically and may get into sleep from which he can never wake up. This condition is called Agni visarpa.

sanskrit_text: कफेन रुद्धः पवनो भित्त्वा तं बहुधा कफम् । रक्तं वा वृद्धिरक्तस्य त्वक्सिरास्नायुमांसगम् ॥ १४ ॥ दूषयित्वा तु दीर्घाणुवृत्तस्थूलखरात्मनाम् । ग्रन्थीनां कुरुते मालां सरक्तां तीव्ररुग्ज्वराम् ॥ १५ ॥ श्वासकासातिसारास्यशोषहिक्काविभ्रमैः । मोहवैवर्ण्यमूर्च्छाकुभङ्गाग्निसदनेयुताम् ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration: Kaphena ruddhaḥ pavano bhittvā taṃ bahudhā kapham | Raktaṃ vā vṛddhiraktasya tvaksirāsnāyumāṃsag am || 14 || Dūṣayitvā tu dīrghāṇuvṛttasthūlakharātmanām | Granthīnāṃ kurute mālāṃ saraktāṃ tīvrarugjvarām || 15 || Śvāsakāsātisārāsyaśoṣahikkāvibhramaiḥ | Mohavaivarṇyamūrcchākubhaṅgāgnisadaneyutām || 16 ||
commentary: Vāta that is obstructed by kapha, breaks that kapha into various forms, or the rakta which is accumulated in the skin, veins, tendons and muscle tissue and on vitiating them causes long, small, round, big and hard tumours in series which are red in colour, severely painful, associated with fever, dyspnoea, cough, diarrhoea, dryness in the mouth, hiccup, vomiting, giddiness, delusion, discolouration, syncope, breaking sensation in the body and loss of appetite. This condition is called Granthi visarpa caused by aggravated kapha and vāta.

sanskrit_text: कफपित्ताज्ज्वरः स्तम्भो निद्रा तन्द्रा शिरोरुजा । अङ्गावसादविक्षेपौ प्रलेपारोचकश्रमाः । मूर्च्छाग्निहानिर्भेदोऽस्थ्नां पिपासेन्द्रियगौरवम् ॥ १७-१८ ॥ आमोपवेशनं लेपः स्रोतसां स च सर्पति । प्रायेणामाशयं गृह्णाति न चातिरुक् ॥ १९ ॥ पिडकैरवकीर्णोऽतिपीतलोहितपाण्डुरैः । स्निग्धोऽसितो मेचकाभो मलिनः शोफवान् गुरुः ॥ २० ॥ गम्भीरपाकः प्राज्योष्मा स्पृष्टः क्लिन्नोऽवदीर्यते । पङ्कवच्छीर्णमांसश्च स्पष्टस्नायुसिरागणः ॥ २१ ॥ शवगन्धी च विसर्पः कर्दमाख्यमुशन्ति तम् ॥
transliteration: Kaphapittājjvaraḥ stambho nidrā tandrā śirorujā | Aṅgāvasādavikṣepau pralepārocakaśramāḥ | Mūrcchāgnihānirbhedo'sthnāṃ pipāsendriyagauravam || 17-18 || Āmopaveśanaṃ lepaḥ srotasāṃ sa ca sarpati | Prāyeṇāmāśayaṃ gṛhṇāti na cātiruk || 19 || Piḍakaira vakīrṇo'tipītalohitapāṇḍuraiḥ | Snigdho'sito mecakābho malinaḥ śophavān guruḥ || 20 || Gambhīrapākaḥ prājyoṣmā spṛṣṭaḥ klinno'vadīryate | Paṅkavacchīrṇamāṃsaśca spaṣṭasnāyusirāgaṇaḥ || 21 || Śavagandhī ca visarpaḥ kardamākhyamuśanti tam ||
commentary: Due to kapha and pitta, there is fever, rigidity in the limbs, excessive sleep, tiredness of the hands and legs, feeling of stickiness, anorexia, giddiness, syncope, loss of appetite, breaking sensation in the bones, thirst, heaviness in the sense-organs, passing stool with more of āma (undigested stuff), sticky feeling, moving in the channels it taken shelter in the āmāśaya and is not much painful. The vesicles that arise are in clusters-yellow in colour, red and pale, oily, blackish like the collyrium, turbid, swollen and heavy, they get ripened internally with lot of warmth and wetness, they wither away even by touch; the muscle looks like mud/black clay, withers out exposing the ligaments and veins with necrosed smell. Such visarpa is called Kardama visarpa.

sanskrit_text: क्षतविसर्पे विसर्पलिङ्गं ज्वरदाहतृष्णाभ्रमोहमूर्च्छाश्च । सर्वे विसर्पाः कृच्छ्रसाध्याः । सन्निपातजश्चासाध्यः ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration: Kṣatavisarpe visarpaliṅgaṃ jvaradāhatṛṣṇābhramohamūrcchāśca | Sarve visarpāḥ kṛcchrasādhyāḥ | Sannipātajaścāsādhyaḥ || 22 ||
commentary: In Kṣata visarpa, there are features of visarpa along with fever, burning sensation, thirst, giddiness, delusion and syncope. All visarpas are difficult to cure, and the sannipātaja type is incurable.

sanskrit_text: कट्वम्लतीक्ष्णविदाहिरूक्षक्षाराजीर्णाध्यशनातपर्तुविपर्ययैः । वातादयः प्रकुपिता रक्तमांसमेदांसि दूषयन्ति । ज्वरपुरःसरान् विस्फोटान् जनयन्ति ॥ १-२ ॥
transliteration: Kaṭvamlatīkṣṇavidāhirūkṣakṣārājīrṇādhyaśanātapartuviparyayaiḥ | Vātādayaḥ prakupitā raktamāṃsamedāṃsi dūṣayanti | Jvarapuraḥsarān visphoṭān janayanti || 1-2 ||
commentary: Consumption of pungent, sour, severe/fast, burnt dry and alkali foods, indigestion, eating without complete digestion of the previous food, exposure to heat/sun and improper seasonal behaviour lead to aggravation of vāta etc., doṣas which take shelter in the skin and in turn vitiate blood, muscle tissue and bones and cause severe eruption of bullae associated with fever.

sanskrit_text: रक्तपित्ताभ्यां दग्धवत् स्फोटा ज्वरपुरःसराः । एकदेशे सर्वदेहे वा विस्फोटाः ॥ ३ ॥ वातिके कृष्णाः सरुजः । पैत्तिके पीतरागाः सदाहाः सरुजः सस्रावाः । कफजे श्वेताः स्निग्धाः स्थिराः सकण्डूरल्परुजः चिरपाकाः ॥ ४-७ ॥
transliteration: Raktapittābhyāṃ dagdhavat sphoṭā jvarapuraḥsarāḥ | Ekadeśe sarvadehe vā visphoṭāḥ || 3 || Vātike kṛṣṇāḥ sarujaḥ | Paittike pītarāgāḥ sadāhāḥ sarujaḥ sasrāvāḥ | Kaphaje śvetāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirāḥ sakaṇḍūralparujaḥ cirapākāḥ || 4-7 ||
commentary: The blisters that look as if caused by burns, with fever, occur on one part or complete body due to Rakta pitta are known as Visphoṭa (bullae). The black colour of these bullae is the feature of Vāta type. In pitta visphoṭa, there will be fever, burning sensation, pain, exudation, ulceration and thirst and the colour of the blister, yellowish-red. Vomiting, anorexia, rigidity, itching sensation, hardness, pale colour, little pain and delayed ripening of the blisters are the features of kapha visphoṭa.

sanskrit_text: सन्निपातिके निम्नमध्यान्युन्नतान्तानि कठिनान्यल्पपाकानि । दाहरागतृष्णामोहच्छर्दिमूर्च्छारुग्ज्वरप्रलापकम्पभ्रमैर्युक्तानि । अचिकित्स्यानि ॥ ८-९ ॥
transliteration: Sannipātike nimnamadhyānyunnatāntāni kaṭhinānyalpapākāni | Dāharāgatṛṣṇāmohacchardimūrcchārugjvarapralāpakampabhramairyuktāni | Acikitsyāni || 8-9 ||
commentary: Centrally depressed and elevated in the ends, hard, slightly ripened, associated with burning sensation, redness, thirst, delusion, vomiting, syncope, pain, fever, delirium, trembling and dizziness are features of Sannipāta variety of Visphoṭa which is incurable.

sanskrit_text: रक्ता रक्तसमुत्थाना गुञ्जाविद्रुमसन्निभाः । वेदितव्यास्तु रक्तेन पैत्तिकेन च हेतुना ॥ १० ॥ न ते सिद्धिं समायान्ति सिद्धैर्योगशतैरपि । एकदोषोत्थितः साध्यः कृच्छ्रसाध्यो द्विदोषजः । सर्वदोषोत्थितो घोरस्त्वसाध्यो भूर्युपद्रवः ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration: Raktā raktasamutthānā guñjāvidrumasannibhāḥ | Veditavyāstu raktena paittikena ca hetunā || 10 || Na te siddhiṃ samāyānti siddhair yogasatairapi | Ekadoṣotthitaḥ sādhyaḥ kṛcchrasādh yo dvidoṣajaḥ | Sarvadoṣotthito ghorastvāsādhyo bhūryupadravaḥ || 11 ||
commentary: The visphoṭa caused by Rakta are blood-red in colour and like seeds of abrus precatorius and coral beads. These are to be known as caused by Rakta and Pitta. They can not be treated even with hundreds of well prepared medicines. Single dosa type of Visphoṭa is difficult for cure. The tridoṣa afflicted one is very severe and incurable when associated with complications.

sanskrit_text: कट्वम्ललवणक्षारविरुद्धाध्यशनाशनैः । दुष्टनिष्पावशाकाद्यैः प्रदुष्टपवनोदकैः ॥ १ ॥ क्रूरग्रहेक्षणाच्चापदेशे दोषाः समुद्धताः । जनयन्ति शरीरेऽस्मिन्दुष्टरक्तेन सङ्गताः ॥ २ ॥ मसूराकृतिसंस्थानाः पिडकाः स्युर्मसूरिकाः । तासां पूर्वं ज्वरः कण्डूर्गात्रभङ्गोऽरतिर्ज्वरः ॥ ३ ॥ त्वचि शोथः सर्ववर्णौ नेत्ररागश्च जायते ॥
transliteration: Kaṭvamlalavaṇakṣāraviruddhādhy aśanāśanaiḥ | Duṣṭaniṣpāvaśākādyaiḥ praduṣṭapavanodakaiḥ || 1 || Krūragrahekṣaṇāccāpadeśe doṣāḥ samuddhatāḥ | Janayanti śarīre'sminduṣṭaraktena saṅgatāḥ || 2 || Masūrākṛtisaṃsthānāḥ piḍakāḥ syurmasūrikāḥ | Tāsāṃ pūrvaṃ jvaraḥ kaṇḍūrgātabhaṅgo'ratirjvaraḥ || 3 || Tvaci śothaḥ sarvavarṇau netrarāgaśca jāyate ||
commentary: Due to consumption of foods that are pungent, sour, salty, alkali in nature, incompatible combinations, eating prior to digestion of previous food, putrified food, lentils, green leaves; drinking of contaminated water; exposure to contaminated air and also due to incompatible zodiac constellation, the doṣas aggravate, get into contact with blood which is already vitiated and cause vesicles of masūra (lathyrus sativa) size and shape which are called masūrikā. Prior to these, there will be fever, itching sensation, breaking sensation in the body, fatigue, giddiness, swelling in the skin, discolouration of the skin and redness in the eyes as prodromata.

sanskrit_text: वातिके श्यावरक्ताः स्थिराः सरुजश्चिरपाकाः । महास्थिसन्धिषु भेदः कम्पश्छर्दिररतिसदनशोषाः ॥ ४-५ ॥
transliteration: Vātike śyāvaraktāḥ sthirāḥ sarujaścirapākāḥ | Mahāsthisaṃdhiṣu bhedaḥ kampaśchardiraratisadanaśoṣāḥ || 4-5 ||
commentary: The blisters are blackish-red in colour, dry, associated with severe pain, hard and delayed-ripening in Vāta type of masūrikā. Breaking sensation in big joints and small bone-joints, cough, trembling, restlessness, fatigue, dryness in the palate, lips and tongue, thirst and distaste are the signs and symptoms of this variety.

sanskrit_text: पैत्तिके पीतरक्ताः सदाहाः सरुजः शीघ्रपाकाः । अतिसारज्वरदाहतृष्णारुचिमुखपाकाक्षिरागाः । दारुणा च सा ॥ ६-७ ॥
transliteration: Paittike pītaraktāḥ sadāhāḥ sarujaḥ śīghrapākāḥ | Atisārajvaradāhatṛṣṇārucimukhapākākṣirāgāḥ | Dāruṇā ca sā || 6-7 ||
commentary: The bullae are red, yellowish white in colour, with burning sensation and severe pain; they ripen fast which are caused by pitta-aggravation. There will be diarrhoea, myalgia, burning sensation, thirst, distaste, stomatitis, redness in the eyes, high temperature and the condition is severe (in pittaja masūrikā).

sanskrit_text: रक्तजे रक्तवर्णाः सदाहाः सरुजः । कफजे श्वेताः स्निग्धाः स्थिराः सकण्डूरल्परुजश्चिरपाकाः ॥ ८-१३ ॥
transliteration: Raktaje raktavarṇāḥ sadāhāḥ sarujaḥ | Kaphaje śvetāḥ snigdhāḥ sthirāḥ sakaṇḍūralparujaścirapākāḥ || 8-13 ||
commentary: Raktaja masūrikā are red in colour, with burning sensation and pain. Kaphaja masūrikā are white, unctuous, stable, with itching, mild pain and delayed ripening.

sanskrit_text: त्वगतास्तु मसूरिका जलबुद्बुदसदृशाः । रक्तस्था लोहिताकाराः शीघ्रपाकास्तनुत्वचः । मांसस्थाः कठिनाः स्निग्धाश्चिरपाका घनत्वचः । मेदोजा मण्डलाकारा मृदवः स्निग्धाः सवेदनाः । अस्थिमज्जोत्थाः सूक्ष्मा रूक्षाश्चिपिटाः किंचिदुन्नताः । शुक्रजायां पक्वाभाः स्निग्धाः सूक्ष्माः सवेदनाः ॥ १४-२३ ॥
transliteration: Tvagatāstu masūrikā jalabudbudasadṛśāḥ | Raktasthā lohitākārāḥ śīghrapākāstanutvacaḥ | Māṃsasthāḥ kaṭhināḥ snigdhāścirapākā ghanatvacaḥ | Medojā maṇḍalākārā mṛdavaḥ snigdhāḥ savedanāḥ | Asthimajjotthāḥ sūkṣmā rūkṣāści piṭāḥ kiṃcidunnatāḥ | Śukrajāyāṃ pakvābhāḥ snigdhāḥ sūkṣmāḥ savedanāḥ || 14-23 ||
commentary: Masūrikā based on skin/rasa look like water bubbles. Based on rakta - red, ripening fast, thin skinned. Based on māmsa - hard, unctuous, delayed ripening, thick skinned. Based on medas - round, soft, unctuous, painful. Based on asthi and majjā - small, dry, flat, slightly elevated. Based on śukra - ripened, unctuous, small and very painful.

sanskrit_text: त्वगताः रक्तजाः पित्तजाः श्लेष्मजाः सुखसाध्याः । वातजाः श्लेष्मपित्तकृताश्च कृच्छ्रसाध्याः । सन्निपातजाश्चासाध्याः ॥ २४-२६ ॥
transliteration: Tvagatāḥ raktajāḥ pittajāḥ śleṣmajāḥ sukhasādhyāḥ | Vātajāḥ śleṣmapittakṛtāśca kṛcchrasādhyāḥ | Sannipātajāścāsādhyāḥ || 24-26 ||
commentary: Masūrikā based on skin/rasa, rakta, pitta and kapha are easily curable. Vātaja and śleṣma-pitta types are difficult to cure. Sannipātaja types are incurable.

sanskrit_text: कासहिक्काप्रमेहातिज्वरविप्लवमूर्च्छातृष्णादाहजिह्वाप्रस्रंसनरक्तशुक्रातिसारस्वरभङ्गाः । नरं मसूरिकया हन्युः ॥ २७-३१ ॥
transliteration: Kāsahikkāpramehātijvaraviplavamūrcchātṛṣṇādāhajihvāprasraṃsanaraktaśukrātisārasvarabhaṅgāḥ | Naraṃ masūrikayā hanyuḥ || 27-31 ||
commentary: If the physician finds the following signs and symptoms in a masūrikā afflicted patient, he should not give any medicine, viz., cough, hiccup, urinary flux, high temperature, delirium, restlessness, syncope, thirst, burning sensation, irrelevant movement of the tongue, bleeding from the mouth, nostrils and ears, making 'ghur-ghur' sounds in the throat and respiration with great difficulty. These complications kill the patient.

sanskrit_text: बालानां कफवाताभ्यां पिडका गौरसर्षपाः । स्निग्धाः स्थूलास्तथा रूक्षाः स्थिरा अजगल्लिकाः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Bālānāṃ kaphavātābhyāṃ piḍakā gaurasarṣapāḥ | Snigdhāḥ sthūlāstathā rūkṣāḥ sthirā ajagallikāḥ || 1 ||
commentary: The papules occurring in children due to aggravation of kapha-vāta which are oily, skin coloured, knotted, painless and look like seeds of green-gram are called ajagallikā.

sanskrit_text: यवाकाराः स्थिराः पिडकाः स्निग्धा मांससम्भवाः । कफवातोत्थिता यावप्रख्या ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Yavākārāḥ sthirāḥ piḍakāḥ snigdhā māṃsasambhavāḥ | Kaphavātothitā yāvaprakhyā || 2 ||
commentary: The macules that look like the seeds of barley, strong and knotted - are based in māṃsadhātu and caused by kapha-vāta which are called yavaprakhyā.

sanskrit_text: अन्त्रालजी विवृता कच्छपिका वल्मीक इन्द्रविद्धा गर्दभिका पाषाणगर्दभः पनसिका जालगर्दभ इरिवेल्लिका कक्षा गन्धमाला अग्निरोहिणी चिप्पा कुनख अनुशयी विदारिका शर्करार्बुद पाददारी कदर अलस इन्द्रलुप्त दारुणक अरूंषिका पलित युवानपिडका पद्मिनीकण्टक जतुमणि मशक तिलकालक न्यच्छ व्यङ्ग नीलिका परिवर्तिका अवपातिका निरुद्धप्रकाश सन्निरुद्धगुद अहिपूतना वृषणकच्छू गुदभ्रंश सूकरदंष्ट्रक/वराहदंष्ट्रक ॥ ३-२३ ॥
transliteration: Antrālajī vivṛtā kacchapikā valmīka indraviddhā gardabhikā pāśāṇagardabhaḥ panasikā jālagardabha irivellikā kakṣā gandhamālā agnirohiṇī cippā kunakha anuśayī vidārikā śarkarārbuda pādadārī kadara alasa indralupta dāruṇaka arūṃṣikā palita yuvānapiḍakā padminīkaṇṭaka jatumaṇi maśaka tilakālaka nyaccha vyaṅga nīlikā parivartikā avapātikā niruddhaprakāśa sanniruddhaguda ahipūtanā vṛṣaṇakacchū gudabhraṃśa sūkaradaṃṣṭraka/varāhadaṃṣṭraka || 3-23 ||
commentary: The various Kṣudrarogas (minor diseases) are: Antrālajī, Vivṛtā, Kacchapikā, Valmīka, Indraviddhā, Gardabhikā, Pāśāṇagardabha, Panasikā, Jālagardabha, Irivellikā, Kakṣā, Gandhamālā, Agnirohiṇī, Cippā, Kunakha, Anuśayī, Vidārikā, Śarkarārbuda, Pādadārī, Kadara, Alasa, Indralupta, Dāruṇaka, Arūṃṣikā, Palita, Yuvānapiḍakā, Padminīkaṇṭaka, Jatumaṇi, Maśaka, Tilakālaka, Nyaccha, Vyaṅga, Nīlikā, Parivartikā, Avapātikā, Niruddhaprakāśa, Sanniruddhaguda, Ahipūtanā, Vṛṣaṇakacchū, Gudabhraṃśa, Sūkaradaṃṣṭraka/Varāhadaṃṣṭraka.

sanskrit_text: ग्राम्यानूपमांसक्षीरदधिमत्स्यातिसेवनात् । कफानुगाः प्रकुपिता दोषा मुखरोगान् जनयन्ति ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Grāmyānūpamāṃsakṣīradadhimatsyātisevanāt | Kaphānugāḥ prakupitā doṣā mukharogān janayanti || 1 ||
commentary: Due to over consumption of flesh of animals that exist in the watery lands, milk, curds and fish, the aggravated doṣas that follow kapha cause diseases in the buccal cavity.

sanskrit_text: वातेनौष्ठौ कठिनौ परुषौ स्तब्धौ सरुजौ दीर्येते । पित्तेन पिडकावन्तौ सदाहौ सपाकौ पीतौ । कफेन सवर्णौ स्निग्धौ गुरू शीतौ । सन्निपातेन नानावर्णौ पिडकाचितौ । रक्तेन खर्जूरफलवर्णौ स्राविणौ । मांसेन गुरू स्थूलौ शोफौ मांसपिण्डोपमौ । मेदसा सर्पिमण्डप्रकाशौ सकण्डू स्राविणौ । अभिघातेन क्षतौ कठिनौ ग्रन्थियुक्तौ सकण्डू ॥ २-९ ॥
transliteration: Vātenauṣṭhau kaṭhinau paruṣau stabdhau sarujau dīryete | Pittena piḍakāvantau sadāhau sapākau pītau | Kaphena savarṇau snigdhau gurū śītau | Sannipātena nānāvarṇau piḍakācitau | Raktena kharjūraphalavarṇau srāviṇau | Māṃsena gurū sthūlau śophau māṃsapiṇḍopamau | Medasā sarpimaṇḍaprakāśau sakaṇḍū srāviṇau | Abhighātena kṣatau kaṭhinau granthiyuktau sakaṇḍū || 2-9 ||
commentary: Vāta type: lips are hard, rough, rigid, painful and cracked. Pitta type: lips have vesicles, burning sensation, ulceration and yellowish colour. Kapha type: same coloured, unctuous, heavy and cold. Sannipāta type: various colours and filled with papules. Rakta type: date-coloured, with discharge. Māṃsa type: heavy, thick, swollen, like a piece of muscle. Medas type: like the supernatant of ghee, with itching and discharge. Abhighāta type: cut, hard, knotted and with itching.

sanskrit_text: शीतदा - दन्तवेष्टात् शोणितं स्रवति । दन्तपुप्पुटकः - द्वित्रदन्तमूले शोफः । दन्तवेष्टः - पूयरक्तस्रावी चलदन्तः । सौषिरः - शोफवान् स्त्रवश्च । महासौषिरः - दन्तच्युतिस्तालुविदारः । परिदरः - दन्तवेष्टशोणितस्रावी । उपकुशः - दाहपाकवान् । वैदर्भः - दन्तवेष्टशोफो दाहः । खलिवर्धनः - अतिरिक्तदन्तोत्पत्तिः । करालः - विषमदन्तः । अधिमांसकः - हनुमूले शोफः । दन्तनाडी - पञ्चविधा ॥ १०-२१ ॥
transliteration: Śītadā - dantaveṣṭāt śoṇitaṃ sravati | Dantapuppuṭakaḥ - dvitradantamūle śophaḥ | Dantaveṣṭaḥ - pūyaraktasrāvī caladantaḥ | Sauṣiraḥ - śophavān sravaśca | Mahāsauṣiraḥ - dantacyutistāluvidāraḥ | Paridaraḥ - dantaveṣṭaśoṇitasrāvī | Upakuśaḥ - dāhapākavān | Vaidarbhaḥ - dantaveṣṭaśopho dāhaḥ | Khalivardhanaḥ - atiriktadantotpattiḥ | Karālaḥ - viṣamadantaḥ | Adhimāṃsakaḥ - hanumūle śophaḥ | Dantanāḍī - pañcavidhā || 10-21 ||
commentary: Various diseases of the teeth and gums are described. Śītadā - bleeding from gums. Dantapuppuṭaka - swelling at the root of two or three teeth. Dantaveṣṭa - discharge of pus and blood, shaky teeth. Sauṣira - swelling and discharge. Mahāsauṣira - tooth loss and palate cracking. Paridara - bleeding from gums. Upakuśa - burning and ulceration. Vaidarbha - swelling and burning of gums. Khalivardhana - extra tooth growth. Karāla - irregular teeth. Adhimāṃsaka - swelling at the root of jaw. Dantanāḍī - five types of sinuses in gums.

sanskrit_text: दालनः - दन्तभेदः । कृमिदन्तकः - कृष्णच्छिद्रः स्रावी । भञ्जनकः - दन्तपातात् मुखविकृतिः । दन्तहर्षः - शीतोष्णादिसहः । दन्तशर्करा - दन्तेषु मलवत् । कपालिका - दन्तभङ्गकरी । श्यावदन्तः - नीलदन्तः । दन्तविद्रधिः - दन्तवेष्टशोफः पूयरक्तस्रावी ॥ २२-२९ ॥
transliteration: Dālanaḥ - dantabhedaḥ | Kṛmidantakaḥ - kṛṣṇacchidraḥ srāvī | Bhañjanakaḥ - dantapātāt mukhavikṛtiḥ | Dantaharṣaḥ - śītoṣṇādisahaḥ | Dantaśarkarā - danteṣu malavat | Kapālikā - dantabhaṅgakarī | Śyāvadantaḥ - nīladantaḥ | Dantavidradhiḥ - dantaveṣṭaśophaḥ pūyaraktasrāvī || 22-29 ||
commentary: Dālana - breaking pain in teeth. Kṛmidantaka - black holes with discharge. Bhañjanaka - facial deformity due to tooth loss. Dantaharṣa - sensitivity to cold, hot etc. Dantaśarkarā - foreign matter on teeth. Kapālikā - causes tooth breaking. Śyāvadanta - bluish-black teeth. Dantavidradhi - swelling of gums with pus and blood discharge.

sanskrit_text: जिह्वाकण्टकः - जिह्वास्फुटनम् । अधिजिह्विका - जिह्वोपरि शोफः । उपजिह्विका - जिह्वामूलशोफः । अलसः - जिह्वामूलशोफः कृच्छ्रसाध्यः ॥ ३०-३२ ॥
transliteration: Jihvākaṇṭakaḥ - jihvāsphuṭanam | Adhijihvikā - jihvopari śophaḥ | Upajihvikā - jihvāmūlaśophaḥ | Alasaḥ - jihvāmūlaśophaḥ kṛcchrasādhyaḥ || 30-32 ||
commentary: Jihvākaṇṭaka - cracking of tongue, loss of taste. Adhijihvikā - swelling on the tongue. Upajihvikā - swelling at the base of tongue with salivation, itching and burning. Alasa - severe inflammation at the base of tongue, difficult to cure.

sanskrit_text: कण्ठशुण्डी - तालुमूले शोफः । तुन्दिकेरी - कफरक्तजशोफः । अघ्रुसः - रक्तजशोफः । कच्छपः - कफजशोफः । ताल्वर्बुदम् - रक्तार्बुदवत् । तालुपुप्पुटः - स्थिरः । तालुपाकः - दाहपाकवान् ॥ ३३-३७ ॥
transliteration: Kaṇṭhaśuṇḍī - tālumūle śophaḥ | Tundikerī - kapharaktajaśophaḥ | Aghrusaḥ - raktajaśophaḥ | Kacchapaḥ - kaphajaśophaḥ | Tālvarbudam - raktārbudavat | Tālupuppuṭaḥ - sthiraḥ | Tālupākaḥ - dāhapākavān || 33-37 ||
commentary: Kaṇṭhaśuṇḍī - elongated inflammation at the base of palate. Tundikerī - gross inflammation caused by kapha and rakta. Aghrusa - red soft inflammation caused by rakta. Kacchapa - tortoise-like growth caused by kapha. Tālvarbuda - lotus-like growth in the centre of palate. Tālupuppuṭa - stable growth in the palate. Tālupāka - severe ulceration of palate caused by pitta.

sanskrit_text: रोहिणी - गलशोफः पञ्चविधः । कण्ठशालूकः - कठिनः शल्यसाध्यः । वलयः - स्थूलः कफजः । बलासः - कफवातजः । एकवृन्दः - कफरक्तजः । वृन्दः - पित्तरक्तजः । शतघ्नी - त्रिदोषजा अचिकित्स्या । गलायुः - कफरक्तजः शल्यसाध्यः । गलविद्रधिः - गले विद्रधिः । गलौघः - कफरक्तजः । स्वरघ्नः - वातिकः । मांसतानः - त्रिदोषजः । विदारी - पित्तजः । सर्वसारः/मुखपाकः - मुखे पिडकाः ॥ ३८-५८ ॥
transliteration: Rohiṇī - galaśophaḥ pañcavidhaḥ | Kaṇṭhaśālūkaḥ - kaṭhinaḥ śalyasādhyaḥ | Valayaḥ - sthūlaḥ kaphajaḥ | Balāsaḥ - kaphavātajaḥ | Ekavṛndaḥ - kapharaktajaḥ | Vṛndaḥ - pittaraktajaḥ | Śataghnī - tridoṣajā acikitsyā | Galāyuḥ - kapharaktajaḥ śalyasādhyaḥ | Galavidradhiḥ - gale vidradhiḥ | Galaughaḥ - kapharaktajaḥ | Svaraghnaḥ - vātikaḥ | Māṃsatānaḥ - tridoṣajaḥ | Vidārī - pittajaḥ | Sarvasāraḥ/mukhapākaḥ - mukhe piḍakāḥ || 38-58 ||
commentary: Rohiṇī - five types of throat swelling. Kaṇṭhaśālūka - hard growth, surgical treatment. Valaya - wide swelling caused by kapha. Balāsa - inflammation caused by kapha-vāta. Ekavṛnda - swelling caused by kapha-rakta. Vṛnda - swelling caused by pitta-rakta. Śataghnī - tridoṣaja, incurable. Galāyu - tumour in throat, surgical treatment. Galavidradhi - abscess in throat. Galaugha - big swelling caused by kapha-rakta. Svaraghna - caused by vāta, causes voice disturbance. Māṃsatāna - tridoṣaja, wide spread. Vidārī - caused by pitta. Sarvasāra/Mukhapāka - blisters in the mouth.

sanskrit_text: ओष्ठयोर्मांसजरक्तजसन्निपातजाः । दन्तमूले त्रिदोषजाः सौषिराः । दन्तेषु श्यावदालनभञ्जनकाः । जिह्वायां बलासः । ताल्वर्बुदम् । कण्ठे स्वरघ्नवलयवृन्दबलासविदारीगलौघमांसतानशतघ्नीरोहिण्यः ॥ ५९ ॥
transliteration: Oṣṭhayormāṃsajaraktajasannipātajāḥ | Dantamūle tridoṣajāḥ sauṣirāḥ | Danteṣu śyāvadālanabhañjanakāḥ | Jihvāyāṃ balāsaḥ | Tālvarbudam | Kaṇṭhe svaraghnavalayavṛndabalāsavidārīgalaughamāṃsatānaśataghnīrohiṇyaḥ || 59 ||
commentary: The incurable diseases of the mouth include: māṃsaja, raktaja and tridoṣaja types of lip diseases; tridoṣaja and sauṣira of gum diseases; śyāva, dālana and bhañjanaka of tooth diseases; balāsa of tongue diseases; arbuda of palate diseases; and svaraghna, valaya, vṛnda, balāsa, vidārī, galaugha, māṃsatāna, śataghnī and rohiṇī of throat diseases.

sanskrit_text: अन्यथाचरन् वायुः कर्णौ प्राप्य दोषैः सह सङ्गतोऽतिवेदनां करोति । स कर्णशूलः कृच्छ्रसाध्यः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Anyathācaran vāyuḥ karṇau prāpya doṣaiḥ saha saṅgato'tivedanāṃ karoti | Sa karṇaśūlaḥ kṛcchrasādhyaḥ || 1 ||
commentary: The vāta having entered the ears moves in an opposite direction and gets associated with the other doṣas and causes severe pain. This condition is called Karṇaśūla and it is incurable.

sanskrit_text: वातेन कर्णे नानाशब्दाः श्रूयन्ते । स कर्णनादः । वातेनैव कर्णे बधिर्यं भवति ॥ २-३ ॥ कर्णक्ष्वेडः - वातपित्ताभ्यां वंशनिध्र्वानसदृशः शब्दः ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Vātena karṇe nānāśabdāḥ śrūyante | Sa karṇanādaḥ | Vātenaiva karṇe badhiryaṃ bhavati || 2-3 || Karṇakṣveḍaḥ - vātapittābhyāṃ vaṃśanidhrvānasadṛśaḥ śabdaḥ || 4 ||
commentary: When the vāta settles in the inner ear, the individual hears different types of sounds like beating Bherī, Mṛdaṅga, blowing Śaṅkha etc. - this condition is called Karṇanāda. When the sound carrying Vāta occupies the ear alone or along with Kapha, there occurs Bādhirya (deafness). Karṇakṣveḍa - vāta associated with pitta causes sounds that resemble the blowing of wind through bamboos.

sanskrit_text: कर्णस्रावः - कर्णात् पूयस्रावः । कर्णकण्डूः - कण्डूः । कर्णगूथः - कर्णमलम् । कर्णप्रतिनाहः - कर्णमलेन नासामुखसम्बन्धः । कृमिकर्णः - कर्णे कृमयः ॥ ५-८ ॥
transliteration: Karṇasrāvaḥ - karṇāt pūyasrāvaḥ | Karṇakaṇḍūḥ - kaṇḍūḥ | Karṇagūthaḥ - karṇamalam | Karṇapratināhaḥ - karṇamalena nāsāmukhasambandhaḥ | Kṛmikarṇaḥ - karṇe kṛmayaḥ || 5-8 ||
commentary: Karṇasrāva - discharge of pus from ears. Karṇakaṇḍū - itching in the ear. Karṇagūtha - ear wax. Karṇapratināha - obstruction caused by ear wax entering the nose and mouth. Kṛmikarṇa - worms in the ear due to necrosis of muscle tissue and blood.

sanskrit_text: कर्णविद्रधिः - कर्णे विद्रधिः । कर्णपाकः - कर्णस्य पाकः । पूतिकर्णः - कर्णात् पूतिस्रावः । कर्णशोफार्बुदार्शांसि - यथास्वलिङ्गैः । वातपित्तकफजाः कर्णरोगाश्चत्वारः ॥ ९-१५ ॥
transliteration: Karṇavidradhiḥ - karṇe vidradhiḥ | Karṇapākaḥ - karṇasya pākaḥ | Pūtikarṇaḥ - karṇāt pūtisrāvaḥ | Karṇaśophārbudārśāṃsi - yathāsvaliṅgaiḥ | Vātapittakaphajāḥ karṇarogāścatvāraḥ || 9-15 ||
commentary: Karṇavidradhi - abscess in the ear. Karṇapāka - ulceration in the ear. Pūtikarṇa - putrified discharge from the ear. Karṇaśopha, Arbuda, Arśas - swelling, abscess and piles of the ear with respective features. The four ear diseases as per Caraka are vātaja, pittaja, kaphaja and sannipātaja.

sanskrit_text: परिपोटः - कर्णपालीशोफः । उत्पातः - रक्तपित्तजः । उन्मन्थकः - कफवातजः । दुःखवर्धनः - त्रिदोषजः । परिलेही - कफरक्तकृमिजः ॥ १६-२२ ॥
transliteration: Paripoṭaḥ - karṇapālīśophaḥ | Utpātaḥ - raktapittajaḥ | Unmanthakaḥ - kaphavātajaḥ | Duḥkhavardhanaḥ - tridoṣajaḥ | Parilehī - kapharaktakṛmijaḥ || 16-22 ||
commentary: Paripoṭa - inflammation of the pinna. Utpāta - blackish or reddish inflammation caused by rakta and pitta. Unmanthaka - inflammation with rigidity caused by kapha-vāta. Duḥkhavardhana - inflammation with itching and ulceration caused by tridoṣa. Parilehī - mustard sized bullae with itching, burning and pain caused by kapha, rakta and worms.

sanskrit_text: नासा आनह्यते प्रक्लिद्यते धूप्यते । गन्धरसावबोधश्च न भवति । सोऽपीनसः प्रतिश्यायसमलिङ्गः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Nāsā ānahyate praklidyate dhūpyate | Gandharasāvabodhaśca na bhavati | So'pīnasaḥ pratiśyāyasamaliṅgaḥ || 1 ||
commentary: When the nose gets blocked, dried, becomes wet, with sensation of fumes coming out of it and when there is no perception of smell and taste, the particular individual should be known as suffering from apīnasa. This should be labelled as Vātakaphaja disease which is similar to pratiśyāya (coryza).

sanskrit_text: विदग्धैर्दोषैः पूतिमुखनासिकः पूतिनास्यः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Vidagdhairdoṣaiḥ pūtimukhanāsikaḥ pūtināsyaḥ || 2 ||
commentary: When the over boiled/baked/burnt doṣa at the throat and roof of the palate get mingled with vāta - it will discharge putrified matter from the mouth and nose - this condition is called Pūtināsya (Atropic Rhinitis).

sanskrit_text: नासापाकः - पित्तेन नासिकायां पिडकाः । पूयरक्तः - नासिकातः पूयरक्तस्रावः । क्षवथुः - वातकफाभ्यां क्षवथुः । भ्रंशथुः - कफस्य नासिकया स्रावः । दीप्ता - नासिकायां दाहः । प्रतिनाहः - नासिकायां रोधः । नासास्रावः - नासिकातः स्रावः । नासाशोषः - नासिकायाः शोषः ॥ ३-७ ॥
transliteration: Nāsāpākaḥ - pittena nāsikāyāṃ piḍakāḥ | Pūyaraktaḥ - nāsikātaḥ pūyaraktasrāvaḥ | Kṣavathuḥ - vātakaphābhyāṃ kṣavathuḥ | Bhraṃśathuḥ - kaphasya nāsikayā srāvaḥ | Dīptā - nāsikāyāṃ dāhaḥ | Pratināhaḥ - nāsikāyāṃ rodhaḥ | Nāsāsrāvaḥ - nāsikātaḥ srāvaḥ | Nāsāśoṣaḥ - nāsikāyāḥ śoṣaḥ || 3-7 ||
commentary: Nāsāpāka - small vesicles in the nose caused by pitta. Pūyarakta - discharge of pus and blood from the nose. Kṣavathu - sneezing caused by vāta-kapha. Bhraṃśathu - discharge of liquefied kapha from the nose. Dīptā - severe burning sensation in the nose. Pratināha - nasal obstruction. Nāsāsrāva - nasal discharge. Nāsāśoṣa - dryness of the nose caused by vāta.

sanskrit_text: प्रतिश्यायः पञ्चविधः वातपित्तकफसन्निपातरक्तभेदात् । तस्य पूर्वरूपाणि - क्षवथुः शिरोगुरुत्वं स्तम्भः सर्वाङ्गरुग्घर्षा रोमहर्षश्च । वातिके - नासिकानद्धता शुष्कस्रावः कषायास्यता । पैत्तिके - पीतस्रावः ज्वरदाहतृष्णाः । कफजे - श्वेतस्निग्धस्रावः शिरोगुरुत्वम् । सन्निपातिके - सर्वलिङ्गम् । रक्तजे - रक्तस्रावः ॥ ८-१२ ॥
transliteration: Pratiśyāyaḥ pañcavidhaḥ vātapittakaphasannipātaraktabhedāt | Tasya pūrvarūpāṇi - kṣavathuḥ śirogurutvaṃ stambhaḥ sarvāṅgaruggharṣā romaharṣaśca | Vātike - nāsikānaddhatā śuṣkasrāvaḥ kaṣāyāsyatā | Paittike - pītasrāvaḥ jvaradāhatṛṣṇāḥ | Kaphaje - śvetasnigdhrasrāvaḥ śirogurutvam | Sannipātike - sarvaliṅgam | Raktaje - raktasrāvaḥ || 8-12 ||
commentary: Pratiśyāya is of five types: vātaja, pittaja, kaphaja, sannipātaja and raktaja. Premonitory symptoms: sneezing, heaviness of head, rigidity, body pain, horripilation. Vātaja - nasal obstruction, dry discharge, astringent taste. Pittaja - yellow discharge, fever, burning, thirst. Kaphaja - white unctuous discharge, head heaviness. Sannipātaja - all symptoms. Raktaja - blood discharge.

sanskrit_text: दुष्टप्रतिश्याये - नासिका कदाचित् क्लिन्ना कदाचिच्छुष्का । कदाचिदानद्धा कदाचिद्विवृता । दुर्गन्धाश्चास्यम् । गन्धाज्ञानम् । कृच्छ्रसाध्यः ॥ १३-१५ ॥
transliteration: Duṣṭapratiśyāye - nāsikā kadācit klinnā kadācicchuṣkā | Kadācidānaddhā kadācidvivṛtā | Durgandhāścāsyam | Gandhājñānam | Kṛcchrasādhyaḥ || 13-15 ||
commentary: In Duṣṭa pratiśyāya, the nose becomes wet sometimes and dry at other times. It gets blocked sometimes and cleared at other times. The individual exhales very bad breath which is foul and he does not perceive the smell of different odours. Such a condition is known as Duṣṭapratiśyāya which is difficult for cure.

sanskrit_text: जलौकसः स्निग्धस्य च रूक्षस्य च स्नेहनात् । धूमरजोवातातपरक्तपित्तश्लेष्मप्रकोपात् । क्षवथोः प्रतिश्यायाच्छिरोऽभिघाताद्वेगविधारणात् ॥ १-३ ॥
transliteration: Jalaukasaḥ snigdhasya ca rūkṣasya ca snehanāt | Dhūmarajovātātaparak tapittashleṣmaprakopāt | Kṣavathoḥ pratiśyāyācchiro'bhighātādvegavidhāraṇāt || 1-3 ||
commentary: Due to - getting into water immediately after being afflicted by heat, looking at distant objects, disturbance in sleep, sweat, dust and smoke entering into the eye, suppression of vomiting, performing the emesis excessively, eating and drinking more during nights, suppression of the natural urges of faeces and urine, continuous weeping, anger and grief, injury to the head, excessive consumption of alcohol, change in the original characteristics of the seasons, suffering due to chronic ailments, excessive coitus, suppression of tears and looking at micro-objects, the doṣas (get aggravated and) cause (various) diseases in the eyes.

sanskrit_text: सर्वनेत्रामयाणामसौ मूलम् अभिष्यन्दः । स च चतुर्विधो वातपित्तकफरक्तभेदात् ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Sarvanetrāmayāṇāmasau mūlam abhiṣyandaḥ | Sa ca caturvidho vātapittakap haraktabhedāt || 4 ||
commentary: The severe Abhisyanda that in turn causes all eye diseases, is of four types, viz., vāta, pitta, kapha and rakta. Since it affects the complete eye and also contributes to the aetiology of all the eye-diseases, Abhisyanda is being given at the start of the diagnosis of eye-diseases.

sanskrit_text: निस्तोदः स्तम्भः संघर्षः पारुष्यं शुष्कता च । शिरोऽभितापः शीताश्रुता च वातजे ॥ ५ ॥
transliteration: Nistodaḥ stambhaḥ saṃgharṣaḥ pāruṣyaṃ śuṣkatā ca | Śiro'bhitāpaḥ śītāśrutā ca vātaje || 5 ||
commentary: Vāta type of abhisyanda is characterised by pinning sensation in the eyes, rigidity of the eye, scintillation, friction in the eyes (as if sand is poured in the eyes) coarseness and dryness of the eye, head-ache and cold tears.

sanskrit_text: दाहः पाको हिमाभिलाषो धूमायनम् । बाष्पसमुच्छ्रयश्च पीताभता च पित्तजे ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Dāhaḥ pāko himābhilāṣo dhūmāyanam | Bāṣpasamucchrayaśca pītābhatā ca pittaje || 6 ||
commentary: In pitta type of Abhisyanda, there will be burning sensation, ulceration, longing for cool things and atmosphere, feeling of fumes coming out of the eye, excessive and warm lacrymation and yellowishness in the eyes.

sanskrit_text: उपदेहः शोफो गुरुत्वं कण्डूः पिच्छिलता च । शीतता च कफजे ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Upadehaḥ śopho gurutvaṃ kaṇḍūḥ picchilatā ca | Śītatā ca kaphaje || 7 ||
commentary: Desire to have warm things and be in warm atmosphere, heaviness and swelling in the eyes, itching sensation, sticky feeling, excessive coldness and excessive thick exudation from the eyes are the characteristics of Kaphābhisyanda.

sanskrit_text: रक्तजे पित्तलिङ्गं ताम्ररागता च ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration: Raktaje pittaliṅgaṃ tāmrarāgatā ca || 8 ||
commentary: The tears have coppery colour and reddish eyes; with all the veins in the eye ball also bright red in colour, along with other symptomatology of Pittābhisyanda in the case of Raktābhisyanda.

sanskrit_text: अभिष्यन्दात् सर्वोऽधिमन्थो जायते । तीव्रवेदनः स भवति । आक्षेपणमिव मन्यते । अर्धशिरश्छेदनमिव च ॥ ९-१० ॥
transliteration: Abhiṣyandāt sarvo'dhimantho jāyate | Tīvravedanaḥ sa bhavati | Ākṣepaṇamiva manyate | Ardhaśiraśchedanamiva ca || 9-10 ||
commentary: These abhisyandas get aggravated and when unattended cause Adhimantha resulting in severe pain in the eyes. Feeling of the eye being plucked out and half part of the head being churned are main features of adhimantha along with other doshik signs and symptoms of abhisyanda.

sanskrit_text: श्लैष्मिकः सप्तरात्रेण हन्ति । रक्तजः पञ्चरात्रेण । वातिकः षड्रात्रेण । पैत्तिकः सद्यो हन्ति ॥ ११ ॥
transliteration: Ślaiṣmikaḥ saptarātreṇa hanti | Raktajaḥ pañcarātreṇa | Vātikaḥ ṣaḍrātreṇa | Paittikaḥ sadyo hanti || 11 ||
commentary: The Ślaiṣmika adhimantha destroys eye sight by seven nights while, raktaja and vātaja types take five and six nights respectively. But the pittaja abhisyanda causes blindness immediately after affliction.

sanskrit_text: सामे नेत्ररोगे तीव्रवेदनारागशोफघर्षनिस्तोदस्रावाः । निरामे मन्दवेदना कण्डूः शोफप्रशमः स्रावः स्वभावप्राप्तिश्च ॥ १२-१४ ॥
transliteration: Sāme netraroge tīvravedanārāgaśophagharṣanistodasrāvāḥ | Nirāme mandavedanā kaṇḍūḥ śophapraśamaḥ srāvaḥ svabhāvaprāptiśca || 12-14 ||
commentary: In the sama condition of eye diseases, there is severe pain, redness, oedema, friction, pinning sensation and painful tears. In the nirāma state, there is dull pain, itching sensation, palliation of swelling and production of tears and regaining original lustre of the eye.

sanskrit_text: हताधिमन्थे - दृष्टिनाशः । अक्षिशोषो वा । वातेन सदयति ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration: Hatādhimanthe - dṛṣṭināśaḥ | Akṣiśoṣo vā | Vātena sadayati || 15 ||
commentary: The vāta type of adhimantha, when unattended, causes severe pain ultimately resulting in loss of vision. This condition is called Hatādhimantha.

sanskrit_text: वातपर्यायः - भ्रुवोर्नेत्रयोर्वेदना । शुष्काक्षिपाकः - वातरक्तजः । अन्यतोवातः - न्यञ्चनादिषु वातः । आम्लाध्युषितम् - आम्लात् नेत्रश्यावरागदाहशोफस्रावः । सिरोत्पातः - सिरारागः । सिराप्रहर्षः - सिरोत्पातजः । सव्रणशुक्लम् - कृष्णे सूचीवद्व्रणः । अव्रणशुक्लम् - शुक्लवर्णम् । अक्षिपाकात्ययः - शुक्लावरणम् । अजकाजातम् - अजापुरीषवत् शुक्रम् ॥ १६-२८ ॥
transliteration: Vātaparyāyaḥ - bhruvornetrayorvedanā | Śuṣkākṣipākaḥ - vātaraktajaḥ | Anyatovātaḥ - nyañcanādiṣu vātaḥ | Āmlādhyuṣitam - āmlāt netraśyāvarāgadāhaśophasrāvaḥ | Sirotpātaḥ - sirārāgaḥ | Sirāpraharsaḥ - sirotpātajaḥ | Savraṇaśuklam - kṛṣṇe sūcīvadvraṇaḥ | Avraṇaśuklam - śuklavarṇam | Akṣipākātyayaḥ - śuklāvaraṇam | Ajakājātam - ajāpurīṣavat śukram || 16-28 ||
commentary: Vātaparyāya - severe pain alternately in eyebrows and eyes. Śuṣkākṣipāka - dry ulceration of the eye caused by vāta-rakta. Anyatovāta - pain in the centre of eyebrows and eyes due to vāta from other parts. Āmlādhyuṣita - bluish, reddened, ulcerated with burning, oedema and discharge caused by sour foods. Sirotpāta - coppery colour of veins in the eye. Sirāpraharsa - coppery discharge, vision loss. Savraṇaśukla - corneal ulcer looking like needle prick. Avraṇaśukla - corneal opacity. Akṣipākātyaya - white covering of cornea. Ajakājātam - goat-dung like corneal growth.

sanskrit_text: तिमिरं - दृष्टिमण्डलगतं दोषैः । प्रथमपटले - रूपाण्यव्यक्तानि पश्यति । द्वितीये - मक्षिकादीन् पश्यति । तृतीये - ऊर्ध्वं पश्यति नाधः । चतुर्थे - सर्वान्ध्यम् । लिङ्गनाशः - दृष्टिनाशः । काचः - कृष्णमण्डले मलम् । नीलिका - नीलवर्णम् ॥ २९-४० ॥
transliteration: Timiraṃ - dṛṣṭimaṇḍalagataṃ doṣaiḥ | Prathamapaṭale - rūpāṇyavyaktāni paśyati | Dvitīye - makṣikādīn paśyati | Tṛtīye - ūrdhvaṃ paśyati nādhaḥ | Caturthe - sarvāndhyam | Liṅganāśaḥ - dṛṣṭināśaḥ | Kācaḥ - kṛṣṇamaṇḍale malam | Nīlikā - nīlavarṇam || 29-40 ||
commentary: Timira - disease of the vision caused by doṣas. In the first layer - sees objects unclearly. In the second layer - sees flies, mosquitoes etc. In the third layer - sees upward but not downward. In the fourth layer - complete blindness. Liṅganāśa - loss of vision. Kāca - opacity in the cornea. Nīlikā - bluish colour of the eye.

sanskrit_text: वातिके - चलं रूक्षमरुणम् । पैत्तिके - पीतं सूर्येन्द्रचापसदृशम् । कफजे - श्वेतं स्निग्धं स्थिरम् । रक्तजे - रक्तवर्णम् । सन्निपातिके - चित्ररूपम् । परिम्लायिकाच - पित्तरक्तजम् ॥ ४१-४७ ॥
transliteration: Vātike - calaṃ rūkṣamaruṇam | Paittike - pītaṃ sūryendracāpasadṛśam | Kaphaje - śvetaṃ snigdhaṃ sthiram | Raktaje - raktavarṇam | Sannipātike - citrarūpam | Parimlāyikāca - pittaraktajam || 41-47 ||
commentary: In vāta predominant timira - mobile, rough and reddish. In pitta - yellow, like sun and rainbow. In kapha - white, unctuous and stable. In rakta - blood red. In sannipāta - multi-coloured. Parimlāyikāca - caused by pitta-rakta, yellowish-blue.

sanskrit_text: लिङ्गनाशः षड्विधः । वातिके रक्तः । पैत्तिके नीलः । कफजे श्वेतः । रक्तजे रक्तः । सन्निपातिके चित्रः । परिम्लायी पित्तरक्तजः ॥ ४८-५४ ॥
transliteration: Liṅganāśaḥ ṣaḍvidhaḥ | Vātike raktaḥ | Paittike nīlaḥ | Kaphaje śvetaḥ | Raktaje raktaḥ | Sannipātike citraḥ | Parimlāyī pittaraktajaḥ || 48-54 ||
commentary: Liṅganāśa is of six types based on colour. Vātika - red. Paittika - blue. Kaphaja - white. Raktaja - blood red. Sannipātika - multi-coloured. Parimlāyī - caused by pitta-rakta, yellowish-blue.

sanskrit_text: पित्तविदग्धदृष्टिः - पीतदर्शनम् । श्लेष्मविदग्धदृष्टिः - श्वेतदर्शनम् । धूमदर्शी - धूमदर्शनम् । ह्रस्वजाड्यम् - सूक्ष्मदर्शनम् । नकुलान्ध्यम् - नकुलाक्षिसदृशम् ॥ ५५-५९ ॥
transliteration: Pittavidagdhadṛṣṭiḥ - pītadarśanam | Śleṣmavidagdhadṛṣṭiḥ - śvetadarśanam | Dhūmadarśī - dhūmadarśanam | Hrasvajāḍyam - sūkṣmadarśanam | Nakulāndhyam - nakulākṣisadṛśam || 55-59 ||
commentary: Pittavidagdhadṛṣṭi - sees everything yellow (day blindness). Śleṣmavidagdhadṛṣṭi - sees everything white (night blindness). Dhūmadarśī - sees everything like smoke. Hrasvajāḍya - sees small objects with difficulty (presbyopia). Nakulāndhya - eye looks like a mongoose (lenticular opacity).

sanskrit_text: गाम्भीरिका - वातेन दृष्टिसंकोचः । आगन्तुजः - सनिमित्तः अनिमित्तश्च । सनिमित्ते - शिरःशूलजः । अनिमित्ते - देवादिदर्शनात् दृष्टिनाशः ॥ ६०-६४ ॥
transliteration: Gāmbhīrikā - vātena dṛṣṭisaṃkocaḥ | Āgantujaḥ - sanimittaḥ animittaśca | Sanimitte - śiraḥśūlajaḥ | Animitte - devādidarśanāt dṛṣṭināśaḥ || 60-64 ||
commentary: Gāmbhīrikā - constriction of vision caused by vāta. Āgantuja linganāsa is of two types: sanimitta (with specific cause) - caused by head-ache; animitta (without specific cause) - loss of vision by seeing extraordinary objects like Gods etc.

sanskrit_text: प्रस्तार्यर्म - श्यावरक्तं तनु विस्तारि । शुक्लार्म - श्वेतं मृदु । रक्तार्म - पद्मपत्राभम् । अधिमांसार्म - यकृद्वर्णम् बहलम् । स्नाय्वर्म - स्थिरं मांसलम् । शुक्तिका - श्यावं मांसनिभम् । अर्जुन - शशशोणितसदृशम् । पिष्टक - पिष्टलेपवत् ॥ ६५-६८ ॥
transliteration: Prastāryarma - śyāvaraktaṃ tanu vistāri | Śuklārma - śvetaṃ mṛdu | Raktārma - padmapatrābham | Adhimāṃsārma - yakṛdvarṇam bahalam | Snāyvarma - sthiraṃ māṃsalam | Śuktikā - śyāvaṃ māṃsanibham | Arjuna - śaśaśoṇitasadṛśam | Piṣṭaka - piṣṭalepavat || 65-68 ||
commentary: Prastāryarma - blackish-red thin spreading layer on white part. Śuklārma - white soft layer on white part. Raktārma - like a lotus petal. Adhimāṃsārma - liver-coloured, thick. Snāyvarma - hard, muscular, dry. Śuktikā - blackish spots like muscle. Arjuna - like rabbit's blood. Piṣṭaka - paste-like coating.

sanskrit_text: सिराजालम् - सिराजालवत् । सिराजपिडका - शुक्ले पिडकाः । बलासग्रथितम् - जलबिन्दुसदृशम् । पूयालस - सन्धौ पूयस्रावः । श्लेष्मोपनाह - सन्धौ शोफः । पूयस्रावः - सन्निपातजः । श्लेष्मस्रावः - श्वेतः सान्द्रः । रक्तस्रावः - रक्तजः । पित्तस्रावः - हरिद्राभः । पर्वणी - कृष्णशुक्लसन्धौ शोफः । अलजी - तत्रैव । कृमिग्रन्थिः - कण्डूः । उत्सङ्गिणी - वर्त्मबाह्ये पिडका । कुम्भिका - वर्त्मान्ते पिडकाः । पोथकी - स्राविण्यः । वर्त्मशर्करा - वर्त्मनि शर्करा । अर्शोवर्त्म - एर्वारुबीजवत् । शुष्कार्शः - शुष्काः । आञ्जननामिका - ताम्रा । बहुलवर्त्म - बहुपिडकम् । वर्त्मबन्धक - निमीलनाभावः । क्लिष्टवर्त्म - रक्तपित्तजम् । वर्त्मकर्दम - क्लिन्नम् । श्याववर्त्म - श्यावम् । प्रक्लिन्नवर्त्म - क्लिन्नम् । अपक्लिन्नवर्त्म - सश्लेष्मम् । वातहतवर्त्म - निमेषाभावः । वर्त्मार्बुदम् - वर्त्मन्यर्बुदम् । निमेष - निमेषातिरेकः । शोणितार्शः - रक्तं स्रवति । लगन - कठिनः । बिसवर्त्म - बिससदृशम् । कुञ्चन - वर्त्मसंकोचः ॥ ६९-७७ ॥
transliteration: Sirājālam - sirājālavat | Sirājapiḍakā - śukle piḍakāḥ | Balāsagrathitam - jalabindusadṛśam | Pūyālasa - sandhau pūyasrāvaḥ | Śleṣmopanāha - sandhau śophaḥ | Pūyasrāvaḥ - sannipātajaḥ | Śleṣmasrāvaḥ - śvetaḥ sāndraḥ | Raktasrāvaḥ - raktajaḥ | Pittasrāvaḥ - haridrābhaḥ | Parvaṇī - kṛṣṇaśuklasandhau śophaḥ | Alajī - tatraiva | Kṛmigranthiḥ - kaṇḍūḥ | Utsaṅgiṇī - vartmabāhye piḍakā | Kumbhikā - vartmānte piḍakāḥ | Pothakī - srāviṇyaḥ | Vartmaśarkarā - vartmani śarkarā | Arśovartma - ervārubījavat | Śuṣkārśaḥ - śuṣkāḥ | Āñjananāmikā - tāmrā | Bahulavartma - bahupiḍakam | Vartmabandhaka - nimīlanābhāvaḥ | Kliṣṭavartma - raktapittajam | Vartmakardama - klinnam | Śyāvavartma - śyāvam | Praklinnavartma - klinnam | Apaklinnavartma - saśleṣmam | Vātahatavartma - nimeṣābhāvaḥ | Vartmārbudam - vartmanyarbudam | Nimeṣa - nimeṣātirekaḥ | Śoṇitārśaḥ - raktaṃ sravati | Lagana - kaṭhinaḥ | Bisavartma - bisasadṛśam | Kuñcana - vartmasaṃkocaḥ || 69-77 ||
commentary: Various diseases of the eye and eye-lids are described including Sirājāla (circumciliary congestion), Sirājapiḍakā (scleritis), Balāsagrathita (episcleritis), Pūyālasa (dacryo-cystitis), Śleṣmopanāha (pinguncula), types of discharge (pūya, śleṣma, rakta, pitta), Parvaṇī (phlyctenular conjunctivitis), Alajī, Kṛmigranthi (blepharitis), Utsaṅgiṇī and Kumbhikā (hardeolum), Pothakī (trachoma), Vartmaśarkarā (follicular conjunctivitis), Arśovartma, Śuṣkārśa (polyps), Āñjananāmikā (stye), Bahulavartma (angio neurotic oedema), Vartmabandhaka, Kliṣṭavartma (allergic conjunctivitis), Vartmakardama (blepharitis), Śyāvavartma (traumatic lid), Praklinna and Apaklinna vartma, Vātahatavartma (lagophthalmitis), Vartmārbuda (tumour of lid), Nimeṣa (tics), Śoṇitārśa (papilloma), Lagana (lid-tumor), Bisavartma, and Kuñcana.

sanskrit_text: वातपित्तकफसन्निपातरक्तक्षयकृमिसूर्यावर्तानन्तवातार्धावभेदशङ्खकाः । एकादश सिरोरोगाः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Vātapittakaphasannipātaraktakṣayakṛmisūryāvartānantavātārdhāvabhedaśaṅkhakāḥ | Ekādaśa sirorogāḥ || 1 ||
commentary: Śirorogas (Diseases of the head) occur due to Vāta, Pitta, Kapha, Sannipāta, Rakta, Kṣaya (emaciation/pthisis), Krimi (worms), Sūryāvarta (Sinusitis), Anantavāta (Trigeminal neuralgia), Ardhāvabhedaka (migrane) and Śaṅkhaka (encephalitis) (Thus there are eleven diseases that affect the head).

sanskrit_text: वातिके - अनिमित्तरुजा निशि चातिमात्रम् । बन्धोपतापाभ्यां शाम्यति । पैत्तिके - अङ्गारचितमिव शिरः । धूमायति चाक्षिनासिकम् । रात्रौ शैत्यादुपशाम्यति । कफजे - कफोपदिग्धं गुरु स्तब्धं शीतं सूनाक्षिकुटम् ॥ २-४ ॥
transliteration: Vātike - animittarujā niśi cātimātram | Bandhopatāpābhyāṃ śāmyati | Paittike - aṅgāracitamiva śiraḥ | Dhūmāyati cākṣināsikam | Rātrau śaityād upaśāmyati | Kaphaje - kaphopadigdhaṃ guru stabdhaṃ śītaṃ sūnākṣikuṭam || 2-4 ||
commentary: Vātaja śiroroga - severe headache without reason, increases at night, palliates by bandage and fomentation. Pittaja - head feels like covered with burning coal, fumes from eyes and nose, palliates at night due to cold. Kaphaja - head feels coated with kapha, heavy, rigid, cold, swollen eye-sack.

sanskrit_text: रक्तजे - पित्तलिङ्गं स्पर्शासहत्वम् । क्षयजे - शिरोऽभितापः क्षयात् । कृमिजे - शिरसि सूचीवेदना कृमिगतिः । पूयस्रावश्च नासिकया ॥ ५-७ ॥
transliteration: Raktaje - pittaliṅgaṃ sparśāsahatvam | Kṣayaje - śiro'bhitāpaḥ kṣayāt | Kṛmije - śirasi sūcīvedanā kṛmigatiḥ | Pūyasrāvaśca nāsikayā || 5-7 ||
commentary: Raktaja - pitta symptoms with inability to bear touch. Kṣayaja - headache due to depletion of blood and kapha. Kṛmija - needle-like pain in head, movement of worms, discharge of pus from nose.

sanskrit_text: सूर्यावर्ते - सूर्योदयात् रुक्प्रवृत्तिः । सूर्यास्ते चोपशाम्यति । सर्वदोषजः कृच्छ्रतमः ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration: Sūryāvarte - sūryodayāt rukpravṛttiḥ | Sūryāste copaśāmyati | Sarvadoṣajaḥ kṛcchratamaḥ || 8 ||
commentary: In Sūryāvarta, pain starts with sunrise and increases, and subsides with sunset. It is caused by all doṣas and is very difficult to cure.

sanskrit_text: अनन्तवाते - मन्याग्रीवयोः रुक् । नेत्रभ्रूशङ्खेषु च । गण्डकम्पो हनुग्रहश्च । त्रिदोषजः ॥ ९-१० ॥
transliteration: Anantavāte - manyāgrīvayoḥ ruk | Netrabhrūśaṅkheṣu ca | Gaṇḍakampo hanugrahaśca | Tridoṣajaḥ || 9-10 ||
commentary: In Anantavāta, there is pain in the sides of the neck and back of neck, spreading to eyes, eyebrows and temples. There is trembling of cheeks and lockjaw. Caused by tridoṣa.

sanskrit_text: अर्धावभेदके - रूक्षाध्यशनाजीर्णावश्यातिप्रसङ्गवेगविधारणव्यायामैः । वातः कफेन वार्धं शिरोऽर्धं गृह्णाति । तत्र भ्रूनेत्रकर्णशङ्खललाटेषु तीव्रा रुक् । छेदनमन्थनसदृशी । दृष्टिश्रुतिहानिकरम् ॥ ११-१३ ॥
transliteration: Ardhāvabhedake - rūkṣādhyaśanājīrṇāvaśyātiprasaṅgavegavidhāraṇavyāyāmaiḥ | Vātaḥ kaphena vārdhaṃ śiro'rdhaṃ gṛhṇāti | Tatra bhrūnetrakarṇaśaṅkhalalāṭeṣu tīvrā ruk | Chedanamanthanasadṛśī | Dṛṣṭiśrutihānikaram || 11-13 ||
commentary: Ardhāvabhedaka is caused by dry foods, over eating, indigestion, fog, excessive coitus, suppression of urges, physical strain. Vāta, alone or with kapha, occupies half the head causing severe pain in eyebrows, eyes, ears, temples and forehead. Pain is like cutting or churning. Can damage vision and hearing.

sanskrit_text: शङ्खके - रक्तं पित्तं वातश्च शङ्खौ प्राप्य तीव्रशूलदाहरागशोफान् कुर्वन्ति । स शोफः शिरःकण्ठं गृह्णाति । त्रिरात्रेण हन्ति । त्र्यहं चिकित्सेत् ॥ १४-१५ ॥
transliteration: Śaṅkhake - raktaṃ pittaṃ vātaśca śaṅkhau prāpya tīvraśūladāharāgaśophān kurvanti | Sa śophaḥ śiraḥkaṇṭhaṃ gṛhṇāti | Trirātreṇa hanti | Tryahaṃ cikitset || 14-15 ||
commentary: In Śaṅkhaka, vitiated rakta, pitta and vāta take shelter in the temples causing severe pain, burning, redness and swelling. The swelling spreads to head and throat and kills within three nights. Treatment should be attempted within three days.

sanskrit_text: प्रदरश्चतुर्विधः श्लेष्मपित्तवातसन्निपातैः । विरुद्धमद्याजीर्णाध्यशनातिकर्शनातिसङ्गमातिप्रवहनातिभाराभिघातशोकशयनैः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Pradaraścaturvidhaḥ śleṣmapittavātasannipātaiḥ | Viruddhamadyājīrṇādhyaśanātikarśanātisaṅgamāt ipravahanātibhārābhighātaśokaśayanaiḥ || 1 ||
commentary: Pradara is told to be of four types i.e due to Śleṣma, pitta, vāta and sannipāta, the aetiological factors being indulging in consumption of foods, alcohol, eating before complete digestion of previously consumed food, indigestion, miscarriage, over indulgence in coitus, excessive travelling, excessive walking, grief, emaciation, lifting weights, injuries and sleeping during day time.

sanskrit_text: सर्वमङ्गरुजा सरुजं च ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Sarvamaṅgarujā sarujaṃ ca || 2 ||
commentary: All varieties of āsrgdara are associated with pain all over the body and painfulness.

sanskrit_text: कफजे सामं सपिच्छं पाण्डु पुलाकोदकप्रतिमम् । पित्तजे नीलं पीतं कृष्णं रक्तमुष्णं पित्तार्तिबहुस्रावम् । वातजे विशदं फेनिलमल्पं वातार्ति मांसधोवनप्रतिमम् । सन्निपातजे मधुसर्पिर्हरितालवर्णं मज्जप्रकाशं कुनपगन्धि चासाध्यम् ॥ ३-५ ॥
transliteration: Kaphaje sāmaṃ sapicchaṃ pāṇḍu pulākodakapratimam | Pittaje nīlaṃ pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ raktamuṣṇaṃ pittārtibahusrāvam | Vātaje viśadaṃ phenilamalpaṃ vātārti māṃsadhovanapratimam | Sannipātaje madhusarpirharitālavarṇaṃ majjaprakāśaṃ kunapagandhi cāsādhyam || 3-5 ||
commentary: In kaphaja āsrgdara - discharge is like undigested stuff, sticky, pale, like pulāka water. In pitta type - yellowish-blue, black, red, warm, with pitta troubles, excessive flow. In vāta type - not oily, froathy, less quantity, with vāta disorders, like meat-washed water. Sannipātaja - like mixture of honey and ghee, orpiment colour, looks like bone marrow, putrified smell - incurable.

sanskrit_text: निष्पिच्छदाहरुक् पञ्चरात्रानुबन्धि शशलाक्षारससदृशं यदप्सु न विरज्यते तच्छुद्धमार्तवम् ॥ ६-७ ॥
transliteration: Niṣpicchadāharuk pañcarātrānubandhi śaśalākṣārasasadṛśaṃ yadapsu na virajyate tacchuddhamārtavam || 6-7 ||
commentary: The menstrual blood that flows for five days, once in a month, without stickiness, burning sensation and pain, not excessive and not very less in quantity - is to be known as pure menstruation. It should look like the blood of the rabbit and lac-water solution. It should not stain the cloth on washing with water. Such artava is considered healthy.

sanskrit_text: विंशतिर्योनिव्यापदः प्रदुष्टार्तवबीजदोषदैवोपसंग्रहात् । ता विस्तरेण वक्ष्यामः ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Viṃśatiryoni vyāpadaḥ praduṣṭārtavabījadoṣadaivopasaṅgrahāt | Tā vistareṇa vakṣyāmaḥ || 1 ||
commentary: The number of vaginal diseases is twenty as per the rogasaṅgraha (enumeration of diseases) in Aṣṭodarya (Ca. Sū. 19). They occur in women due to vitiated menstrual blood, due to genetic disorder and also due to unseen (super-human) reasons which please listen in detail.

sanskrit_text: उदावर्ता वन्ध्या विप्लुता परिप्लुता च । वातला चेति पञ्च वातिकाः । तत्रोदावर्तायां फेनिलमार्तवम् । वन्ध्यायामनार्तवम् । विप्लुतायां सततयोनिवेदना । परिप्लुतायां सरुक् च । वातलायां परुषस्तब्धरुक्स्तोदः ॥ २-४ ॥
transliteration: Udāvartā vandhyā viplutā pariplutā ca | Vātalā ceti pañca vātikāḥ | Tatrodāvartāyāṃ phenilamārtavam | Vandhyāyāmanārtavam | Viplutāyāṃ satatayonivedanā | Pariplutāyāṃ saruk ca | Vātalāyāṃ paruṣastabdh arukstodaḥ || 2-4 ||
commentary: Udāvartā - froathy menstrual discharge. Vandhyā - no menses. Viplutā - continuous vaginal pain. Pariplutā - pain during coitus. Vātalā - rough, rigid, painful vagina with pinning sensation. First four also have vāta symptoms.

sanskrit_text: लोहितक्षया वामिनी प्रस्रंसिनी पुत्रघ्नी च । पित्तला चेति पञ्च पैत्तिकाः । तत्र लोहितक्षयायां रक्तक्षयः । वामिन्यां बीजक्षयः । प्रस्रंसिन्यां गर्भाशयपतनम् । पुत्रघ्न्यां गर्भपातः । पित्तलायां दाहपाकज्वरः ॥ ५-७ ॥
transliteration: Lohitakṣayā vāminī prasraṃsinī putraghnī ca | Pittalā ceti pañca paittikāḥ | Tatra lohitakṣayāyāṃ raktakṣayaḥ | Vāminyāṃ bījakṣayaḥ | Prasraṃsinyāṃ garbhāśayapatanam | Putraghnyāṃ garbhapātaḥ | Pittalāyāṃ dāhapākajvaraḥ || 5-7 ||
commentary: Lohitakṣayā - excessive bleeding with burning. Vāminī - semen expelled with vāta. Prasraṃsinī - repeated prolapse, delayed fertility. Putraghnī - repeated abortion. Pittalā - severe burning, ulceration, fever. First four have pitta symptoms.

sanskrit_text: अत्यानन्दा कर्णिनी आचरणा अतिचरणा च । श्लेष्मला चेति पञ्च श्लैष्मिकाः । तत्रात्यानन्दायां तृप्तिर्न लभ्यते । कर्णिन्यां ग्रन्थिः । आचरणायां बीजनाशः । अतिचरणायां बीजनाशः । श्लेष्मलायां पिच्छिलशीतकण्डूः ॥ ८-१० ॥
transliteration: Atyānandā karṇinī ācaraṇā aticaraṇā ca | Śleṣmalā ceti pañca ślaiṣmikāḥ | Tatrātyānandāyāṃ tṛptirna labhyate | Karṇinyāṃ granthiḥ | Ācaraṇāyāṃ bījanāśaḥ | Aticaraṇāyāṃ bījanāśaḥ | Śleṣmalāyāṃ picchilaśītakaṇḍūḥ || 8-10 ||
commentary: Atyānandā - no satiation in coitus. Karṇinī - tumour in vagina caused by śleṣma-rakta. Ācaraṇā - orgasm before male, semen not retained. Aticaraṇā - orgasm after prolonged coitus, semen not retained. Śleṣmalā - sticky, cold, itching vagina. First four have śleṣma symptoms.

sanskrit_text: षण्ढी आण्डाली विवृता सूचीमुखी च । सन्निपातिका चेति पञ्चासाध्याः ॥ ११-१३ ॥
transliteration: Ṣaṇḍhī āṇḍālī vivṛtā sūcīmukhī ca | Sannipātikā ceti pañcāsādhyāḥ || 11-13 ||
commentary: Ṣaṇḍhī - no menstruation, underdeveloped breasts. Āṇḍālī - inflamed due to oversized penis. Vivṛtā - wide opening. Sūcīmukhī - narrow opening. Sannipātikā - symptoms of all three doṣas. All five are incurable.

sanskrit_text: दिवास्वप्नातिकोपातिव्यायामातिसंगमानखदन्ताभिघातैः । दोषाः प्रकुपिता योनौ कन्दं कुर्वन्ति ॥ १-२ ॥
transliteration: Divāsvapnātikopātivyāyāmātisaṅgamanakhadantābhighātaiḥ | Doṣāḥ prakupitā yonau kandaṃ kurvanti || 1-2 ||
commentary: Due to sleeping in day time, excessive anger, strenuous exercise, excessive coitus, injury by nails and teeth the vāta etc., doṣas get aggravated and cause a round shaped abscess in the yoni (vagina) which resemble the shade of pus and blood, is called yonikanda.

sanskrit_text: वातिकं रूक्षं विवर्णं विदीर्णम् । पैत्तिकं दाहरागज्वरम् । कफजं नीलं सकण्डूम् । सन्निपातिकं सर्वलिङ्गम् ॥ ३-४ ॥
transliteration: Vātikaṃ rūkṣaṃ vivarṇaṃ vidīrṇam | Paittikaṃ dāharāgajvaram | Kaphajaṃ nīlaṃ sakaṇḍūm | Sannipātikaṃ sarvaliṅgam || 3-4 ||
commentary: Vātika - dry, discoloured, broken. Paittika - burning, redness, fever. Kaphaja - blue, with itching. Sannipātika - all symptoms.

sanskrit_text: शोकाभिघातादुष्णतीक्ष्णान्नपानैश्च गर्भः पतति । तस्य पूर्वरूपं योनिशोणितदर्शनं सरुजम् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Śokābhighātāduṣṇatīkṣṇānnapānaiśca garbhaḥ patati | Tasya pūrvarūpaṃ yoniśoṇitadarśanaṃ sarujam || 1 ||
commentary: Due to fear, injury, consuming fast and warm foods and drinks, the pregnancy gets dislodged and when it comes out there appears blood in the vaginal canal associated with pain.

sanskrit_text: गर्भस्रावो नाम चतुर्थे मासि द्रवीभूतस्य गर्भस्य स्रवणम् । गर्भपातस्तु पञ्चमे षष्ठे वा मासि स्थिरस्य पतनम् ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Garbhasrāvo nāma caturthe māsi dravībhūtasya garbhasya sravaṇam | Garbhapātastu pañcame ṣaṣṭhe vā māsi sthirasya patanam || 2 ||
