commentary: Until the fourth month after gestation, the pregnancy when disturbed oozes out in the form of liquid - this condition is called 'garbhasrāva' (abortion) and on attaining fifth and sixth months it falls out (in solid form) and such a condition is known as garbhapāta (miscarriage).

sanskrit_text: प्रजाते काले यदि न प्रजायते न च गर्भचेष्टा लभ्यते स मूढगर्भः । तत्र योनिशूलमुदरशूलं मूत्रसङ्गश्च भवति ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Prajāte kāle yadi na prajāyate na ca garbhaceṣṭā labhyate sa mūḍhagarbhaḥ | Tatra yoniśūlamudaraśūlaṃ mūtrasaṅgaśca bhavati || 3 ||
commentary: In appropriate delivery time if the delivery has not occurred and if the child does not show signs of moving out (delivering) such a situation is called mūḍhagarbha. Mūḍha means having lost the movements. There will be pain in the vagina, stomach and retention of urine.

sanskrit_text: स मूढगर्भो बहुधा योनिमार्गमावृत्य तिष्ठति । शिरसोदरपृष्ठपार्श्वैः । एकेन द्वाभ्यां च पाणिभ्याम् । ऊर्ध्वं तिर्यगधश्च शिरसा । एवमष्टौ मूढगर्भाः ॥ ४-५ ॥
transliteration: Sa mūḍhagarbho bahudhā yonimārgamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati | Śirasodarapṛṣṭhapārśvaiḥ | Ekena dvābhyāṃ ca pāṇibhyām | Ūrdhvaṃ tiryagadhaśca śirasā | Evamaṣṭau mūḍhagarbhāḥ || 4-5 ||
commentary: The foetus disturbed by the aggravated vāta, comes out through the vagina in many ways. Some by presentation of head and some by abdomen, some buttock presentation after being dwarfed by folding, by one hand, by two hands, some in reverse direction, some with head downwards and some with side-ward head presentation to the vaginal canal. Thus there are eight types of improper presentation.

sanskrit_text: शङ्कीलकः प्रतिखुरः परिघो बीजकश्चेति चत्वारः ॥ ६ ॥
transliteration: Śaṅkīlakaḥ pratikhuraḥ parigho bījakaśceti catvāraḥ || 6 ||
commentary: The four specific types of mūḍhagarbha are also seen viz., Śaṅkīlaka, Pratikhura, Parigha and Bījaka. The condition in which hands, legs and head presentation appear upwards and the vaginal canal is thus obstructed is called Śaṅkīlaka. When the hands, legs and head are presented out, it is called Pratikhura. The presentation of two hands and head is called Bījaka and when the body or any part is curved, it is called Parigha which obstructs the pathway.

sanskrit_text: अपावृत्तशिराः शीतगात्रा निरपत्रपा । नीलसिरा च मूढगर्भिणी न सिध्यति ॥ ७ ॥
transliteration: Apāvṛttaśirāḥ śītagātrā nirapatrapā | Nīlasirā ca mūḍhagarbhiṇī na sidhyati || 7 ||
commentary: When the pregnant woman is not able to keep her head straight, whose body becomes cool, does not feel shy of her body posture and the veins on her body become bluish, then - the delivery kills her.

sanskrit_text: निष्पन्दं निर्वेदनं नीलं पाण्डु दुर्गन्धनिश्वासं शूनं च मृतगर्भम् ॥ ८ ॥
transliteration: Niṣpandaṃ nirvedanaṃ nīlaṃ pāṇḍu durgandhaniḥśvāsaṃ śūnaṃ ca mṛtagarbham || 8 ||
commentary: When the child is dead inside the uterus (or vaginal canal) the foetal movements and pains are ceased, the body (of the pregnant woman) becomes bluish and pale, the exhalation stinks and there is swelling.

sanskrit_text: जनन्या उपतापैः स्वकर्मभिश्च गर्भो म्रियते ॥ ९ ॥
transliteration: Jananyā upatāpaiḥ svakarmabhiśca garbho mriyate || 9 ||
commentary: Due to the mental and sudden agony of the mother and its own pathological conditions, the garbha dies inside the garbhāśaya.

sanskrit_text: योनिसंवरणं कुक्षिसङ्गो मक्कल्लादयश्च मूढगर्भं हन्ति ॥ १० ॥
transliteration: Yonisaṃvaraṇaṃ kukṣisaṅgo makkallādayaśca mūḍhagarbhaṃ hanti || 10 ||
commentary: Constriction of the vagina, the garbha getting stuck in the abdomen, due to makkalla and other complication kill the woman suffering from mūḍhagarbha.

sanskrit_text: अङ्गमर्दो ज्वरः कम्पस्तृष्णा गौरवं शोफः । कुक्षिशूलमतीसारश्च सूतिकारोगलिङ्गम् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Aṅgamardo jvaraḥ kampastṛṣṇā gauravaṃ śophaḥ | Kukṣiśūlamatīsāraśca sūtikārogaliṅgam || 1 ||
commentary: Pain all over the body, fever, trembling, thirst, heaviness in the body, oedema, pain in the abdomen and diarrhoea are the symptoms of Sūtikāroga.

sanskrit_text: अपथ्याहारविहारैः सूतिका रोगाः सञ्जायन्ते । ते च दुःसाध्याः क्षीणबलमांसाग्नित्वात् ॥ २-४ ॥
transliteration: Apathyāhāravihāraiḥ sūtikā rogāḥ sañjāyante | Te ca duḥsādhyāḥ kṣīṇabalamāṃsāgnitvāt || 2-4 ||
commentary: Due to improper handling of the puerperal period, consumption of food that aggravates doṣas, irregular dietetic practices and eating before digestion of the previously ingested food, the diseases which occur are considered to be very serious. Due to depleted musculature, strength and digestive fire, these (simple looking) diseases become difficult for cure and further complications also arise.

sanskrit_text: दोषाः स्तनौ प्राप्य मांसं रक्तं च विदूष्य स्तनरोगान् जनयन्ति ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Doṣāḥ stanau prāpya māṃsaṃ raktaṃ ca vidūṣya stanarogān janayanti || 1 ||
commentary: The doṣas reaches the two breasts of the women which are either with milk or without milk and on vitiating the muscle and blood, there arise disease of the breasts.

sanskrit_text: त एते स्तनरोगाः पञ्चापि बाह्यविद्रधिलिङ्गैः समानलिङ्गाः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Ta ete stanarogāḥ pañcāpi bāhyavidradhiliṅgaiḥ samānaliṅgāḥ || 2 ||
commentary: The symptomatology of all the five stanarogah (diseases of the breast) are similar to all bāhya vidradhi (external abscess) except raktaja vidradhi.

sanskrit_text: यथा शुक्रं सर्वशरीरस्थमपि न दृश्यते । स्मरणदर्शनस्पर्शश्रवणैः स्त्रीणां प्रवर्तते । एवं स्तन्यं च मनसा प्रवर्तते ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Yathā śukraṃ sarvaśarīrasthamapi na dṛśyate | Smaraṇadarśanasparśaśravaṇaiḥ strīṇāṃ pravartate | Evaṃ stanyaṃ ca manasā pravartate || 1 ||
commentary: Though it exists all over the body, the semen is not seen on cutting any part of the body. The same ejaculates out by the pleasure caused by appearance, remembering, hearing the signs of her presence, touch of an young lady of one's own liking. The reason here for this is - pleasant condition of the mind. Since it is originated from the āhārarasa, the breast milk in the women is also like this. By touch of the progeny, by looking at them, remembering them holding them-the breastmilk due to mental attachment-discharges out from the breasts.

sanskrit_text: वातेन दुष्टं कषायं प्लवते । पित्तेन दुष्टं कट्वम्ललवणं पीतरेखम् । कफेन दुष्टं गुरु पिच्छिलं सीदति ॥ २-३ ॥
transliteration: Vātena duṣṭaṃ kaṣāyaṃ plavate | Pittena duṣṭaṃ kaṭvamlalavaṇaṃ pītarekhām | Kaphena duṣṭaṃ guru picchilaṃ sīdati || 2-3 ||
commentary: The breast-milk vitiated by vāta tastes kaṣāya (Astringent) and floats on water; due to pitta affliction, it tastes kaṭu (pungent), sour and salty and putting in water shows yellowish lines and that breast-milk afflicted by kapha is heavy and sticky and sinks in water.

sanskrit_text: अविवर्णं मधुरं विशदं सलिले चैकीभवति शुद्धं स्तन्यम् ॥ ४ ॥
transliteration: Avivarṇaṃ madhuraṃ viśadaṃ salile caikībhavati śuddhaṃ stanyam || 4 ||
commentary: The pure (unvitiated) breastmilk is in pale colour, sweet in taste, not having any particular colour, clear, and gets mixed up with water (readily).

sanskrit_text: वातदुष्टस्तन्यपानाद्वातरोगी स्याद्बालः । पित्तदुष्टात् पित्तरोगी । कफदुष्टात् कफरोगी । द्वन्द्वदुष्टात् द्वन्द्वरोगी । सन्निपातदुष्टात् सन्निपातरोगी ॥ १-३ ॥
transliteration: Vāta duṣṭa stanya pānād vātarogī syādbālaḥ | Pitta duṣṭāt pitta rogī | Kapha duṣṭāt kapha rogī | Dvandva duṣṭāt dvandva rogī | Sannipāta duṣṭāt sannipāta rogī || 1-3 ||
commentary: When the child is fed with breast-milk that is vitiated by vāta, he suffers from vāta-disorders. On being fed with breast-milk that is vitiated by pitta, the child suffers from pitta diseases. On feeding with the breast-milk which is vitiated by kapha, it suffers from kapha-diseases. When the breast-milk is afflicted by two of the tridoṣa, those two particular related symptoms are seen in the child and when it is tridoṣa affected milk, the child suffers from all the symptomatology of all three of the doṣas.

sanskrit_text: बालस्य रुदितेन वेदनाबलं ज्ञायते । यदङ्गं स्पृशति तत्र वेदना । यत्र स्पर्शासहत्वं तत्र वेदना । मीलिताक्षो ज्ञेयः शिरोरोगी । विण्मूत्रसङ्गच्छर्दिस्तननाशनोदरशब्दानाहपृष्ठनमनोदरोन्नमनैश्च कोष्ठगतरोगः ॥ ४-७ ॥
transliteration: Bālasya ruditena vedanābalaṃ jñāyate | Yadaṅgaṃ spṛśati tatra vedanā | Yatra sparśāsahatvaṃ tatra vedanā | Mīlitākṣo jñeyaḥ śirorogī | Viṇmūtrasaṅgacchardistananāśanodaraśabdānāhapṛṣṭhanamanodaronnamanaiśca koṣṭhagatarogaḥ || 4-7 ||
commentary: The severity of the pain the child experiences is known by the intensity of its cry. The particular place of the body repeatedly touched by the child is to be known as the site of pain and also the place where the child can not withstand the touch is also to be recognised as site of pain. If the child keeps its eyes closed, it should be known that it is suffering from head-ache. On seeing the symptoms of constipation, vomittings, biting the nipples of the mother, noise in the intestines, bloating of the abdomen, bending the back and raising the stomach, it should be understood as the child is suffering from some abdominal disorder.

sanskrit_text: कुकूनकं नाम वर्त्मरोगो बालानाम् । तत्र कण्डूः स्रावश्च मुहुर्मुहुः । न च वर्त्मोन्मीलनक्षमः ॥ ८-९ ॥
transliteration: Kukūnakaṃ nāma vartmarogo bālānām | Tatra kaṇḍūḥ srāvaśca muhurmuhuḥ | Na ca vartmonmīlanakṣamaḥ || 8-9 ||
commentary: Due to intake of vitiated breast-milk, the child is afflicted by a disease called Kukūnaka in the eye-lids. By this, there is repeated itching sensation and discharge in that particular eye. The child cannot bear the sight of sun-light and cannot lift the eye-lid.

sanskrit_text: गर्भिणीस्तन्यपानात् कासमन्दाग्निछर्दिभ्रमकर्शनारोचकतन्द्रानाहयुक्तः परिगर्भिकाख्यो रोगः ॥ १०-११ ॥
transliteration: Garbhiṇīstanyapānāt kāsamandāgnichardibhramakarśanārocakatandrānāhayuktaḥ parigarbhikākhyo rogaḥ || 10-11 ||
commentary: By drinking the breast-milk of a pregnant woman, the child gets a disease called Parigarbhikā which is characterised by cough, depleted digestive fire, vomiting, dizziness, emaciation, anorexia, giddiness and bloating of the abdomen.

sanskrit_text: संचितः कफस्तालुनि प्रकुपितस्तालुकण्टकं करोति । तत्र तालुपातः स्तन्याद्वेषः पानासामर्थ्यमतिसारस्तृष्णा नेत्रकण्ठमुखरुक् ग्रीवादुर्धारता च ॥ १२-१३ ॥
transliteration: Saṃcitaḥ kaphastāluni prakupitastālukaṇṭakaṃ karoti | Tatra tālupātaḥ stanyādveṣaḥ pānāsāmarthyamatisārastṛṣṇā netrakaṇṭhamukharuk grīvādhurāratā ca || 12-13 ||
commentary: When kapha accumulated in the palate gets aggravated, it causes Tālukaṇṭaka due to which depression of the Talu pradesha takes place. There will be protrusion of palate, aversion towards breast, drinking with difficulty, loose motions, thirst, pain in eye, throat and mouth and not being able to straighten the neck.

sanskrit_text: वस्तिशिरोजो विसर्पः पद्मवर्णो महापद्मसंज्ञः । स त्रिदोषजः । शङ्खाभ्यां हृदयं गच्छति । हृदयाद्वा गुदम् ॥ १४ ॥
transliteration: Vastiśirojo visarpaḥ padmavarṇo mahāpadmasaṃjñaḥ | Sa tridoṣajaḥ | Śaṅkhābhyāṃ hṛdayaṃ gacchati | Hṛdayādvā gudam || 14 ||
commentary: The visarpa (erysipelas) occurring in children in the bladder and head region is considered as a lethal disease. Since it is of the lotus (red) colour, it is named as Mahāpadma. This is caused by tridoṣa. This spreads from the temples to the heart region or from heart region to the anus.

sanskrit_text: अजगल्लिका च अहिपूतना च क्षुद्ररोगेषु उक्ते ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration: Ajagallikā ca ahipūtanā ca kṣudrarogeṣu ukte || 15 ||
commentary: Ajagallikā and ahipūtanā are described in kṣudra roga (minor-diseases) chapter.

sanskrit_text: ज्वरादयो बालानां वयस्कवद् ज्ञेयाः ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration: Jvarādayo bālānāṃ vayaskavad jñeyāḥ || 16 ||
commentary: The experts should know the fever etc., disease occurring children, in the same manner as they are seen in the elders.

sanskrit_text: ग्रहैर्गृहीतस्य बालस्य सामान्यलिङ्गम् - उद्विजते त्रस्यति रोदिति कण्डूयति मातरम् । ऊर्ध्वं निरीक्षते दन्तान् खादति विरुतं करोति । जृम्भते भ्रूदन्तौष्ठान् क्षिपति फेनिललालं वमति । कृशो भवति रात्रौ जागर्ति शूनाक्षो भिन्नविट्कः भिन्नस्वरः । मांसशोणितगन्धी च यथापूर्वं न भुङ्क्ते ॥ १७-१९ ॥
transliteration: Grahairgṛhītasya bālasya sāmānyaliṅgam - Udvijate trasyati roditi kaṇḍūyati mātaram | Ūrdhvaṃ nirīkṣate dantān khādati virutaṃ karoti | Jṛmbhate bhrūdantauṣṭhān kṣipati phenilalālaṃ vamati | Kṛśo bhavati rātrau jāgarti śūnākṣo bhinna viṭkaḥ bhinna svaraḥ | Māṃsaśoṇitagandhī ca yathāpūrvaṃ na bhuṅkte || 17-19 ||
commentary: The common symptomatology of the children who are afflicted by the graha - demons is as follows - At every moment, the child gets agitated, gets terrified, weeps repeatedly, scratches itself or the mother, looks upwards, bites the teeth, makes typical sounds, keeps yawning, keeps constricting the eye-brows, teeth and lips, brings out froathing saliva from the mouth. It becomes emaciated, remains awake during nights. Its eyes get swollen; suffers from diarrhoea and shrillness in the voice; stinks like meat and blood and does not eat as earlier (to this affliction).

sanskrit_text: एकाक्षिस्रावी एकपार्श्वस्पन्दनकम्पी । ऊर्ध्वं पश्यति वक्त्रं वक्रयति । रक्तगन्धी दन्तान् खादति । भीतो भवति । स्तन्यं नेच्छति । मन्दं रोदिति स्कन्दग्रहगृहीतः ॥ २०-२१ ॥
transliteration: Ekākṣisrāvī ekapārśvaspandanakampī | Ūrdhvaṃ paśyati vaktraṃ vakrayati | Raktagandhī dantān khādati | Bhīto bhavati | Stanyaṃ necchati | Mandaṃ roditi skandagrahagṛhītaḥ || 20-21 ||
commentary: One of the eye has discharge and on one side the body keeps pulsating and shaking in the child. It looks upwards as if awaiting for somebody, keeps the face curved, its body stinks like blood, bites the teeth, fears, does not like the breast feeding and weeps mildly when the skandagraha takes hold of the child.

sanskrit_text: मूर्छितः फेनिललालं वमति । प्रत्यागते चेतसि सुमहद् रोदिति । पूयशोणितगन्धी च स्कन्दापस्मारः ॥ २२ ॥
transliteration: Mūrchitaḥ phenilalālaṃ vamati | Pratyāgate cetasi sumahad roditi | Pūyaśoṇitagandhī ca skandāpasmāraḥ || 22 ||
commentary: The child gets unconscious and vomits froathy saliva, weeps loudly on getting back to senses, and its body stinks like pus and blood - this condition is called Skandāpasmāra.

sanskrit_text: स्रस्ताङ्गो भयचकितः । विहङ्गगन्धी । स्रावव्रणैः परिपूर्णः । स्फोटैश्च दग्धाकृतिभिः शकुनिग्रहेण गृहीतः ॥ २३ ॥
transliteration: Srastāṅgo bhayacakitaḥ | Vihaṅgagandhī | Srāvavraṇaiḥ paripūrṇaḥ | Sphoṭaiśca dagdhākṛtibhiḥ śakunigraheṇa gṛhītaḥ || 23 ||
commentary: All the bodily limbs become loosened, it gets terrified, stinks like a bird, the whole body is full of wounds with discharge. The body is full of opened vesicles with ulceration and burning sensation when the child is gripped by Śakunigraha.

sanskrit_text: रेवतीग्रहः पूतना अन्धपूतना शीतपूतना मुखमण्डिका नैगमेषश्च । तेषां लिङ्गानि यथाक्रमम् - व्रणस्फोटपूर्णं पङ्कगन्धि । अतीसारज्वरदाहयुतम् । अतीसारज्वरतृषाक्रोधनातिरोदनानिद्राक्षोभाः । छर्दिकासज्वरतृष्णास्नेहगन्धितिरोदनस्तन्यद्वेषातीसाराः । शरीरकम्पकासकर्शननेत्रविकारदुर्गन्धिच्छर्द्यतीसाराः । मुखमण्डिकायां प्रसन्नवदनः सुवर्णः सिरापूर्णो मूत्रगन्धी च बह्वाशी । छर्द्यल्पकम्पशोषतृष्णामूर्च्छादुर्गन्ध्यूर्ध्वदर्शनदन्तखादनाः नैगमेषे । यस्तु स्तन्यद्वेषी मुहुर्मूर्च्छति सर्वग्रहलिङ्गयुक्तः सोऽल्पेन कालेन म्रियते ॥ २४-३० ॥
transliteration: Revatīgrahaḥ pūtanā andhapūtanā śītapūtanā mukhamandikā naigameśaśca | Teṣāṃ liṅgāni yathākramam - vraṇasphoṭapūrṇaṃ paṅkagandhi | Atisārajvaradāhayutam | Atisārajvaratṛṣākrodhanātir odananidrākṣobhāḥ | Chardikāsajvaratṛṣṇāsnehagandhitirodanastanyadveṣātisārāḥ | Śarīrakampakāsakarśananetravikāradurgandhichard yatīsārāḥ | Mukhamandikāyāṃ prasannavadanaḥ suvarṇaḥ sirāpūrṇo mūtragandhī ca bahvāśī | Chardyalkampakaśoṣatṛṣṇāmūrcchādurgandhyūrdhvadarśanadantakhādanāḥ naigameśe | Yastu stanyadveṣī muhurmūrcchati sarva grahaliṅgayuktaḥ so'lpena kālena mriyate || 24-30 ||
commentary: The body of a child becomes dirty with full of wounds and bullae; Blood oozes with stinking smell that is similar to mud; it has diarrhoea, fever and burning sensation, when the Revatīgraha holds that particular child. Diarrhoea, fever, thirst, cross looks, intense weeping, lack of sleep and agitation are seen in the child when it is gripped by Pūtanā graha. Vomiting, cough, fever thirst, stinking like fat, intense weeping, disliking the breast-milk and diarrhoea are the signs and symptoms of the child gripped by Andhapūtanā. When the child is held by Śītapūtanā, there will be trembling of the body, cough, emaciation, eye-problems, unnatural smell in the body, vomiting and diarrhoea. The child afflicted by Mukhamandikā has pleasant face with good colour, the body is full of veins (swollen veins); it stinks like urine and the child eats more. There will be vomiting, mild tremors of the body, drying of throat and mouth, syncope, unnatural smell, looking upwards and biting of teeth when the child is gripped by Naigameśa graha. When a child has staring looks, has aversion towards breast-milk, gets syncope repeatedly and has all the symptoms of holding by a particular graha he will be killed with that problem within a short-time.

sanskrit_text: विषं द्विविधं स्थावरं जङ्गमं च । तत्र मूलाद्यात्मकं स्थावरम् । सर्पादिजं जङ्गमम् ॥ १ ॥
transliteration: Viṣaṃ dvividhaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ ca | Tatra mūlādyātmakaṃ sthāvaram | Sarpādijaṃ jaṅgamam || 1 ||
commentary: The Poison is basically categorised into two types viz., Sthāvara (static) and Jaṅgama (mobile). The first one is (obtained from) roots of plants etc., while the second, originates in snakes etc.

sanskrit_text: जङ्गमविषस्य सामान्यलिङ्गम् - निद्रा भ्रमः क्लमो दाहोऽविपाको रोमहर्षः शोफोऽतीसारः ॥ २ ॥
transliteration: Jaṅgamaviṣasya sāmānyaliṅgam - nidrā bhramaḥ klamo dāho'vipāko romaharṣaḥ śopho'tisāraḥ || 2 ||
commentary: The affliction of jaṅgamaviṣa causes sleep, dizziness, fatigue, burning sensation, indigestion, horripilation, oedema and diarrhoea.

sanskrit_text: स्थावरस्य - ज्वरो हिक्का दन्तहर्षः कण्ठग्रहः फेनच्छर्दिररुचिः श्वासो मूर्च्छा च ॥ ३ ॥
transliteration: Sthāvarasya - jvaro hikkā dantaharṣaḥ kaṇṭhagrahaḥ phenacchardiraruciḥ śvāso mūrcchā ca || 3 ||
commentary: The affliction of Sthāvara viṣa causes fever, hiccup, sensitivity of teeth, gripping sensation in the throat, vomiting of froathy saliva, anorexia, dyspnoea and syncope repeatedly.

sanskrit_text: विषदाता लक्ष्यते - वचनैश्चेष्टितैश्चिह्नैः । संक्षिप्तं न ब्रूते । भीतो भ्रमति । विपरीतं वा ब्रूते । आकस्मिकं हसति । अङ्गुलीः स्फोटयति । पद्भ्यां भूमिं लिखति । कम्पते सर्वतो भीतो दीनवदनः । नखैस्तृणादीन् छिनत्ति । आसनासक्तो मुहुर्मुहुरासनं परिवर्तयति ॥ ४-७ ॥
transliteration: Viṣadātā lakṣyate - vacanaiśceṣṭitaiścihnaiḥ | Saṃkṣiptaṃ na brūte | Bhīto bhramati | Viparītaṃ vā brūte | Ākasmikaṃ hasati | Aṅgulīḥ sphoṭayati | Padbhyāṃ bhūmiṃ likhati | Kampate sarvato bhīto dīnavadanaḥ | Nakhaiḥ tṛṇādīn chinatti | Āsanāsakto muhurmuhurāsanaṃ parivartayati || 4-7 ||
commentary: The intelligent physician should identify the Viṣadāta (the one who gives poison to others) by his words, actions and facial gestures. He does not give direct answer to the questions. He is petrified and deludes while explaining. Even if he gives answer it will be irrelevant, he speaks negatively, more than needed and babbles; laughs suddenly, kneads his fingers and scratches on the earth with toes; he trembles and looks at others with fear; his face becomes discoloured, he keeps cutting the grass or something etc., with nails, he gets stuck to the seat keeping the hands on his head and changes the posture and he loses his consciousness.

sanskrit_text: मूलविषेण - पीडनं जल्पनं मूर्च्छा । पत्रविषेण - जृम्भा कम्पः श्वासो मूर्च्छा । फलविषेण - मुष्कशोफो दाहोऽरुचिः । पुष्पविषेण - छर्दिरानाहः श्वासः । त्वक्सारनिर्यासविषेण - मुखदुर्गन्धः पारुष्यं शिरोरुक् । क्षीरविषेण - प्रसेकः फेनिलास्यता । धातुविषेण - हृद्रुक् मूर्च्छा तालुदाहः । एते कालेन घातिनः ॥ ८-१२ ॥
transliteration: Mūlaviṣeṇa - pīḍanaṃ jalpanaṃ mūrcchā | Patraviṣeṇa - jṛmbhā kampaḥ śvāso mūrcchā | Phalaviṣeṇa - muṣkaśopho dāho'ruciḥ | Puṣpaviṣeṇa - chardirānāhaḥ śvāsaḥ | Tvaksāraniryāsaviṣeṇa - mukhadurgandhaḥ pāruṣyaṃ śiroruk | Kṣīraviṣeṇa - prasekaḥ phenilāsyatā | Dhātuviṣeṇa - hṛdruk mūrcchā tāludāhaḥ | Ete kālena ghātinaḥ || 8-12 ||
commentary: Squeezing pain in the body, blabbering and delusion are caused by mūla viṣa (poisonous roots). Patra viṣa (poisonous leaves) causes yawning, shivering, dyspnoea and delusion. Inflammation of the testes, burning sensation and aversion to food is caused by phalaviṣa (poisonous fruits). Vomiting, bloating of the abdomen and dyspnea occur due to puṣpa viṣa (poisonous flower). Tvak-sāra-niryāsa viṣas (poisonous barks, pith and gum-resin) cause bad odour of the mouth, roughness, head-ache and dribbling of phlegm. Froath from the mouth, diarrhoea, and heaviness of the body, are caused by kṣīra viṣa (poisonous latex). Pain in the heart, syncope and burning sensation in the palate occur by dhātuviṣa (metallic poisons). These poisons kill the individuals in due course of time.

sanskrit_text: विषदिग्धेन शस्त्रेण क्षतः क्षिप्रं पच्यते । अस्रावी च भवति । कृष्णं स्रवति क्लिन्नं पूति मांसावदारणम् । तृष्णामूर्च्छाज्वरदाहैश्च युक्तः ॥ १३-१४ ॥
transliteration: Viṣadigdhena śastreṇa kṣataḥ kṣipraṃ pacyate | Asrāvī ca bhavati | Kṛṣṇaṃ sravati klinnam pūti māṃsāvadāraṇam | Tṛṣṇāmūrcchājvaradāhaiśca yuktaḥ || 13-14 ||
commentary: The instantaneous wound caused by the weapon which is applied with poison gets ripened fast, there will be continuous bleeding and the ripening continues very fast, gets blackened, becomes wet, putrified and the withering of flesh takes place from the wound. The patient suffers from thirst, syncope, fever and burning sensation.

sanskrit_text: पीतविट्को धूम्रविट्कः फेनिलास्यः पीतविषः ॥ १५ ॥
transliteration: Pītaviṭko dhūmraviṭkaḥ phenilāsyaḥ pītaviṣaḥ || 15 ||
commentary: If an individual keeps passing stools in yellowish and smoky colour and vomits froath from the mouth, it should be known that he has drunk the poison.

sanskrit_text: भोगी वातिकः । मण्डली पैत्तिकः । राजिलः कफजः । द्व्यन्तरा द्वन्द्वरूपाः ॥ १६ ॥
transliteration: Bhogī vātikaḥ | Maṇḍalī paittikaḥ | Rājilaḥ kaphajaḥ | Dvyantarā dvandvarūpāḥ || 16 ||
commentary: The Bhogī type of snakes are of vāta temperament, maṇḍalī ones are of pitta temperament and rājila are of kapha temperament. By mixture of the quantities of two of these varieties the dvyantara types of snakes are seen which have the temperament of both the corresponding doṣas.

sanskrit_text: भोगिदष्टे कृष्णं वातरुजः । मण्डलीदष्टे पीतं मृदुशोफः पित्तरुजः । राजिलदष्टे स्थिरशोफः पिच्छिलस्रावः पाण्डुः स्निग्धो गाढरक्तस्रावी कफरुजः ॥ १७-१८ ॥
transliteration: Bhogidaṣṭe kṛṣṇaṃ vātarujaḥ | Maṇḍalīdaṣṭe pītaṃ mṛduśophaḥ pittarujaḥ | Rājiladaṣṭe sthiraśophaḥ picchilasrāvaḥ pāṇḍuḥ snigdho gāḍharaktasrāvī kapharujaḥ || 17-18 ||
commentary: The bite of bhogī type of snake is black in colour and causes all vāta-disorders. The bite caused by maṇḍalī is in yellow colour and has soft oedema and also associated with pitta disorders. The bite of Rājila is stable, swollen, with sticky exudation, pale in colour, oily for touch, has thick blood coming out of bite-area and associated with all the Śleṣma-disorders.

sanskrit_text: अश्वत्थदेवकुलश्मशानवल्मीकसन्ध्यारात्रिचतुष्पथभरण्यादिर्क्षेषु सिरामर्मसु च दष्टोऽसाध्यः ॥ १९ ॥
transliteration: Aśvatthadevakulaśmaśānavalmīkasaṃdhyārātricatuṣpathabharaṇyādir kṣeṣu sirāmarmasu ca daṣṭo'sādhyaḥ || 19 ||
commentary: If the snake-bite takes place under a pipul tree, in a temple, in the grave-yard, near the ant-hill, during the dawn and dusk times, in the cross roads, on the days when bharaṇī, ārdrā etc., deadly stars are present and also on the veins and vital parts of the body-that situation is incurable (lethal).

sanskrit_text: अजीर्णपित्तातपतरुणवृद्धक्षुत्क्षतकृशमेहकुष्ठशुष्कदुर्बलगर्भिणां दष्टोऽसाध्यः ॥ २० ॥
transliteration: Ajīrṇapittātapataruṇavṛddhakṣutkṣatakṛśamehakuṣṭhaśuṣkadurbalagarbhiṇāṃ daṣṭo'sādhyaḥ || 20 ||
commentary: If the individual, at the time of snake bite, is in one of these conditions, it becomes difficult for cure - indigestion, pitta affliction, suffering from hot-Sun, early-age, old-age, hunger stricken, emaciated due to injury, suffering with delusion, suffering with skin disease, dryness of the body weakened and in pregnancy.

sanskrit_text: यो न स्रवति छिन्ने न लक्ष्यते पाशबन्धनैः । न हर्षयति शीताम्बुना तमुपेक्षेत् । वक्रास्यः केशस्रस्तो नासाग्रपतितः कण्ठभग्नो रक्तश्यावशोफी हनुस्तम्भी च । लाला वर्तिरूपिणी रक्तं चोर्ध्वाधोमुखान्नासागुदैः स्रवेत् । चतुर्दंष्ट्रनिपातश्च । उन्मत्तोऽतिव्याकुलो हीनस्वरो विवर्णः सारिष्टो दुर्बलो मन्दवेगश्च त्याज्यः ॥ २१-२४ ॥
transliteration: Yo na sravati chinne na lakṣyate pāśabandhanaiḥ | Na harṣayati śītāmbunā tam upekṣet | Vakrāsyaḥ keśasrasto nāsāgrapatitaḥ kaṇṭhabhagno raktasyāvaśophī hanustambhī ca | Lālā vartirūpiṇī raktaṃ cordhvādhomukhānnāsāgudaiḥ sravet | Caturdaṃṣṭranipātaśca | Unmatto'tivyākulo hīnasvaro vivarṇaḥ sāriṣṭo durbalo mandavegaśca tyājyaḥ || 21-24 ||
commentary: When an snake-bitten individual does not bleed on being cut with weapon, does not show any signs on tying tightly with vines and ropes and does not get skintillation by the touch of cold water, he should not be taken for treatment. When the face becomes curved, the hair keeps falling, there is depression of the brim of the nose, suffers from neck problem (not being able to hold the neck straight), the bite area becomes reddish black with inflammation and when there is lockjaw, such patient also should be discarded from treating. If salivation gets solidified and comes out in the form of a wick and blood comes out from the mouth nose and anus and has four marks of snake bite, such an individual also should be left without treating. When the snake-bitten individual becomes insane or gets many complications, the voice becomes very weak, the body becomes discoloured, there are many fatal complications and the natural urges are not passed or becomes very slow-such a person also should not be treated.

sanskrit_text: जीर्णं विषघ्नैर्मन्दीकृतं मन्दाग्निवातातपैर्वा स्वभावतो वा दूषीविषम् ॥ २५ ॥
transliteration: Jīrṇaṃ viṣaghnairmandīkṛtaṃ mandāgnivātātapai rvā svabhāvato vā dūṣīviṣam || 25 ||
commentary: The poison that has become old, made weak by adding antidotes or exposed to mild-fire, wind and hot sun or by nature, looses its potency and is called dūṣīviṣa.

sanskrit_text: तनुत्वात्कफसंगाच्च न हन्ति । अजीर्यन् वर्षगणानुबन्धी भवति । तत्र भिन्नवर्चा विगन्धो वैरस्यतृष्णामूर्च्छाभ्रमप्रलापच्छर्दिविचेष्टितारतियुक्तः ॥ २६-२७ ॥
transliteration: Tanutvāt kaphasaṃgācca na hanti | Ajīryan varṣagaṇānubandhī bhavati | Tatra bhinnavarcā vigandho vairasyatṛṣṇāmūrcchā bhramapralāpacchardiviceṣṭitāratiyuktaḥ || 26-27 ||
commentary: Due to less potency and being associated with kapha, that does not kill the individual who takes it. As it does not get digested in the body and stays there for years. Affected by this, the individual has diarrhoea, discolouration, unnatural odour of the body, perception of different tastes, thirst, syncope, giddiness, blabbering, vomiting, typical physical activity and restlessness.

sanskrit_text: आमाशयगतं कफवातरोगं करोति । पक्वाशयगतं वातपित्तरोगं करोति । केशशातश्च भवति ॥ २८ ॥
transliteration: Āmāśayagataṃ kaphavātarogaṃ karoti | Pakvāśayagataṃ vātapittarogaṃ karoti | Keśaśātaśca bhavati || 28 ||
commentary: When dūṣīviṣa is seated in the āmāśaya (stomach), it makes the individual suffer from kapha-vāta disorders and when it takes shelter in the pakvāśaya (intestines) it causes vāta-pitta diseases and the hairs fall down from head and body due to which the individual looks like a bird that has withered wings.

sanskrit_text: धातुगतं रुच्यरुचिकरम् । शीतवातातपे चोपशायात् ॥ २९ ॥
transliteration: Dhātugataṃ rucyarucikaram | Śītavātātape copaśāyāt || 29 ||
commentary: When Dūṣīviṣa gets seated in dhātus (Rasa etc.), it causes symptoms - aversion to food, anorexia etc. There will be aggravation on exposure to cold winds and on a cloudy day.

sanskrit_text: अतिनिद्रा गौरवं जृम्भा विश्लेषः सर्वाङ्गहर्षः पूर्वरूपम् । प्रादुर्भावे त्वन्नमदोऽविपाकोऽरुचिः कोठो दद्रुः शोफः पादकरयोः शोफो मूर्च्छा छर्दिरतीसारः श्वासो ज्वर आनाहश्च ॥ ३०-३१ ॥
transliteration: Atinidrā gauravaṃ jṛmbhā viśleṣaḥ sarvāṅgaharṣaḥ pūrvarūpam | Prādurbhāve tva nnamado'vipāko'ruciḥ koṭho dadruḥ śophaḥ pādakarayoḥ śopho mūrcchā chardiratīsāraḥ śvāso jvara ānāhaśca || 30-31 ||
commentary: In the premonitary stage of Dūṣīviṣa affliction, there will be excessive sleep, heaviness of the body, over yawning, looseness in the body, skintillation or pain all over the body and when the manifestation takes place there will be intoxicated feeling after food, indigestion, anorexia, patches on the body and rashes, emaciation of muscle, over swelling in hands and legs, syncope, vomiting, diarrhoea, dyspnoea, fever and bloating of abdomen.

sanskrit_text: किञ्चिदुन्मादं करोति किञ्चिदानाहं किञ्चिच्छुक्रं क्षपयति । किञ्चिद्वाक्सङ्गं किञ्चित्कुष्ठं किञ्चिदन्यान् रोगान् ॥ ३२ ॥
transliteration: Kiñcidunmādaṃ karoti kiñcidānāhaṃ kiñcicchukraṃ kṣapayati | Kiñcidvāksaṅgaṃ kiñcitkuṣṭhaṃ kiñcidanyān rogān || 32 ||
commentary: Some kinds of dūṣīviṣa cause insanity, some anāha (distension of the abdomen), some deplete the semen, some - stammering, some-skin disorders and some, various other diseases.

sanskrit_text: देशकालान्नदिवास्वप्नैर्विषं दूषयति दूषीविषम् । तत् सद्यः साध्यं बलिनो निरुपद्रवस्य । दुर्बलस्य विरुद्धाहारिणश्चासाध्यम् ॥ ३३-३४ ॥
transliteration: Deśakālānnadivāsvapnairviṣaṃ dūṣayati dūṣīviṣam | Tat sadyaḥ sādhyaṃ balino nirupadravasya | Durbalasya viruddhāhāriṇaścāsādhyam || 33-34 ||
commentary: On getting vitiated by place of availability, time, foods and day sleep, this keeps vitiating the tissues repeatedly, hence the name dūṣīviṣa (Vitiating poison). It is curable for a strong person and immediately and it is incurable in a weak and the one who consumes foods and drinks which are not suitable.

sanskrit_text: काश्चित् स्वेदमार्तवं पुरीषं चान्ने प्रयच्छन्ति । तद्भुक्त्वा पाण्डुः कृशो मन्दाग्निर्भवति । गरस्तस्य मर्मप्रध्मानमानाहपाणिपादशोफलक्षणं जठरग्रहणीराजयक्ष्माध्मानशोषज्वरान् करोति ॥ ३५-३७ ॥
transliteration: Kāścit svedamārtavaṃ purīṣaṃ cānne prayacchanti | Tadbhuktvā pāṇḍuḥ kṛśo mandāgnirbhavati | Garastasya marmapradhmānamānāhapāṇipādaśophalakṣaṇaṃ jaṭharagrahaṇīrājayakṣmādhmānaśoṣajvarān karoti || 35-37 ||
commentary: Some women add - sweat, menstrual blood and excreta of various parts of the body of animals and the garaviṣa prepared by the enemies - in the food and give it to the men. By consuming such food, the individual becomes pale, emaciated and his digestive fire becomes weak. By the above substance, there originates garaviṣa in his body. Further he suffers from pain in the vital parts, abdominal distension, signs of oedema in the hands, abdominal diseases, sprue, pthisis, oppression of vāta in the abdomen, emaciation, fever and the symptoms of certain other diseases.

sanskrit_text: लूता षोडशविधा । तासां सामान्यलिङ्गं दंशे कोथः स्रावो ज्वरो दाहोऽतीसारः । कृष्णरक्ताः स्फोटाश्च ॥ ३८-४० ॥
transliteration: Lūtā ṣoḍaśavidhā | Tāsāṃ sāmānyaliṅgaṃ daṃśe kothaḥ srāvo jvaro dāho'tisāraḥ | Kṛṣṇaraktāḥ sphoṭāśca || 38-40 ||
commentary: Since the lūna grass had got contact with the sweat of the sage (Vasiṣṭha) and became spider (mythological reference), it is called lūtā which is of sixteen types. On being bitten by them (the lūtās), the place of bite/sting gets putrified with discharge of blood, fever, burning sensation, diarrhoea and other diseases of tridoṣa origin, vesicles of various sizes with mobile nature in black and red in colour. These are the common signs and symptoms of spider-sting.

sanskrit_text: ऊर्ध्वकृतिः सशोफः स्रावी क्षिप्रपाकी दूषीविषलूतादष्टलिङ्गम् ॥ ४१-४२ ॥
transliteration: Ūrdhvakṛtiḥ saśophaḥ srāvī kṣiprapākī dūṣīviṣalūtādaṣṭaliṅgam || 41-42 ||
commentary: There appears elevated sieve like structure in the centre of the bite-place that gets ulcerated quickly and associated with wetness, inflammation, and fever. Such a condition is known as the bite of Dūṣīviṣa type of lūtās.

sanskrit_text: शोफः स्फोटाः पीतरक्ता ज्वरः श्वासः शिरोग्रहश्च प्राणान्तिकानाम् ॥ ४३ ॥
transliteration: Śophaḥ sphoṭāḥ pītaraktā jvaraḥ śvāsaḥ śirograhaśca prāṇāntikānām || 43 ||
commentary: By the affliction of the poison of Sauvarṇikā etc., eight lūtās, there arise inflammation, vesicles of red or yellow colour, fever, dyspnoea and gripping sensation in the head. These lūtās are considered fatal.

sanskrit_text: आखुदष्टे गलति शोणितम् । पाण्डुमण्डलानि ज्वरोऽरुचिरोमहर्षदाहाः ॥ ४४ ॥
transliteration: Ākhudaṣṭe galati śoṇitam | Pāṇḍumaṇḍalāni jvaro'ruciromaharṣadāhāḥ || 44 ||
commentary: The bite area which is bitten by rat, keeps oozing of the blood. There will also be pale-coloured patches, fever, anorexia, horripillation and burning sensation in the individual.

sanskrit_text: आसाध्याखुदष्टे मूर्च्छा शोफो वैवर्ण्यं क्लेदो बाधिर्यं ज्वरः शिरोगुरुत्वं लालास्रावो रक्तच्छर्दिश्च ॥ ४५ ॥
transliteration: Āsādhyākhudaṣṭe mūrcchā śopho vaivarṇyaṃ kledo bādhiryaṃ jvaraḥ śirogurutvaṃ lālāsrāvo raktacchardica || 45 ||
commentary: When the rats of fatal poisonous nature bite, there will be syncope, oedema, discolouration, wetness, deafness, fever, heaviness in the head, salivation and vomiting of blood.

sanskrit_text: कृकलाददष्टे कृष्णं नीलं चित्रं वा भवति । भ्रमोऽतीसारश्च ॥ ४६ ॥
transliteration: Kṛkalādadaṣṭe kṛṣṇaṃ nīlaṃ citraṃ vā bhavati | Bhramo'tisāraśca || 46 ||
commentary: When the lizard bites, the bite area becomes black, bluish or multi-coloured. The individual suffers from delusion and diarrhoea.

sanskrit_text: वृश्चिकदष्टे प्रथमं दाहशूलम् । ततः क्षिप्रं विषमूर्ध्वं गत्वा पुनरुपसर्पति ॥ ४७ ॥
transliteration: Vṛścikadaṣṭe prathamaṃ dāhaśūlam | Tataḥ kṣipraṃ viṣamūrdhvaṃ gatvā punarupasarpati || 47 ||
commentary: Initially on scorpion sting, there will be pain that resembles the suffering of burning with fire and breaking pain. Later the poison ascends to the upper part of the body fast and comes back to the sting area and settles there.

sanskrit_text: हृन्नासिकाजिह्वातिवेदनासाध्यः । मांसावदारणे म्रियते ॥ ४८ ॥
transliteration: Hṛnnāsikājihvātivedanāsādhyaḥ | Māṃsāvadāraṇe mriyate || 48 ||
commentary: The effect of scorpion sting becomes incurable if the patient has severe suffering in the heart, nose and tongue. He dies if there is withering of muscles from the bite-area.

sanskrit_text: कणभदष्टे विसर्पः शोफो रुग्ज्वरच्छर्दयः ॥ ४९ ॥
transliteration: Kaṇabhadaṣṭe visarpaḥ śopho rugjvaracchardayaḥ || 49 ||
commentary: Erysipelas, inflammation, pain, fever and vomiting are the features when a creature called kaṇabha stings.

sanskrit_text: उच्चिटिङ्गदष्टे रोमहर्षः शिश्नोद्गमः सतीव्ररुक् शीताम्बुसिक्त इव च मन्यते ॥ ५० ॥
transliteration: Ucciṭiṅgadaṣṭe romaharṣaḥ śiśnodgamaḥ satīvr aruk śītāmbusikta iva ca manyate || 50 ||
commentary: There will be horripilation by the stings of ucciṭiṅga (a variety of scorpion), the penis gets erect and severe pain is associated (in the sting-area). The patient feels as if his body is drenched with cold water.

sanskrit_text: मण्डूकदष्टे शोफः पीतो रुजावान् तृष्णा छर्दिर्निद्रा च । मत्स्यदष्टे दाहशोफरुक् । जलौकादष्टे कण्डूशोफज्वरमूर्च्छाः ॥ ५१-५२ ॥
transliteration: Maṇḍūkadaṣṭe śophaḥ pīto rujāvān tṛṣṇā chardirnidrā ca | Matsyadaṣṭe dāhaśopharuk | Jalaukādaṣṭe kaṇḍūśophajvaramūrcchāḥ || 51-52 ||
commentary: When a poisonous frog bites, with one fang there will be inflammation (of the bite area) yellow in colour and painful. The patient suffers from thirst, vomiting and excessive sleep. By the bite of poisonous fish, there will be burning sensation inflammation and pain. When a leech of poisonous nature takes on the human being, there will be itching sensation, inflammation fever and syncope.

sanskrit_text: गृहगोधिकादष्टे शोफस्तोदः स्वेदश्च । शतपद्यां स्वेदरुग्दाहाः ॥ ५३ ॥
transliteration: Gṛhagodhikādaṣṭe śophastodaḥ svedaśca | Śatapadyāṃ svedarugdāhāḥ || 53 ||
commentary: When a house-lizard bites, there will be inflammation, pinning sensation and sweating. By the bite of śatapadī (centipede) there will be sweating pain and burning sensation.

sanskrit_text: मशकदष्टे कण्डूरल्पशोफोऽल्परुक् । आसाध्यमशकदष्टे स्यादासाध्यकीटवत् ॥ ५४ ॥
transliteration: Maśakadaṣṭe kaṇḍūralpaśopho'lparuk | Āsādhyamaśakadaṣṭe syādāsādhyakīṭavat || 54 ||
commentary: On being bitten by the mosquito, there will be itching sensation, slight inflammation and mild pain, when a fatal mosquito bites the features will be like those of a fatal insect-bite.

sanskrit_text: मक्षिकादष्टे स्फोटाः सस्रावाः कृष्णा दाहमूर्च्छाज्वरकराः । तासां स्थगिका प्राणहरा ॥ ५५ ॥
transliteration: Makṣikādaṣṭe sphoṭāḥ sasrāvāḥ kṛṣṇā dāhamūrcchājvarakarāḥ | Tāsāṃ sthagikā prāṇaharā || 55 ||
commentary: On getting stung by the makṣikā (Honey-bee), there arise vesicles that start oozing immediately, black in colour and associated with burning sensation, syncope and fever. Among these bees the Sthagikā variety are fatal ones.

sanskrit_text: द्विपदां चतुष्पदां च दंष्ट्रानखाभिघाते शोफः पाकश्च स्रावो ज्वरश्च ॥ ५६ ॥
transliteration: Dvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ ca daṃṣṭrānakhābhighāte śophaḥ pākaśca srāvo jvaraśca || 56 ||
commentary: When there occurs an injury due to the hit by the fang or claw of the two legged or four legged animals the hit area will get swollen and ulcerated. There will be discharge from the ulcer and the patient suffers from fever.

sanskrit_text: श्वानवराहगोमायुतरक्षुरिक्षुसिंहादीनां क्षते । विषण्णगात्राणि जायन्ते । आलस्यं मूर्च्छा ज्वरः । तानि दष्ट्वा सजलादर्शने भयं मरणम् ॥ ५७-६४ ॥
transliteration: Śvānavarāhagomāyutarakṣurikṣusiṃhādīnāṃ kṣate | Viṣaṇṇagātrāṇi jāyante | Ālasyaṃ mūrcchā jvaraḥ | Tāni daṣṭvā sajalādarśane bhayaṃ maraṇam || 57-64 ||
commentary: When vāta gets aggravated by kapha and takes shelter in the sensory nerves of the dog, fox, Tarakṣu, Ṛkṣa, tiger etc.; wild animals, they lose their senses when their tail, lower jaw and shoulders droop down and there will be excessive salivation. They become partly blind and deaf and run after each other. When such animals bite any person, the bite area becomes sense-less, black and with excessive discharge of blood along with the symptoms that are caused by the hit with a poison smeared weapon. When a man is bitten by a mad-dog etc., animals he repeatedly behaves like that animal and can not perform his own routine and finally attains death. If he sees the image of the bitten animal when he looks into the mirror or water, it is considered as a bad omen. When he touches or looks at water he gets frightened which is also a bad omen and this symptom is called jalatṛṣṇā.

sanskrit_text: अन्नाभिकामो मूत्रपुरीषसमं समजिह्वतालुश्च विषमुक्तो भवति । इति श्रीमाधवकरविरचिते माधवनिदाने विसरोगनिदानं समाप्तम् ॥ ६९ ॥
transliteration: Annābhikāmo mūtrapurīṣasamaṃ samajihvatāluśca viṣamukto bhavati | Iti śrīmādhavakaraviracite mādhavanidāne visaroganidānaṃ samāptam || 69 ||
commentary: When an individual has the doṣas in an equilibrium state and the dhātus in natural status, he has longing for eating, passing the urine and faeces normally, and has pleasant colour of the body, sense organs, mind and bodily activity, he should be considered by the physician, as free from poison. Thus ends the diagnosis of diseases caused by poison in Madhava's book on diagnosis written by Śrīmādhavakara.
